Feature Use --- --- Breakpoint Pause at a line Conditional breakpoint Pause only when a condition holds, such as i == 9999 Data breakpoint (watchpoint) Pause when a variable's value changes : the fastest way to find who corrupted it Call stack See the chain of calls that led here Crash dump Examine a program's state after it has crashed, on another machine Continuous integration Continuous integration (CI) builds the project and runs every check automatically for each change pushed to the repository, on every platform you support. yaml jobs: build: strategy: { matrix: { os: ubuntu-latest, windows-latest } } runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }} steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - run: cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug - run: cmake --build build - run: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure The value is that the checks cannot be forgotten. A change that breaks a test, or the build on another platform, is caught within minutes and before it is merged. Check yourself quiz ? Which sanitizer finds data races? - AddressSanitizer + ThreadSanitizer - UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer - MemorySanitizer ThreadSanitizer ( -fsanitize=thread ) tracks accesses from different threads. AddressSanitizer finds memory errors such as use-after-free. ? What is the difference between static analysis and a sanitizer? - There is none - Static analysis runs the program; a sanitizer reads the code + Static analysis needs no run; a sanitizer checks while running - Sanitizers only work on Windows They complement each other: analysers find problems in code that never runs in tests; sanitizers catch real failures in code that does. ? Why does high coverage not prove the tests are good? - Because coverage tools are often wrong - Because coverage counts comments too + It shows code ran, not that a bug there would be caught - Because 100% coverage is impossible A test with no checks can still run every line. Coverage finds untested code; it does not measure the checks. ? What does a data breakpoint do? - It pauses at a chosen line of code - It logs every variable to a file - It stops the program when it allocates memory + It pauses the program when a particular variable's value changes Data breakpoints (watchpoints) find the code that modifies a variable unexpectedly.

title: Tests that catch bugs
where: 13.09 Testing, Sanitizers, Static Analysis and Tooling
body: This time you write the tests , and the checker judges how good they are. Somebody has written a function that should behave like this: clampTo(value, low, high) returns value if it lies between low and high inclusive, low if it is smaller, and high if it is larger. Write bool passesMyTests(ClampFn clampTo) . It receives an implementation, tries it on inputs of your choosing, and returns true only if every answer is right. The checker hands your function one correct implementation, which must pass, and several subtly broken ones, each of which must fail . This is called mutation testing : tests are only worth something if they notice when the code is wrong. Think about where implementations go wrong: at the edges, exactly on a boundary, with negative numbers, and when low equals high .

title: Test by property
where: 13.09 Testing, Sanitizers, Static Analysis and Tooling
body: Checking a sort against hand-written expected answers only goes so far. A stronger approach is to state what must be true of every correct answer and check that: 1. The output is in non-decreasing order. 2. The output is a rearrangement of the input: the same values, each the same number of times. Nothing lost, nothing invented, no duplicates dropped. With those two properties you can throw any input at a sort, including inputs you generate in a loop, without working out the expected output yourself. Write bool passesMyTests(SortFn sortIt) . sortIt takes a std::vector<int and returns the sorted version. Return true only if the implementation holds both properties on all your inputs. As before, the checker feeds you one correct sort and a row of broken ones. Inputs worth including: empty, one element, already sorted, reversed, all equal, duplicates, negative numbers, and something long. std::is_sorted and std::is_permutation in <algorithm do most of the work.

title: 13.10  C++ Standards Timeline and Where to Go Next
match: 13.10 C++ Standards Timeline and Where to Go Next
body: C++ gets a new standard every three years. Knowing what arrived when helps you read older code, choose compiler settings and know what you can rely on. After that: pick a field and go deep. What each standard added Standard Principal additions In this course --- --- --- C++98 / 03 Classes, templates, exceptions, the containers and algorithms The foundation of everything C++11 auto , lambdas, rvalue references and move semantics, unique_ptr and shared_ptr , threads and atomics, constexpr , range-based for , nullptr , enum class , variadic templates, override Milestones 4 to 12 C++14 Generic lambdas, std::make_unique , decltype(auto) , binary literals, digit separators Milestones 2 and 5 C++17 optional , variant , any , string_view , filesystem , structured bindings, if constexpr , fold expressions, CTAD, inline variables, parallel algorithms, guaranteed copy elision Milestones 9 to 12 C++20 Concepts, ranges, coroutines, modules, <= , std::format , span , jthread , semaphores and latches, consteval and constinit , designated initializers, calendars and time zones Milestones 9 to 13 C++23 std::print , std::expected , std::generator , mdspan , flat_map , import std , deducing this , ranges::to , views::zip and enumerate Milestones 10 to 13 C++26 Static reflection, contracts, std::execution , embed , linear algebra, defined behaviour for uninitialized reads Mentioned in Milestones 11 to 13 C++11 was the turning point. Code written before it looks like a different language, with raw new and delete , hand-written iterator loops and no auto . "Modern C++" means C++11 and later. !note A standard and its implementation are different things A feature is usable only once your compiler and its standard library implement it, which can lag the standard by years. cppreference.com keeps a compiler-support table for each feature. Reading older code You will spend more time reading existing code than writing new code. A translation table: In older code Today --- --- new and delete std::make_unique , containers NULL or 0 for a pointer nullptr typedef using for (iterator it = v.begin(); it != v.end(); ++it) A range-based for A hand-written function object class A lambda std::enable_if A concept Output parameters for several results Return a struct, or structured bindings printf , or chains of << with manipulators std::format , std::print A char and a length std::string_view , std::span Where to go next You have covered the language. Depth now comes from a field. Since your aim is computer science, three subjects build directly on this course and are worth taking next: data structures and algorithms (trees, graphs, hashing, dynamic programming), computer architecture (what 13.04 Performance, Caches and Data-Oriented Design only sketched), and operating systems (what threads, memory and files really are). C++ is the language most of that material is taught and implemented in. Resources Kind Recommendation --- --- Reference cppreference.com . Keep it open. Guidelines The C++ Core Guidelines Books: foundations A Tour of C++ and Programming: Principles and Practice Using C++ , both by Stroustrup Books: using it well Effective Modern C++ (Meyers); C++ Concurrency in Action (Williams); C++ Templates: The Complete Guide (Vandevoorde, Josuttis, Gregor) Books: performance Optimized C++ (Guntheroth); Data-Oriented Design (Fabian) Talks CppCon, C++Now and Meeting C++, all online. Start with the "Back to Basics" series. Experiment Compiler Explorer (godbolt.org) shows the machine code. C++ Insights shows what the compiler makes of your source. Practice Advent of Code, Exercism's C++ track, contributing to open source Four pieces of advice --- --- Build things Every project you finish teaches more than any lesson. The projects in this course are a start; the ones you invent yourself teach the most. Read other people's code Good libraries, and the standard library's own implementation, show how experienced programmers solve problems. Keep the safety net on Warnings, sanitizers and tests, always: 13.09 Testing, Sanitizers, Static Analysis and Tooling Simple first, clever later The best C++ is unremarkable to read. Reach for the advanced techniques of the last three milestones when a problem needs them, and not before. Check yourself quiz ? Which standard is the start of "modern C++"? - C++98 - C++03 + C++11 - C++20 C++11 added auto , lambdas, move semantics, smart pointers and much else, changing how C++ is written. ? Why might a feature in the current standard be unavailable to you? + A feature can be used only when both your compiler and its standard library have implemented it - Because new features need a licence - Because each feature must be enabled one at a time in the code - Because the standard is only a draft for its first three years Implementations catch up over time. Check your compiler's support tables before relying on a new feature. ? What is the modern replacement for new and delete in ordinary code? - malloc and free - std::shared_ptr for every object + std::make_unique and the standard containers - Placement new Owning objects through std::unique_ptr and containers removes manual delete , and with it leaks and double frees. ? How often is a new C++ standard published? - Every year - Every five years + Every three years - Whenever a compiler adds features C++11, 14, 17, 20 and 23 followed a three-year cycle, with C++26 next.

title: 1.01  C# and .NET: Your First Program
body: What C and .NET are, how a program is compiled and run, the dotnet command-line tool, top-level statements, Console.WriteLine and ReadLine, comments, and reading compiler errors. C and .NET C is a statically typed language from Microsoft, used for desktop and web applications, cloud services, tools and games (Unity and Godot use it). .NET is the platform it runs on: a runtime that executes the program, manages memory with a garbage collector, and a large standard library for text, collections, files, networking and much more. .NET is free, open source and runs on Windows, macOS and Linux. Compiling turns C into IL (intermediate language) stored in a .dll . When the program starts, the runtime compiles the IL to machine code for the processor it runs on (just-in-time compilation). You get the safety of a managed language with speed close to C++. Your first program csharp // Program.cs Console.WriteLine("Hello, Xenon!"); Console.WriteLine(2 + 3); This is a complete program. Code written at the top of Program.cs , outside any class, is made of top-level statements : the compiler wraps it in a Main method for you. Each statement ends with a semicolon. Console.WriteLine prints a line; Console.Write prints without moving to a new line. Reading input csharp Console.Write("What is your name? "); string? name = Console.ReadLine(); Console.WriteLine($"Hello, {name}!"); Console.Write("Your age? "); int age = int.Parse(Console.ReadLine()!); Console.WriteLine($"Next year you will be {age + 1}."); Console.ReadLine() returns the line typed, or null when the input has ended, so its type is string? (a string that may be null; lesson 2.05). int.Parse turns text into a whole number. The $"..." string can include values in braces: an interpolated string (lesson 1.04). The Run button on examples like this one asks for input below the output. Comments csharp // A comment to the end of the line. / A comment that can span lines. / /// <summary An XML documentation comment, shown by editors when you hover.</summary Console.WriteLine("Comments are ignored by the compiler."); The dotnet tool On your own computer, install the .NET SDK from dot.net. The dotnet command creates, builds and runs projects: bash dotnet new console -o Hello a new console project in the folder Hello cd Hello dotnet run compile and run dotnet build compile only A project is a folder with a .csproj file (the project's settings) and .cs source files. Visual Studio, VS Code with the C Dev Kit, and JetBrains Rider all work with these projects. In this course, the practice editor compiles and runs your code on .NET 9 for you. Compiler errors C checks your program before it runs. An error names the file, line and column, a code, and what is wrong: text Program.cs(3,9): error CS0029: Cannot implicitly convert type 'string' to 'int' Program.cs(5,1): error CS1002: ; expected Read the first error first: later ones are often caused by it. The CS number can be searched for in Microsoft's documentation. Warnings (such as an unused variable) do not stop the build, but they usually point at real problems. Check yourself quiz ? What are top-level statements? - Statements at the top of a class, before its methods + Code written directly in Program.cs outside any class, wrapped in Main for you - The using lines at the start of a file that import namespaces - Setup code the runtime runs before it calls Main The compiler wraps code written outside any class in a generated Main method. They are not a separate step before Main : they are its body. ? Why is the type of Console.ReadLine() string? and not plain string? - The ? means the line may be empty, so it can be "" - The ? means the value may be text or a number + It returns null when the input has ended, and ? says the string may be null string? is a string that may be null, and ReadLine gives null when there is no more input. An empty line is still a real string, "", not null. ? What does Console.Write("a"); Console.WriteLine("b"); Console.Write("c"); print? - a, b and c on three lines + ab on one line, then c on the next - abc on one line - a on one line, then bc Write does not end the line; WriteLine does, after printing its text.

title: Input and output
body: Write a program that asks for a name and a birth year, then greets the person and says how old they turn in 2026: Name? Ada Birth year? 1990 Hello, Ada! In 2026 you turn 36. The prompts are written with Console.Write (no new line); the input after them comes from the person typing. Use int.Parse for the year.

title: 1.02  Variables and Types
body: Declaring variables with explicit types and var, the built-in value types - int, long, double, decimal, bool, char - and string, constants, default values, value versus reference types, and converting between types with casts, Parse, TryParse and Convert. Declaring variables Every variable in C has a type that never changes: csharp int count = 3; double price = 2.50; string name = "Ada"; bool done = false; char grade = 'A'; // a single character, in single quotes var total = count price; // var: the compiler infers the type (double here) const int MaxPlayers = 4; // a constant: fixed at compile time count = count + 1; // fine // count = "four"; // error CS0029: cannot convert string to int Console.WriteLine($"{name}: {count} x {price} = {total}, max {MaxPlayers}, grade {grade}, done {done}"); var is still statically typed: var total is a double , decided once. Use var when the type is obvious from the right-hand side ( var list = new List<int () ), and the explicit type when it helps the reader. Names use camelCase for local variables and PascalCase for constants, methods, classes and properties. Number types Type Holds Example --- --- --- int Whole numbers, about ±2.1 billion 42 long Whole numbers, about ±9.2 × 10¹⁸ 42L double Floating point, about 15 digits 3.14 float Floating point, about 7 digits 3.14f decimal Exact decimal, 28 digits: money 19.99m byte 0 to 255 (byte)200 csharp Console.WriteLine(0.1 + 0.2); // 0.30000000000000004: binary floating point Console.WriteLine(0.1m + 0.2m); // 0.3: decimal is exact for decimal fractions Console.WriteLine(int.MaxValue); int big = int.MaxValue; big = big + 1; // wraps around silently Console.WriteLine(big); Console.WriteLine(1_000_000); // underscores make long numbers readable Use int for counts, double for measurements and science, and decimal for money. checked { ... } turns silent overflow into an OverflowException . Value types and reference types Numbers, bool , char and structs (lesson 3.02) are value types : the variable holds the value itself, and assigning copies it. Strings, arrays, lists and classes are reference types : the variable holds a reference to an object, and assigning copies the reference, so both variables see the same object. csharp int a = 1; int b = a; // a copy b = 2; Console.WriteLine(a); // 1 int x = { 1, 2, 3 }; int y = x; // the same array y 0 = 99; Console.WriteLine(x 0 ); // 99 string is a reference type that behaves like a value: strings can never be changed (they are immutable ), so sharing them is safe. Converting csharp int whole = (int)3.99; // explicit cast: cuts off to 3 double d = 7; // int to double is automatic (no information lost) long l = 5; // int to long too int parsed = int.Parse("123"); // text to number; throws FormatException for "12x" bool ok = int.TryParse("12x", out int value); // false, value is 0: no exception double rate = double.Parse("2.5", System.Globalization.CultureInfo.InvariantCulture); string text = 42.ToString(); Console.WriteLine($"{whole} {d} {l} {parsed} {ok} {value} {rate} {text}"); Conversions that may lose information need a cast (type) . For user input, prefer TryParse : it returns false instead of throwing. Parsing decimals depends on the computer's culture ( 2.5 or 2,5 ), so pass CultureInfo.InvariantCulture when reading data files. Default values Fields and array elements start with default values : 0 for numbers, false , '\0' , and null for reference types. Local variables have no default: using one before assigning it is error CS0165. Check yourself quiz ? Which type should hold an amount of money, and why? - double, because it has the most precision of the number types - float, because it uses less memory for long lists of prices + decimal, because it stores decimal fractions like 0.10 exactly decimal stores base-10 fractions exactly. double is binary, so amounts like 0.1 + 0.2 come out with rounding errors, however many digits it has. ? After int y = x; y 0 = 5; what is x 0 ? + 5 - Whatever x 0 was before, because y is a copy - 0, because y = x makes a new empty array - It does not compile: y must be created with new Arrays are reference types: y = x copies the reference, so x and y are the same array. ? What does var n = 10 / 4; give? - 2.5, a double + 2, an int - 2.5, a decimal - an error Both operands are int, so the division is whole-number division and var infers int.

title: Types and conversions
body: Complete the static methods in Solution : csharp public static double ToCelsius(double fahrenheit) // (F - 32) 5 / 9 public static double Average(int a, int b, int c) // the exact average: Average(1, 2, 2) is 1.666... public static int ParseOrDefault(string text, int fallback) // the number in text, or fallback if it is not a whole number public static decimal TotalPrice(decimal unitPrice, int quantity, decimal taxRate) TotalPrice is unitPrice quantity , plus tax at taxRate (0.2 means 20 %), rounded to 2 decimals with halves rounded away from zero .

title: 1.03  Operators and Math
body: Arithmetic and integer division, remainder, compound assignment and increment, comparison and logical operators with short-circuiting, the conditional operator, operator precedence, and the Math class for rounding, powers and roots. Arithmetic csharp int a = 17, b = 5; Console.WriteLine(a + b); // 22 Console.WriteLine(a - b); // 12 Console.WriteLine(a b); // 85 Console.WriteLine(a / b); // 3: int / int cuts off the fraction Console.WriteLine(a % b); // 2: the remainder Console.WriteLine(a / 5.0); // 3.4: one double operand makes it a double division Console.WriteLine((double)a / b); Console.WriteLine(-17 / 5); // -3: rounds toward zero Console.WriteLine(-17 % 5); // -2: the remainder has the sign of the left side Integer division and % are useful together: minutes / 60 hours and minutes % 60 left over. Dividing an int by zero throws DivideByZeroException ; dividing a double by zero gives Infinity or NaN . Assignment shortcuts csharp int score = 10; score += 5; // score = score + 5 score = 2; // 30 score -= 1; // 29 score++; // 30 score--; // 29 Console.WriteLine(score); int i = 5; Console.WriteLine(i++); // prints 5, then i becomes 6 Console.WriteLine(++i); // i becomes 7, then prints 7 Use ++ and -- as statements on their own line; inside larger expressions they are easy to misread. Comparison and logic Operator Meaning --- --- == , != Equal, not equal < , <= , , = Ordering && And: true when both are true \ \ Or: true when either is true ! Not csharp int age = 20; bool hasTicket = true; bool canEnter = age = 18 && hasTicket; bool discount = age < 12 age = 65; Console.WriteLine($"{canEnter} {discount} {!canEnter}"); string? name = null; if (name != null && name.Length 3) Console.WriteLine("long name"); // safe: && stops early && and short-circuit : if the left side already decides the result, the right side is not evaluated. That is what makes the name != null && name.Length 3 check safe. Conditions must be bool : if (count) is an error in C , unlike C or JavaScript. Write if (count != 0) . The conditional operator csharp int n = 7; string parity = n % 2 == 0 ? "even" : "odd"; Console.WriteLine($"{n} is {parity}"); Precedence , / and % bind tighter than + and - ; comparisons come next; then && , then , then ?: , then assignment. When in doubt, add parentheses: (a + b) c . Math csharp Console.WriteLine(Math.Sqrt(16)); // 4 Console.WriteLine(Math.Pow(2, 10)); // 1024 Console.WriteLine(Math.Abs(-3.5)); // 3.5 Console.WriteLine(Math.Max(3, 9)); // 9 Console.WriteLine(Math.Round(2.5)); // 2: rounds halves to even by default Console.WriteLine(Math.Round(2.5, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero)); // 3 Console.WriteLine(Math.Round(3.14159, 2)); // 3.14 Console.WriteLine(Math.Floor(-2.5) + " " + Math.Ceiling(2.1)); // -3 3 Console.WriteLine(Math.Clamp(15, 0, 10)); // 10 Console.WriteLine(Math.PI); Math.Round uses banker's rounding (halves go to the even neighbour) unless you ask for MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero , which is the rounding taught in school and usually wanted for money. Check yourself quiz ? What are 23 / 4 and 23 % 4 with ints? - 5.75 and 3 - 6 and 1 + 5 and 3 - 5 and 0.75 Integer division drops the fraction, giving 5, and % is the remainder: 23 = 4 × 5 + 3. You only get 5.75 when one side is a double. ? Why is if (name != null && name.Length 0) safe when name is null? - The compiler removes name.Length when it sees a null check - name.Length counts as 0 when name is null, so the test is false - Exceptions thrown inside an if condition are ignored + && stops when the left side is false, so name.Length is never evaluated && short-circuits: if the left side is false, the right side never runs. Reading name.Length on null would throw a NullReferenceException. ? What does Math.Round(3.5) + Math.Round(4.5) give? - 9 + 8 - 7 - 8.0 and a warning Banker's rounding takes 3.5 to 4 and 4.5 to 4, the even neighbours.

title: 1.04  Strings and Formatting
body:
Working with text - string literals, escapes, verbatim and raw strings, interpolation with format specifiers and alignment, the common string methods, comparing strings, characters, and building text efficiently with StringBuilder. String literals csharp string plain = "Tab:	Quote:" Backslash:\ Newline:
next line"; string path = @"C:\Users\Ada
otes.txt"; // verbatim: backslashes are literal string json = """ { "name": "Ada", "tags": "math" } """; // raw string: no escaping at all Console.WriteLine(plain); Console.WriteLine(path); Console.WriteLine(json); Raw strings (three or more quotes) keep everything exactly, which suits JSON, SQL and regular expressions. The indentation of the closing quotes is removed from every line. Interpolation and formatting csharp string name = "Ada"; decimal price = 1234.5m; double ratio = 0.4567; int n = 42; Console.WriteLine($"{name} paid {price:C2}"); // currency, depends on the machine's culture Console.WriteLine($"{price:N2}"); // 1,234.50 Console.WriteLine($"{price:F1}"); // 1234.5 Console.WriteLine($"{ratio:P1}"); // 45.7 % Console.WriteLine($"{n:D5} {n:X}"); // 00042 2A Console.WriteLine($" {name,8} {name,-8} "); // right- and left-aligned in 8 characters Console.WriteLine($" {price,10:F2} "); // alignment and format together Console.WriteLine($"{(n 40 ? "big" : "small")}"); // expressions in parentheses After the value, ,width aligns (negative means left) and :format formats. Common formats: F2 fixed decimals, N2 with thousands separators, P percent, D5 zero-padded integer, X hexadecimal, C currency. For dates: {DateTime.Now:yyyy-MM-dd} . N , C and dates follow the computer's culture . Output meant for files or other programs should use CultureInfo.InvariantCulture : price.ToString("F2", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture) . String methods Strings never change: each method returns a new string. Code Gives --- --- s.Length , s 0 , s ^1 Length, first character, last character s.Substring(start, length) , s 2..5 Part of the string s.ToUpper() , s.ToLower() , s.Trim() Case, without surrounding spaces s.Contains(x) , s.StartsWith(x) , s.EndsWith(x) Tests s.IndexOf(x) , s.LastIndexOf(x) Position, or -1 s.Replace(a, b) , s.Insert(i, x) , s.Remove(i, n) New strings with changes s.Split(',') , string.Join(", ", parts) Split into an array, join back s.PadLeft(5, '0') , s.PadRight(10) Padded string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(s) Null, empty or only spaces csharp string line = " Ada Lovelace, 1815 , mathematician "; string parts = line.Split(',', StringSplitOptions.TrimEntries); Console.WriteLine(parts 0 .ToUpper()); Console.WriteLine(int.Parse(parts 1 ) + 200); Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", parts)); Console.WriteLine("banana".Replace("an", "AN") + " " + "banana".IndexOf('n') + " " + "banana" 1..4 ); 1..4 is a range : from index 1 up to, not including, 4. ^1 counts from the end. Comparing == compares string contents. For case-insensitive comparison, use string.Equals(a, b, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) ; for sorting, string.Compare(a, b, StringComparison.Ordinal) . Characters csharp char c = 'b'; Console.WriteLine(char.IsLetter(c) + " " + char.IsDigit('7') + " " + char.ToUpper(c)); Console.WriteLine((int)c); // 98: its character code Console.WriteLine((char)(c + 1)); // 'c' foreach (char ch in "hi!") Console.Write($" {ch} "); Console.WriteLine(); Building strings Because strings are immutable, += in a loop copies the whole string each time. For many pieces, use a StringBuilder : csharp using System.Text; var sb = new StringBuilder(); for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) sb.Append(i).Append(i < 5 ? ", " : "
"); sb.AppendLine("done"); Console.Write(sb.ToString()); Check yourself quiz ? What does $" {x,-6} " do? + Writes x left-aligned in 6 characters, padded with spaces on the right - Writes x right-aligned in 6 characters, padded with spaces on the left - Writes only the first 6 characters of x and cuts the rest - Writes the value of x minus 6 In {value,width} a negative width left-aligns and a positive one right-aligns. The width is a minimum, so a longer value is not cut. ? Why use a StringBuilder in a loop instead of +=? - += changes the string in place, so other variables holding it change too + Strings are immutable, so each += copies the whole string; StringBuilder appends in place - += cannot join a string and a number, but StringBuilder can A string never changes: += builds a new string and copies everything so far, which gets slow in a loop. StringBuilder grows one buffer instead. ? What is "hello" 1..^1 ? - "hell" + "ell" - "ello" - "el" From index 1 up to, not including, the last character.

C 13 " gives "hello-world-c-13" public static string PriceLine(string item, decimal price) // item left in 12 characters, price right in 8 with 2 decimals public static int CountVowels(string text) // a, e, i, o, u in either case - Initials ignores extra spaces between and around the names. - Slug keeps letters and digits in lower case, turns every run of other characters into one - , and has no - at either end. - PriceLine("Tea", 2.5m) is "Tea 2.50" : 12 characters for the item, then 8 for the price. title: 1.05  Control Flow
body: Making decisions with if, else if and else, the switch statement and switch expressions, loops with while, do-while, for and foreach, break and continue, nested loops, and input loops that keep asking until the input is valid. if and else csharp int temperature = 23; if (temperature = 30) { Console.WriteLine("Hot"); } else if (temperature = 18) { Console.WriteLine("Pleasant"); } else { Console.WriteLine("Cold"); } Braces can be left out around a single statement, but always writing them avoids the classic bug where a second indented line is not actually part of the if . switch A switch statement compares one value against cases: csharp string command = "stop"; switch (command) { case "go": case "start": Console.WriteLine("Starting"); break; case "stop": Console.WriteLine("Stopping"); break; default: Console.WriteLine("Unknown command"); break; } Each case ends with break (or return ); C does not let one case fall through into the next by accident. A switch expression produces a value, which is usually neater: csharp int day = 6; string kind = day switch { 6 or 7 = "weekend", = 1 and <= 5 = "weekday", _ = "not a day", }; Console.WriteLine(kind); _ matches anything. Patterns like or , and and = 1 are covered fully in lesson 2.05. while and do-while csharp int n = 27, steps = 0; while (n != 1) { n = n % 2 == 0 ? n / 2 : 3 n + 1; steps++; } Console.WriteLine($"{steps} steps"); do { ... } while (condition); runs the body at least once, which suits "ask, then check": csharp int guess; do { Console.Write("Pick 1 to 3: "); string? line = Console.ReadLine(); if (line == null) break; // the input has ended if (!int.TryParse(line, out guess)) guess = 0; } while (guess < 1 guess 3); for and foreach csharp for (int i = 1; i <= 3; i++) { Console.Write($"{i} "); } Console.WriteLine(); for (int i = 10; i 0; i -= 3) Console.Write($"{i} "); Console.WriteLine(); string names = { "Ada", "Grace", "Linus" }; foreach (string name in names) { Console.WriteLine(name.ToUpper()); } Use for when you need the index or a count, and foreach to visit every item of an array, list, string or any other collection. break and continue csharp int numbers = { 4, 7, -1, 12, 0, 9 }; int sum = 0; foreach (int x in numbers) { if (x < 0) continue; // skip this one if (x == 0) break; // stop the loop sum += x; } Console.WriteLine(sum); // 4 + 7 + 12 = 23 Nested loops csharp for (int row = 1; row <= 3; row++) { for (int col = 1; col <= 4; col++) { Console.Write($"{row col,4}"); } Console.WriteLine(); } break leaves only the innermost loop. To leave several, move the loops into a method and return (lesson 2.01). Check yourself quiz ? When does a do-while loop differ from a while loop? - A do-while checks its condition before each round, a while after it + A do-while always runs its body at least once, since it checks the condition after it - A do-while cannot use break or continue - They differ only in style; both can run zero times The condition of a do-while is tested after the body, so the body runs once even when the condition is false from the start. ? What does continue do inside a for loop? - Leaves the loop completely, like break - Starts the loop again from the beginning, with i reset - Skips the rest of the body and also skips the i++ step + Skips the rest of this round's body, runs i++, then goes on with the next round continue ends only the current round. In a for loop the update part ( i++ ) still runs before the condition is checked again. ? How many times does for (int i = 0; i < 10; i += 3) run its body? - 3 + 4 - 10 - 9 i takes the values 0, 3, 6 and 9.

title: A bank account at the console
match: A bank account at the console
body: Write a program that keeps one bank account and follows commands typed one per line: deposit 100 Deposited 100.00. Balance: 100.00 withdraw 30.5 Withdrew 30.50. Balance: 69.50 withdraw 500 Not enough money. Balance: 69.50 interest 2 Added interest 1.39. Balance: 70.89 history 1. deposit 100.00 2. withdraw 30.50 3. interest 1.39 quit Goodbye. Final balance: 70.89 Rules: - Write the prompt before reading each line. Commands are not case-sensitive, and extra spaces are ignored. - Amounts are decimal numbers read with CultureInfo.InvariantCulture (so 30.5 works everywhere), rounded to cents as they are read (halves away from zero), and printed with 2 decimals ( F2 , invariant). - deposit <amount and withdraw <amount : the amount must be a number above 0, else print Amount must be a positive number. A withdrawal larger than the balance prints Not enough money. Balance: <balance and changes nothing. - interest <percent : adds balance × percent / 100, rounded to cents with halves away from zero. The percent must be 0 or more (else Amount must be a positive number. ); an interest of 0.00 is still recorded. - balance prints Balance: <balance . - history prints the successful transactions numbered from 1, as in the example, or No transactions. - quit , or the end of the input, prints Goodbye. Final balance: <balance and stops. - Anything else prints Unknown command: <first word , and a command with a missing or extra argument prints Usage: <command <amount (for balance , history and quit , extra words are ignored).

title: 2.01  Methods and Parameters
body: Writing methods with parameters and return values, expression-bodied methods, overloading, optional and named arguments, params arrays, ref, out and in parameters, local functions, recursion, and static methods in classes. Methods A method is a named block of code that takes parameters and may return a value. Methods live in classes; in a top-level program you can also write them directly as local functions : csharp Console.WriteLine(Area(3, 4)); Console.WriteLine(Describe("Ada", 36)); Greet("Grace"); static double Area(double width, double height) { return width height; } static string Describe(string name, int age) = $"{name} ({age})"; // expression-bodied static void Greet(string name) // void: returns nothing { Console.WriteLine($"Hello, {name}!"); } Each parameter has a type, and so does the result: the compiler checks every call. = expression is shorthand for a body that returns one expression. In a class, the same methods look like this; static means they belong to the class itself rather than to an object (lesson 3.05): csharp-norun public static class Geometry { public static double Area(double width, double height) = width height; } // called as Geometry.Area(3, 4) Overloading Several methods in a class may share a name if their parameter lists differ. The compiler picks the best match: csharp Console.WriteLine(MathX.Max(3, 9)); Console.WriteLine(MathX.Max(2.5, 1.5)); Console.WriteLine(MathX.Max(4, 8, 6)); static class MathX { public static int Max(int a, int b) = a b ? a : b; public static double Max(double a, double b) = a b ? a : b; public static int Max(int a, int b, int c) = Max(Max(a, b), c); } Local functions in a top-level program cannot be overloaded; methods in classes can. Optional and named arguments csharp Console.WriteLine(Format(1234.5)); Console.WriteLine(Format(1234.5, decimals: 0)); Console.WriteLine(Format(1234.5, prefix: "EUR ")); static string Format(double amount, int decimals = 2, string prefix = "") = prefix + amount.ToString("F" + decimals); Parameters with default values are optional; they must come after the required ones. Named arguments ( decimals: 0 ) make calls readable and let you skip optional parameters. params A params parameter accepts any number of arguments as an array: csharp Console.WriteLine(Sum()); Console.WriteLine(Sum(1, 2, 3)); int values = { 10, 20 }; Console.WriteLine(Sum(values)); static int Sum(params int numbers) { int total = 0; foreach (int n in numbers) total += n; return total; } ref, out and in Arguments are normally passed by value : the method gets a copy of the variable's value (for reference types, a copy of the reference). Three keywords pass the variable itself: csharp int a = 1, b = 2; Swap(ref a, ref b); Console.WriteLine($"{a} {b}"); if (TryDivide(10, 4, out double result)) Console.WriteLine(result); if (!TryDivide(1, 0, out _)) Console.WriteLine("cannot divide by zero"); static void Swap(ref int x, ref int y) = (x, y) = (y, x); static bool TryDivide(int x, int y, out double quotient) { if (y == 0) { quotient = 0; return false; } quotient = (double)x / y; return true; } - ref : the method can read and change the caller's variable. - out : the method must assign it; used for extra results, as in the TryParse pattern. out _ discards a result you do not need. - in : passed by reference but read-only, to avoid copying large structs. For several results, a tuple is often clearer than out : static (int Min, int Max) Range(int xs) , used as var (lo, hi) = Range(xs); . Recursion A method can call itself. Every recursive method needs a base case that stops: csharp Console.WriteLine(Factorial(10)); Console.WriteLine(Gcd(84, 36)); static long Factorial(int n) = n <= 1 ? 1 : n Factorial(n - 1); static int Gcd(int a, int b) = b == 0 ? a : Gcd(b, a % b); Without a base case, the calls never end and the program stops with a StackOverflowException . Good methods A method should do one thing that its name says. Prefer returning results over printing them: CalculateTotal that returns a number can be tested and reused; one that prints cannot. Keep reading input and printing at the edges of the program. Check yourself quiz ? What is the difference between ref and out? + ref needs the variable assigned before the call; out needs the method to assign it - ref passes a copy of the value; out passes the variable itself - out copies the value back at the end; ref shares the variable during the call - None: out is just the older spelling of ref Both pass the caller's own variable, not a copy. The difference is who must assign it: the caller before a ref call, the method before it returns for out . ? Can optional parameters come before required ones? - Yes, as long as every caller uses named arguments + No: optional parameters must come after all the required ones - Yes: the compiler moves them to the end for you - Only if the default value is null Optional parameters go at the end of the list. Named arguments let callers skip some optional ones, but they do not change where they may be declared. ? Given static int F(int x) { x = 5; return x; } , what is a after int a = 1; F(a); ? - 5 - 0 - an error + 1 The argument is passed by value: F changes its own copy.

title: Methods, out parameters and tuples
body: Complete the methods: csharp public static (int Min, int Max, double Mean) Stats(params int values) public static bool TryParseTime(string text, out int minutes) public static string Repeat(string text, int times, string separator = "") public static long Power(long baseValue, int exponent) - Stats throws an ArgumentException when there are no values. - TryParseTime("9:05", out int m) returns true with m = 545 (minutes after midnight). The text must be h:mm or hh:mm with hours 0 to 23 and minutes 00 to 59; otherwise it returns false and sets minutes to 0. - Repeat("ab", 3, "-") is "ab-ab-ab" ; 0 times gives "" . - Power is recursive and fast: b^e is (b^(e/2))² , times b once more when e is odd. e is 0 or more.

title: 2.02  Arrays and Lists
body: Fixed-size arrays and growable List<T - creating, indexing, ranges and Index from the end, iterating, adding, inserting and removing, searching, sorting with comparisons, copying versus sharing, collection expressions, and two-dimensional and jagged arrays. Arrays An array holds a fixed number of values of one type: csharp int scores = new int 3 ; // three zeros scores 0 = 90; scores 2 = 75; string days = { "Mon", "Tue", "Wed" }; int primes = 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 ; // a collection expression (C 12) Console.WriteLine(scores.Length); Console.WriteLine(days ^1 ); // last item Console.WriteLine(string.Join(",", primes 1..3 )); // 3,5 Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", scores)); Indexes start at 0. Reading scores 3 throws an IndexOutOfRangeException : C always checks bounds. List<T A List grows and shrinks. List<string is a list of strings: the type in angle brackets is a type argument (generics, lesson 4.01). csharp var names = new List<string { "Grace", "Ada" }; names.Add("Linus"); names.Insert(0, "Ken"); names.Remove("Grace"); // by value; returns false if not found names.RemoveAt(names.Count - 1); // by index Console.WriteLine($"{names.Count}: {string.Join(", ", names)}"); Console.WriteLine(names.Contains("Ada") + " " + names.IndexOf("Ada")); names.AddRange( "Barbara", "Margaret" ); Console.WriteLine(string.Join(", ", names)); Arrays use Length , lists use Count . Use an array when the size is fixed and known; use a list for everything that changes. Iterating csharp List<int numbers = 4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42 ; int sum = 0; foreach (int n in numbers) sum += n; for (int i = numbers.Count - 1; i = 0; i--) { if (numbers i % 2 == 1) numbers.RemoveAt(i); // removing: go backwards } Console.WriteLine($"{sum} {string.Join(" ", numbers)}"); Changing a list while foreach walks over it throws InvalidOperationException . Loop backwards with for , or use numbers.RemoveAll(n = n % 2 == 1) . Searching and sorting csharp var words = new List<string { "pear", "fig", "banana", "kiwi" }; words.Sort(); // alphabetical, in place Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", words)); words.Sort((a, b) = a.Length.CompareTo(b.Length)); // by length Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", words)); Console.WriteLine(words.Find(w = w.StartsWith("b"))); Console.WriteLine(words.Exists(w = w.Length 5)); int arr = 5, 1, 4 ; Array.Sort(arr); Console.WriteLine(Array.BinarySearch(arr, 4)); // index 1: needs a sorted array A comparison returns a negative number when a comes first, zero when equal, positive when b comes first; x.CompareTo(y) does that for numbers and strings. List.Sort is not stable: equal items may change order. LINQ's OrderBy (lesson 2.04) is stable and returns a new sequence. Copying versus sharing Arrays and lists are reference types: csharp var a = new List<int { 1, 2 }; var b = a; // the same list var c = new List<int (a); // a copy b.Add(3); Console.WriteLine($"{a.Count} {c.Count}"); // 3 2 int x = 1, 2, 3 ; int y = (int )x.Clone(); y 0 = 9; Console.WriteLine(x 0 ); // 1 A method that receives a list can change the caller's list. If it should not, accept IReadOnlyList<T instead: the method then cannot call Add or Remove . Two dimensions csharp int , grid = new int 3, 4 ; // rectangular: 3 rows, 4 columns grid 1, 2 = 7; Console.WriteLine($"{grid.GetLength(0)}x{grid.GetLength(1)}, {grid 1, 2 }"); int jagged = 1 , 2, 3 , 4, 5, 6 ; // an array of arrays, rows of any length foreach (int row in jagged) Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", row)); Check yourself quiz ? Why remove items from a list inside a loop by going backwards? - Going backwards is faster because lists are stored back to front - Removing while counting forwards always throws an exception + Removing shifts later items down; going backwards, the indexes still to visit do not move - RemoveAt only works on the last item, so you must start there Removing at i moves every later item down one place. Counting forwards with a for loop then silently skips an item; it does not throw (foreach is the loop that throws when the list changes). ? After var b = a; b.Add(1); does a contain the 1? - No: var b = a makes a copy of the list - No: b is a new empty list of the same type + Yes: a and b refer to the same list A List is a reference type, so b = a copies the reference, not the items. To copy the list, write new List<int (a) . ? What does new List<int { 3, 1, 2 }.IndexOf(5) return? - 0 - null + -1 - it throws IndexOf returns -1 when the value is not in the list.

title: Arrays and lists
body: Complete the methods. None of them may change the collections they are given. csharp public static int Rotate(int values, int k) // move every item k places to the right, wrapping around public static List<int MergeSorted(IReadOnlyList<int a, IReadOnlyList<int b) public static List<int RunningTotals(IReadOnlyList<int values) // 1, 2, 3 gives 1, 3, 6 public static List<string Compact(IReadOnlyList<string? items) // without nulls, blanks and repeats (first kept), trimmed - Rotate( 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 , 2) is 4, 5, 1, 2, 3 ; a negative k rotates left, and k may be larger than the length. - MergeSorted merges two sorted lists into one sorted list in a single pass (do not just sort the combined list). - Compact compares after trimming: " a", "a", null, " ", "b" gives "a", "b" .

title: 2.03  Dictionaries and Sets
body: Dictionary<TKey, TValue for lookups by key - adding, reading safely with TryGetValue, updating, counting and grouping, iterating key-value pairs - and HashSet<T for unique values and set operations, with case-insensitive keys, sorted variants and queues and stacks. Dictionary A dictionary maps keys to values , with fast lookup by key: csharp var ages = new Dictionary<string, int { "Ada" = 36, "Grace" = 85, }; ages "Linus" = 55; // add or replace ages.Add("Ken", 81); // add; throws if the key exists Console.WriteLine(ages "Ada" ); Console.WriteLine(ages.ContainsKey("Bob")); Console.WriteLine(ages.Count); ages.Remove("Grace"); foreach (var (name, age) in ages) Console.WriteLine($"{name}: {age}"); Reading a missing key with ages "Bob" throws KeyNotFoundException . Read safely with TryGetValue or GetValueOrDefault : csharp var stock = new Dictionary<string, int { "apple" = 3 }; if (stock.TryGetValue("pear", out int pears)) Console.WriteLine(pears); else Console.WriteLine("no pears"); Console.WriteLine(stock.GetValueOrDefault("pear", 0)); Counting and grouping Two patterns that come up constantly: csharp string text = "the cat and the hat and the bat"; var counts = new Dictionary<string, int (); foreach (string word in text.Split(' ')) { counts word = counts.GetValueOrDefault(word) + 1; } Console.WriteLine(string.Join(", ", counts.Select(kv = $"{kv.Key}={kv.Value}"))); var byFirstLetter = new Dictionary<char, List<string (); foreach (string word in new { "apple", "avocado", "banana", "blueberry", "cherry" }) { if (!byFirstLetter.TryGetValue(word 0 , out var list)) { list = new List<string (); byFirstLetter word 0 = list; } list.Add(word); } foreach (var (letter, words) in byFirstLetter) Console.WriteLine($"{letter}: {string.Join(" ", words)}"); LINQ's GroupBy and CountBy (lesson 2.04) do both in one line, but the loops show what happens. A Dictionary does not promise any order. In practice it keeps insertion order until items are removed, but do not rely on it: sort the keys when the order matters, or use a SortedDictionary , which keeps keys sorted. Keys Keys must not change while in a dictionary, and two keys are the same when Equals says so. For text keys that should ignore case, pass a comparer: csharp var users = new Dictionary<string, string (StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase) { "Ada" = "admin" }; Console.WriteLine(users "ADA" ); HashSet A HashSet holds unique values with fast Contains : csharp var seen = new HashSet<string (); foreach (string tag in new { "c ", "dotnet", "c ", "linq" }) { if (!seen.Add(tag)) Console.WriteLine($"duplicate: {tag}"); // Add returns false for repeats } var a = new HashSet<int { 1, 2, 3, 4 }; var b = new HashSet<int { 3, 4, 5 }; var both = new HashSet<int (a); both.IntersectWith(b); var either = new HashSet<int (a); either.UnionWith(b); a.ExceptWith(b); Console.WriteLine($"{string.Join(",", both)} {string.Join(",", either)} {string.Join(",", a)}"); list.Contains(x) checks every item; set.Contains(x) takes about the same time however large the set is. When you check membership often, use a set. Queues and stacks csharp var queue = new Queue<string (); // first in, first out queue.Enqueue("first"); queue.Enqueue("second"); Console.WriteLine(queue.Dequeue()); var stack = new Stack<int (); // last in, first out stack.Push(1); stack.Push(2); Console.WriteLine(stack.Pop() + " " + stack.Peek()); Queues suit work waiting its turn (and breadth-first search); stacks suit undo history and matching brackets. Check yourself quiz ? What happens when you read dict "missing" ? - It returns null, or 0 for a value type - It adds the key with a default value and returns that + It throws KeyNotFoundException; use TryGetValue or GetValueOrDefault instead Reading a missing key with the indexer throws. Returning the default is what GetValueOrDefault does, and only writing dict "missing" = v adds a key. ? What does HashSet.Add return for a value already in the set? + false, and the set is unchanged - true, and the value is now stored twice - Nothing: it throws an ArgumentException A set never holds duplicates, so Add reports false and changes nothing. Throwing for a duplicate is what Dictionary.Add does. ? Which collection should store "has this user name been taken?" for a million names? - List<string + HashSet<string - string - Queue<string HashSet.Contains takes about the same time however many items there are; a list checks every item.

title: Dictionaries and sets
body: Complete the methods: csharp public static Dictionary<string, int WordCounts(string text) // lower-case words; letters and ' only public static List<List<string GroupAnagrams(IEnumerable<string words) public static char? FirstRepeated(string text) // the first character seen a second time public static Dictionary<string, List<string Invert(Dictionary<string, string owners) - WordCounts splits the text into words made of letters and apostrophes (anything else separates words), lower-cased. - GroupAnagrams( "tea", "eat", "tan", "ate", "nat", "bat" ) gives "tea", "eat", "ate" , "tan", "nat" , "bat" : groups in the order their first word appears, words in their original order. Anagrams have the same letters in any order; compare ignoring case. - FirstRepeated("swiss") is 's' ; FirstRepeated("abc") is null . - Invert turns item → owner into owner → items, with each owner's items sorted alphabetically (ordinal).

title: 2.04  LINQ
body: Language Integrated Query - filtering, projecting and ordering with Where, Select, OrderBy and ThenBy, aggregates like Count, Sum, Average, Min and Max, First, Any and All, grouping with GroupBy and CountBy, ToDictionary, SelectMany, Distinct, Zip, deferred execution and query syntax. Queries over collections LINQ adds methods to every collection (anything that is an IEnumerable<T ) for filtering, transforming and summarising. Each takes a lambda , a small inline function written x = expression : csharp int numbers = 5, 3, 8, 1, 9, 2 ; var evensSquared = numbers.Where(n = n % 2 == 0).Select(n = n n); Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", evensSquared)); // 64 4 Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", numbers.OrderBy(n = n))); Console.WriteLine($"{numbers.Sum()} {numbers.Average():F2} {numbers.Max()} {numbers.Count(n = n 4)}"); using System.Linq; is needed in a project; the practice editor and new projects add it automatically. The common methods Method Gives --- --- Where(x = cond) The items that match Select(x = value) Each item transformed OrderBy(x = key) , OrderByDescending , ThenBy Sorted (stable) First() , FirstOrDefault() , Single() , Last() One item (First throws if none) Any(x = cond) , All(x = cond) , Contains(v) Tests Count() , Sum() , Average() , Min() , Max() Aggregates MinBy(x = key) , MaxBy(x = key) The item with the smallest / largest key Distinct() , DistinctBy(x = key) Without repeats Take(n) , Skip(n) , TakeWhile , Chunk(n) Parts GroupBy(x = key) , CountBy(x = key) Groups / counts per key ToList() , ToArray() , ToDictionary(k, v) , ToHashSet() Collected results SelectMany(x = many) Flattened Zip(other) Pairs Aggregate(seed, (acc, x) = ...) A general fold Working with records LINQ shines on lists of objects. Here, records (lesson 3.02) are short data classes: csharp var people = new List<Person { new("Ada", "London", 36), new("Grace", "New York", 85), new("Linus", "Helsinki", 55), new("Alan", "London", 41), }; var londoners = people.Where(p = p.City == "London").OrderBy(p = p.Name).Select(p = p.Name); Console.WriteLine(string.Join(", ", londoners)); var oldest = people.MaxBy(p = p.Age); Console.WriteLine(oldest!.Name); foreach (var group in people.GroupBy(p = p.City).OrderByDescending(g = g.Count())) { Console.WriteLine($"{group.Key}: {group.Count()} ({string.Join(", ", group.Select(p = p.Name))})"); } var ageByName = people.ToDictionary(p = p.Name, p = p.Age); Console.WriteLine(ageByName "Linus" ); Console.WriteLine(people.Any(p = p.Age 80) + " " + people.All(p = p.Age 30)); record Person(string Name, string City, int Age); GroupBy gives groups, each with a Key and its items. ToDictionary throws if two items have the same key. Flattening and pairing csharp var orders = new { new { "tea", "cake" }, new { "tea" }, new string 0 }; Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", orders.SelectMany(o = o).Distinct())); string names = "Ada", "Grace" ; int scores = 91, 88 ; foreach (var (name, score) in names.Zip(scores)) Console.WriteLine($"{name} {score}"); Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", Enumerable.Range(1, 5).Select(i = i i))); Deferred execution Where , Select , OrderBy and most other methods do not run when called: they build a query that runs each time you iterate over it. ToList() , Count() , Sum() and First() run it immediately. csharp var source = new List<int { 1, 2, 3 }; var big = source.Where(n = n 1); // nothing has run yet source.Add(10); Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", big)); // 2 3 10: the query sees the new item var snapshot = big.ToList(); // run once and keep the results If you iterate a query several times, or it is expensive, call ToList() once and reuse the list. Query syntax LINQ also has a SQL-like syntax, which the compiler turns into the same method calls: csharp int nums = 4, 9, 1, 7 ; var result = from n in nums where n 3 orderby n descending select n 10; Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", result)); Most C code uses the method syntax; query syntax is sometimes clearer for joins and several from clauses. Check yourself quiz ? What is the difference between First() and FirstOrDefault()? - First returns null when nothing matches; FirstOrDefault throws - They are the same, but FirstOrDefault is faster + First throws when nothing matches; FirstOrDefault returns the type's default First throws an InvalidOperationException for no match. FirstOrDefault returns default : null for classes, 0 for int. ? When does a Where query actually run? - Immediately, on the line where Where is called + When it is enumerated (foreach, ToList, Count, Sum), and again each time - The first time it is enumerated; later loops reuse those results - Whenever the source list changes LINQ queries are deferred and not cached: every enumeration runs the query again. Call ToList() to run it once and keep the results. ? What does new { 3, 1, 2 }.OrderBy(x = x).Select(x = x 2).Last() give? - 4 + 6 - 2 - 3 Sorted 1 2 3, doubled 2 4 6, the last is 6.

title: 2.05  Nullable Types and Pattern Matching
body: null and nullable reference types, the warnings that catch null bugs, the operators ?. ?? and ??=, nullable value types like int?, tuples, and pattern matching with is, switch expressions, type, relational, logical, property and list patterns. null A reference-type variable can hold null : no object at all. Using a member of null throws NullReferenceException , one of the most common crashes in any program. Modern C projects turn on nullable reference types ( <Nullable enable</Nullable , the default for new projects). Then string means "never null" and string? means "may be null", and the compiler warns when you use a string? without checking: csharp-norun string? middleName = GetMiddleName(); Console.WriteLine(middleName.Length); // warning CS8602: Dereference of a possibly null reference. if (middleName != null) Console.WriteLine(middleName.Length); // fine: checked first Treat these warnings as errors: each one is a possible crash. Null operators csharp string? name = null; Console.WriteLine(name?.Length); // ?. gives null instead of throwing (prints an empty line) int length = name?.Length ?? 0; // ?? supplies a fallback for null Console.WriteLine(length); name ??= "anonymous"; // assign only if null Console.WriteLine(name); string ? tags = null; Console.WriteLine(tags? 0 ?? "no tags"); The ! operator ( name!.Length ) tells the compiler "this is not null"; it changes nothing at run time, so use it only when you are sure. Nullable value types Value types cannot be null, unless you add ? : int? holds an int or null. It suits "no value yet" or "not given": csharp int? score = null; Console.WriteLine(score.HasValue); score = 42; Console.WriteLine(score.Value + 1); int? missing = null; Console.WriteLine((missing ?? -1) + " " + (missing + 5 == null)); // arithmetic with null gives null Tuples A tuple groups a few values without declaring a type, handy for returning several results: csharp var (min, max) = MinMax( 4, 9, 1, 7 ); Console.WriteLine($"{min} {max}"); (string Name, int Age) person = ("Ada", 36); Console.WriteLine(person.Name); static (int Min, int Max) MinMax(int values) = (values.Min(), values.Max()); Pattern matching is tests a value against a pattern , and can capture it in a variable: csharp object things = 42, "hello", 3.5, null!, new List<int { 1, 2 } ; foreach (object thing in things) { if (thing is int n && n 40) Console.WriteLine($"a big int {n}"); else if (thing is string s) Console.WriteLine($"a string of length {s.Length}"); else if (thing is null) Console.WriteLine("null"); else Console.WriteLine($"something else: {thing.GetType().Name}"); } Switch expressions combine patterns into a value: csharp Console.WriteLine(Classify(-5)); Console.WriteLine(Classify(0)); Console.WriteLine(Classify(7)); Console.WriteLine(Classify(150)); Console.WriteLine(Shipping(new Order(30, "NL", false))); Console.WriteLine(Shipping(new Order(120, "NL", false))); Console.WriteLine(Shipping(new Order(10, "US", true))); Console.WriteLine(Describe( 1, 2, 3 ) + " " + Describe( ) + " " + Describe( 7 )); static string Classify(int n) = n switch { < 0 = "negative", 0 = "zero", 0 and <= 100 = "small", _ = "large", }; static decimal Shipping(Order o) = o switch { { Express: true } = 25m, // property pattern { Total: = 100 } = 0m, { Country: "NL" or "BE" } = 4.95m, _ = 12m, }; static string Describe(int xs) = xs switch { = "empty", var only = $"one item {only}", var first, .., var last = $"from {first} to {last}", // list pattern }; record Order(decimal Total, string Country, bool Express); Pattern Matches --- --- 42 , "NL" , null That constant int n , string s That type, captured in a variable < 0 , = 1 and <= 5 Relational, combined with and , or , not { Total: = 100 } Objects whose properties match var a, .., var z Arrays and lists by shape _ Anything (the discard) Arms are tried from top to bottom; the compiler warns when a switch expression does not cover every possible value, and when an arm can never be reached. Check yourself quiz ? What does name?.Length ?? 0 give when name is null? - It throws a NullReferenceException - null + 0 ?. gives null instead of throwing, and ?? replaces that null with 0. ? Why does the order of switch arms matter? + Arms are tried from the top, and the first one that matches wins - The most specific arm wins, wherever it is written - Every arm that matches runs, from top to bottom - It does not; the compiler sorts the arms Only the first matching arm runs, so a broad arm (like _ ) above a narrower one hides it. The compiler reports an arm that can never be reached. ? What does x is 10 and < 20 test? - x is either above 10 or below 20 + x is between 10 and 20, both excluded - x is between 10 and 20, both included - it is not valid C Relational patterns combined with and must both match.

Summarize uses list patterns: "none" for an empty array, "just N" for one item, "N and M" for two, and "F ... L (K items)" for more, with the first, last and count.
