title: Settings that know they changed
body: Keep a settings struct, notice edits, and offer Apply and Revert. edit volume 0.8 - 0.5 (unsaved changes: 1) edit fullscreen false - true (unsaved changes: 2) revert - volume 0.8, fullscreen false edit and apply - saved, unsaved changes: 0

title: A searchable combo
body: Filter a long list as the user types, and move the highlight with the arrow keys. items: Apple Apricot Banana Blueberry Cherry typed "ap" - Apple Apricot, highlight Apple Down - Apricot Down - Apricot (stays at the end) typed "b" - Banana Blueberry, highlight reset to Banana Enter - selected Banana

title: Text with undo
body: Keep an undo history for a text field, grouping typing into words. type "Hello" type " " type "World" undo - "Hello " undo - "Hello" undo - "" redo - "Hello"

title: A developer console
body: Most games built with ImGui have a developer console: a text field where you type god , give gold 500 or teleport 12 40 , with history and Tab completion. ImGui gives you the text field and callbacks (lesson 2.02); write the logic behind them. cpp class Console { public: void addCommand(const std::string& name, std::function<std::string(const std::vector<std::string &) run); std::string execute(const std::string& line); // runs a line, returns what to print std::string historyUp(const std::string& current); // Up arrow: an older line std::string historyDown(const std::string& current); // Down arrow: a newer line std::string complete(const std::string& current); // Tab const std::vector<std::string & log() const; // everything printed so far }; Executing ( execute ): - Split the line into words on spaces; a part in double quotes is one word without its quotes ( say "hello there" gives say , hello there ). Empty input does nothing and returns "" . - The first word is the command name, matched without regard to case. Run it with the remaining words and return what it returns. - An unknown command returns Unknown command: <name . - Add plus the line to the log, then the result if it is not empty. Add the line to the history unless it is the same as the most recent history entry. - help is built in: it returns all command names, sorted, joined with ", " . History ( historyUp , historyDown ): like a terminal. Up from the edited line shows the newest history entry, then older ones; it stops at the oldest. Down goes back towards newer entries, and past the newest returns to the line that was being typed before Up was first pressed (the current argument at that first Up). execute resets the position. Completion ( complete ): complete the first word only, against the command names (and help ): - if exactly one name starts with it (ignoring case), return that name followed by a space; - if several do, return their longest common prefix (in lower case), or the input unchanged if that is no longer than the input, and add a log line listing the candidates sorted, joined with " " ; - if none do, return the input unchanged.

title: 3.01  Sizes, SameLine, Spacing and Groups
body: ImGui places widgets with a cursor that moves down after each one. This lesson shows how to control it - SameLine , item widths, spacing, indentation, groups, alignment and disabled sections - so a tool's window reads cleanly at any font size. The cursor Every window has a layout cursor . Each widget is placed at the cursor, then the cursor moves to the start of the next line. That is why widgets stack vertically by default. Everything in this lesson changes where the cursor goes, or how wide the next widget is. SameLine cpp-norun ImGui::Text("Stones:"); ImGui::SameLine(); // the next widget goes to the right of the last one ImGui::Text("%d", count); ImGui::SameLine(200.0f); // ...at x = 200 from the window's left edge ImGui::Button("Add"); ImGui::SameLine(0.0f, 2.0f); // default position, but only 2 pixels of spacing ImGui::Button("-"); Widths By default, widgets with a frame (sliders, inputs, combos) take about two thirds of the window width, leaving room for the label on the right. Change it: cpp-norun ImGui::SetNextItemWidth(120.0f); // the next widget only ImGui::DragFloat("Mass", &mass); ImGui::PushItemWidth(-FLT_MIN); // all following widgets: fill to the right edge ImGui::InputText(" notes", &notes); // (hide the label with , or it would be cut off) ImGui::PopItemWidth(); ImGui::PushItemWidth(ImGui::GetFontSize() 10); // ten "M" widths: scales with the font Prefer sizes based on GetFontSize() , GetFrameHeight() and GetContentRegionAvail() over fixed pixel numbers, so the tool still looks right when someone raises the font size or the display scale. cpp-norun const float avail = ImGui::GetContentRegionAvail().x; // width left on this line ImGui::Button("Half", ImVec2(avail 0.5f, 0)); // 0 height = the normal height Spacing, separators, indentation cpp-norun ImGui::Spacing(); // a little vertical space ImGui::Separator(); // a horizontal line ImGui::SeparatorText("Physics"); // a line with a title ImGui::Indent(); // move the left edge right (by the style's indent width) ImGui::Text("indented"); ImGui::Unindent(); ImGui::Dummy(ImVec2(0, 20)); // an invisible widget that takes space ImGui::NewLine(); // move to the next line, like pressing Enter Groups A group makes several widgets act as one item for layout: you can put the whole group on the same line as something else, and IsItemHovered asks about the whole group. cpp-norun ImGui::BeginGroup(); ImGui::Text("Player"); ImGui::Text("HP %d", hp); ImGui::Text("MP %d", mp); ImGui::EndGroup(); ImGui::SameLine(); // the next group sits to the right of the whole first group ImGui::BeginGroup(); ImGui::Text("Enemy"); ImGui::Text("HP %d", enemyHp); ImGui::EndGroup(); Alignment ImGui lays text from the top of the line. Next to a framed widget (a button, an input) plain text looks too high. Call ImGui::AlignTextToFramePadding() before such text to line it up with the frames on the same line. To right-align something, move the cursor yourself: cpp-norun const float w = ImGui::CalcTextSize("Delete").x + ImGui::GetStyle().FramePadding.x 2; ImGui::SameLine(ImGui::GetContentRegionMax().x - w); ImGui::Button("Delete"); CalcTextSize measures text with the current font. The practice uses that kind of measurement to lay out a row of buttons. Disabled sections cpp-norun ImGui::BeginDisabled(!level.loaded); // greyed out and not interactive while no level is loaded if (ImGui::Button("Save")) saveLevel(); ImGui::EndDisabled(); Better than hiding the button: the user sees it exists and why it cannot be used yet (add a tooltip, lesson 4.02). Common mistakes !warning Fixed pixel sizes everywhere They break at other font sizes and display scales. Measure from the font and the available width. !warning A full-width widget with a visible label The label is pushed off the right edge. Hide it with and put a Text in front instead. Check yourself quiz ? How does ImGui decide where a widget goes? + At the window's layout cursor, which moves to the next line after each widget unless SameLine or other layout calls change it - At a position you must give every widget, measured from the window's top-left corner - In a grid of rows and columns that ImGui works out from all the widgets at the end of the frame Widgets stack vertically because the cursor moves down after each one. Layout happens immediately, widget by widget. ? Why measure sizes from the font and the available region? - Because ImGui ignores sizes given in pixels + So the layout adapts to other font sizes, display scaling and window sizes - Because measured sizes make widgets draw faster A fixed 120 pixels looks cramped once someone raises the font size; GetFontSize() 10 grows with it. ? What does a group do? - It draws a frame around several widgets with a title, like a group box - It gives every widget inside it the same ID, so they share state + It makes several widgets act as one item for layout and item queries After EndGroup, SameLine puts the next widget to the right of the whole group, and IsItemHovered asks about all of it. ? Which call puts the next widget to the right of the previous one? - ImGui::NewLine() + ImGui::SameLine() - ImGui::Indent() SameLine moves the cursor back up to the end of the last item. Indent moves the left edge of following lines. ? What does a width of -FLT_MIN mean for PushItemWidth? - No width at all, so the widgets are hidden - The default width, about two thirds of the window + Fill up to the right edge of the window It is ImGui's idiom for "all the space that is left". Hide the label with or it is pushed off the edge. ? Why use BeginDisabled instead of hiding a button? - Disabled buttons cost less to draw than hidden ones do - Hidden buttons still receive clicks, disabled ones do not + The user sees the action exists and that it cannot be used right now Make it clear why with a tooltip.

title: Right-aligned buttons
body: Lay out a row of buttons aligned to the right edge of a window, the way dialog boxes put "Cancel Apply OK" at the bottom right. Text is measured with a fixed character width (a monospace font), so: buttonWidth(label) = label.size() charWidth + 2 framePadding Write cpp std::vector<float rightAlignedX(const std::vector<std::string & labels, float charWidth, float framePadding, float spacing, float contentMaxX, float contentMinX); It returns the left x position of each button, in the given order, so that: - the last button's right edge is exactly at contentMaxX ; - there are spacing pixels between neighbouring buttons; - if the row does not fit between contentMinX and contentMaxX , start the first button at contentMinX instead and let the row run off the right (never off the left). rightAlignedX({ "Cancel", "OK" }, 7, 4, 8, 400, 10) "Cancel" is 6 7+8 = 50 wide, "OK" is 2 7+8 = 22 wide, total 50 + 8 + 22 = 80 == { 320, 378 }

title: 3.02  Child Windows and Scrolling
body: A child window is a scrolling region inside a window - a list that scrolls while the buttons below it stay put, or a two-pane layout. This lesson covers BeginChild , sizing children to fill space, scrolling from code, auto-scrolling logs, and clipping so a list of a hundred thousand items costs nothing. BeginChild cpp-norun ImGui::BeginChild("stones", ImVec2(0, 200), ImGuiChildFlags_Borders); // full width, 200 high, with a border for (const Stone& s : stones) ImGui::Text("%s", s.name.c_str()); ImGui::EndChild(); // ALWAYS, like End if (ImGui::Button("Add")) addStone(); // stays below, not scrolled BeginChild / EndChild follow the window rule: EndChild is always called, whatever BeginChild returned. Sizes: 0 means "fill what is available", a positive number is a fixed size, a negative number means "fill, minus this much". So "a list that fills the window except for one row of buttons below it" is: cpp-norun const float footer = ImGui::GetFrameHeightWithSpacing(); // the height of one row of buttons ImGui::BeginChild("list", ImVec2(0, -footer), ImGuiChildFlags_Borders); // ... ImGui::EndChild(); ImGui::Button("Add"); Two panes side by side cpp-norun ImGui::BeginChild("left", ImVec2(200, 0), ImGuiChildFlags_Borders ImGuiChildFlags_ResizeX); // resizable drawLevelList(); ImGui::EndChild(); ImGui::SameLine(); ImGui::BeginChild("right"); // takes the rest drawLevelDetails(); ImGui::EndChild(); ImGuiChildFlags_ResizeX adds a handle on the child's right edge the user can drag. (Before version 1.90 the second argument of BeginChild was a bool border ; the flags replaced it.) Scrolling from code cpp-norun ImGui::SetScrollHereY(0.5f); // scroll so the current cursor position is in the middle ImGui::SetScrollY(0.0f); // to the top float y = ImGui::GetScrollY(), maxY = ImGui::GetScrollMaxY(); A log window wants to follow new lines, but only if the user has not scrolled up to read something: cpp-norun const bool atBottom = ImGui::GetScrollY() = ImGui::GetScrollMaxY(); // measure BEFORE adding lines for (const auto& line : log) ImGui::TextUnformatted(line.c_str()); if (atBottom) ImGui::SetScrollHereY(1.0f); // keep following Clipping long lists Drawing 100,000 lines every frame is slow even if only 30 are visible. ImGuiListClipper works out which items are on screen, so you only draw those, while the scroll bar still behaves as if all of them were there: cpp-norun ImGuiListClipper clipper; clipper.Begin((int)lines.size()); // all items have the same height while (clipper.Step()) for (int i = clipper.DisplayStart; i < clipper.DisplayEnd; ++i) ImGui::TextUnformatted(lines i .c_str()); The idea is simple arithmetic: with each item h pixels high, the scroll position y and the visible height H , the first visible item is floor(y / h) and the last is ceil((y + H) / h) . The clipper reserves empty space for the items above and below so the scroll bar is right. The practice writes this calculation. Clipping needs every item to have the same height . For variable heights, keep a prefix sum of heights and binary-search it, or group items into rows of equal height. Common mistakes !warning Calling EndChild only when BeginChild returned true Like End, EndChild is always called. !warning Auto-scroll that fights the user Check whether you were at the bottom before adding lines, and only follow then. !warning Drawing every line of a huge log Use ImGuiListClipper; the cost then depends on the window height, not the log length. Check yourself quiz ? What does a negative child size mean? - The child is hidden until the user scrolls to it + Fill the available space minus that amount, leaving room for widgets after the child - A fixed size measured from the right or bottom edge of the screen 0 fills all the space, a positive number is a fixed size, and a negative one fills minus that much. ? How does ImGuiListClipper make a huge list cheap? + It computes which equal-height items are visible from the scroll position and draws only those, while reserving space for the rest - It draws every item once into a texture and reuses the texture each frame - It draws a different slice of the list each frame, so the whole list is drawn over many frames Only the visible items are drawn, so the cost depends on the window height, not the list length, and the scroll bar still behaves as if all items were there. ? How do you make a log follow new lines without fighting the user? - Call SetScrollHereY(1.0f) every frame after drawing the lines - Call SetScrollY(0.0f) each time a new line is added + Scroll to the bottom only if it was already at the bottom Check whether the scroll is at the bottom before adding lines. Scrolling down every frame drags the user away from whatever they scrolled up to read. ? A child should fill the window except for 40 pixels of buttons below it. What height do you pass? - 40 + -40 - 0 Negative sizes mean "fill, minus this much"; 0 would fill everything and push the buttons out of view. ? What must be true of the items for ImGuiListClipper to work? - They are sorted - There are fewer than 1000 of them + They all have the same height It computes the visible range from a fixed item height. For variable heights you need a prefix sum of heights instead. ? With items 20 pixels high, scrolled to y = 1000, what is the first visible item? - 20 + 50 - 1000 - 51 floor(1000 / 20) = 50, counting items from 0.

title: What the clipper draws
body: Write the calculation inside ImGuiListClipper : cpp struct Range { int start; int end; }; // draw items start .. end-1 Range visibleRange(int itemCount, float itemHeight, float scrollY, float viewHeight); float contentHeight(int itemCount, float itemHeight); bool shouldFollow(float scrollY, float scrollMaxY); - visibleRange : the first visible item is floor(scrollY / itemHeight) ; the end is ceil((scrollY + viewHeight) / itemHeight) . Clamp both to 0 .. itemCount . An item height of 0 or less, or no items, gives {0, 0} . - contentHeight : the total height the scroll bar must cover. - shouldFollow : a log keeps following new lines only if it was scrolled to the bottom: scrollY = scrollMaxY - 1 (allowing one pixel of rounding). visibleRange(100000, 20, 1000, 300) == { 50, 65 }

title: 3.03  Tables
body: Tables are ImGui's most capable layout tool - columns that resize, reorder, hide and sort, frozen header rows, scrolling with clipping, and alternate row backgrounds. This lesson builds an entity table step by step and explains sorting specs, the part most people find confusing. A basic table cpp-norun if (ImGui::BeginTable("entities", 3, ImGuiTableFlags_Borders ImGuiTableFlags_RowBg)) { ImGui::TableSetupColumn("Name"); ImGui::TableSetupColumn("HP", ImGuiTableColumnFlags_WidthFixed, 60.0f); ImGui::TableSetupColumn("Position"); ImGui::TableHeadersRow(); for (const Entity& e : entities) { ImGui::TableNextRow(); ImGui::TableNextColumn(); ImGui::TextUnformatted(e.name.c_str()); ImGui::TableNextColumn(); ImGui::Text("%d", e.hp); ImGui::TableNextColumn(); ImGui::Text("%.1f, %.1f", e.x, e.y); } ImGui::EndTable(); // only if BeginTable returned true } BeginTable returns false when the table is clipped (scrolled out of view); then you skip it and do not call EndTable (lesson 1.04's second rule). Inside, any widget can go in any cell. Useful flags Flag Effect --- --- Resizable Drag column borders to resize Reorderable Drag headers to reorder columns Hideable Right-click the header to hide columns Sortable Click headers to sort (see below) ScrollY (with an outer size) The table scrolls; combine with TableSetupScrollFreeze(0, 1) to keep the header row visible RowBg Alternate row colours SizingFixedFit , SizingStretchProp ... How column widths are chosen The table remembers widths, order, visibility and sort per table ID, and saves them in imgui.ini (lesson 4.06). Scrolling a large table cpp-norun const ImVec2 outer(0, ImGui::GetTextLineHeightWithSpacing() 15); // 15 rows high if (ImGui::BeginTable("big", 3, ImGuiTableFlags_ScrollY ImGuiTableFlags_RowBg, outer)) { ImGui::TableSetupScrollFreeze(0, 1); // keep the first row (headers) visible / TableSetupColumn x3, TableHeadersRow / ImGuiListClipper clipper; clipper.Begin((int)rows.size()); while (clipper.Step()) for (int i = clipper.DisplayStart; i < clipper.DisplayEnd; ++i) { / TableNextRow, cells for rows i / } ImGui::EndTable(); } Sorting With ImGuiTableFlags_Sortable , clicking a header changes the table's sort specs . ImGui does not sort your data: it tells you what the user asked for, and you sort. cpp-norun if (ImGuiTableSortSpecs specs = ImGui::TableGetSortSpecs()) { if (specs- SpecsDirty) // the user changed the sort (or first frame) { std::sort(entities.begin(), entities.end(), & (const Entity& a, const Entity& b) { for (int n = 0; n < specs- SpecsCount; ++n) { const ImGuiTableColumnSortSpecs& s = specs- Specs n ; // ColumnIndex, SortDirection int cmp = compareColumn(a, b, s.ColumnIndex); // -1, 0 or 1 if (cmp != 0) return s.SortDirection == ImGuiSortDirection_Ascending ? cmp < 0 : cmp 0; } return false; }); specs- SpecsDirty = false; } } Call this after TableSetupColumn / TableHeadersRow and before the rows. Key points: - Sort only when SpecsDirty , not every frame. - With ImGuiTableFlags_SortMulti , Shift-clicking adds secondary sort columns: Specs 0 is the primary key, Specs 1 breaks its ties, and so on. The loop above handles any number. - ColumnIndex is the column's place in your TableSetupColumn calls (dragging headers around does not change it). If the set of columns your code sets up can change (optional columns, a different order in another view), give each column a stable meaning with TableSetupColumn("Name", flags, width, userId) and compare by ColumnUserID . The practice writes this multi-key comparison. Common mistakes !warning Sorting every frame Sort when SpecsDirty is set, then clear it. !warning Expecting ImGui to sort the data It only reports what the user clicked. Your data, your sort. Check yourself quiz ? What does TableSetupScrollFreeze(0, 1) do? - Stops the table from scrolling until the first row is clicked + Keeps the first row, normally the headers, visible while the table scrolls - Freezes the first column so it cannot be resized The arguments are columns then rows to freeze: 0 columns and 1 row. ? How do you sort a table's data? - Pass ImGuiTableFlags_Sortable and ImGui reorders your vector when a header is clicked - Sort the data every frame by the first column, before BeginTable + When TableGetSortSpecs reports SpecsDirty, sort by its specs, then clear the flag After setting up the columns, compare column by column in spec order, each in its direction. ImGui only reports what the user asked for, and sorting every frame wastes time. ? Why compare by a column's user ID rather than its index? - Because ColumnIndex changes whenever the user drags a header to a new place + A user ID names the column's meaning, so the comparison stays right even if the columns your code sets up change - Because ColumnIndex is only filled in when SortMulti is on ColumnIndex is the column's place in your TableSetupColumn calls; if optional columns come and go, the indexes shift but a user ID does not. ? When BeginTable returns false, what do you do? + Skip the table and do not call EndTable - Call EndTable anyway, as with End for windows - Call BeginTable again with a larger size Tables follow the "End only if Begin returned true" rule. ? With SortMulti, the user sorts by Team, then Shift-clicks HP. What is Specs 1 ? - Team + HP, which breaks ties between rows with the same Team - Nothing; only one key is allowed Specs are in order of priority: Specs 0 is the primary key. ? Who sorts the rows of an ImGui table? - ImGui, automatically, when Sortable is set + Your code, using the sort specs when they are dirty - The renderer back end, when it draws the rows ImGui reports the requested order; you apply it to your data.

title: Sort by the table's specs
body: A sortable table hands you a list of sort specs, most important first. Sort the rows the way they ask: cpp struct Row { std::string name; std::string team; int hp; }; struct SortSpec { int column; bool ascending; }; // 0 = name, 1 = team, 2 = hp void sortRows(std::vector<Row & rows, const std::vector<SortSpec & specs); - Compare by the first spec's column; if equal, by the second's; and so on. - Text columns compare as plain strings; hp compares as a number. - Each spec has its own direction. - Rows equal in every spec keep their original order (use a stable sort). - No specs: leave the order alone.

title: 3.04  Trees and Selection
body: A scene hierarchy, a file browser and an asset list all need a tree and a selection that behaves like every other program - click to select, Ctrl+click to add, Shift+click for a range. This lesson covers TreeNode and its flags, building a tree from your data, and implementing multi-selection properly. Tree nodes cpp-norun if (ImGui::TreeNode("Level")) // true while open { ImGui::Text("child item"); if (ImGui::TreeNode("Props")) { ImGui::Text("rock"); ImGui::TreePop(); } ImGui::TreePop(); // only if TreeNode returned true } ImGui remembers whether each node is open by its ID (lesson 1.05), so two nodes with the same label in the same place open and close together. In a loop, use PushID or the TreeNode(ptr_id, fmt, ...) overload, which takes a pointer as the ID and a separate display text. TreeNodeEx and its flags cpp-norun ImGuiTreeNodeFlags flags = ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_OpenOnArrow // click the arrow to open, the label to select ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_OpenOnDoubleClick ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_SpanAvailWidth; // the whole row is clickable if (node.children.empty()) flags = ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_Leaf ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_NoTreePushOnOpen; if (isSelected(node.id)) flags = ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_Selected; const bool open = ImGui::TreeNodeEx((void )(intptr_t)node.id, flags, "%s", node.name.c_str()); if (ImGui::IsItemClicked() && !ImGui::IsItemToggledOpen()) // clicked the label, not the arrow select(node.id); - Leaf draws no arrow; with NoTreePushOnOpen you also skip TreePop for it. - DefaultOpen opens a node the first time it is seen. - ImGui::SetNextItemOpen(true) opens the next node from code: "reveal the selected object in the tree". Building a tree from your data Scene data is usually a flat list where each object knows its parent. Draw it recursively: cpp-norun void drawNode(const Scene& scene, int id) { const Object& o = scene.objects id ; ImGuiTreeNodeFlags flags = ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_OpenOnArrow ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_SpanAvailWidth; if (o.children.empty()) flags = ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_Leaf ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_NoTreePushOnOpen; const bool open = ImGui::TreeNodeEx((void )(intptr_t)id, flags, "%s", o.name.c_str()); if (open && !o.children.empty()) { for (int child : o.children) drawNode(scene, child); ImGui::TreePop(); } } The practice builds the "children of each node" lists from parent links and produces the order rows appear in, which is also what Shift+click ranges need. Selection that behaves Users expect: Action Result --- --- Click Select only this item; it becomes the anchor Ctrl+click Toggle this item, keep the others; it becomes the anchor Shift+click Select every item between the anchor and this one , in display order, replacing the selection Ctrl+Shift+click Add that range to the existing selection The anchor is the last item clicked without Shift. Ranges are measured in display order : the order rows appear on screen, which for a tree is depth-first over the open nodes. Store the selection as a set of stable IDs, never as row positions, so it survives sorting and filtering. Dear ImGui 1.91 added a full multi-select API ( BeginMultiSelect / EndMultiSelect ) that handles these rules, box-selection and keyboard navigation for you; writing the rules yourself once, as the practice does, makes it much easier to use well. Common mistakes !warning Selecting when the arrow was clicked Check IsItemToggledOpen so opening a node does not also select it. !warning Storing the selection as row numbers Rows change when the list is sorted, filtered or a node opens. Store IDs. Check yourself quiz ? What are the Leaf and NoTreePushOnOpen flags for? - Leaf keeps a node always open; NoTreePushOnOpen stops it being selected + Leaf draws a node without an arrow for items with no children; NoTreePushOnOpen means TreePop must not be called for it - Leaf hides the node's label; NoTreePushOnOpen makes it open on a double click With NoTreePushOnOpen the node does not push onto the tree stack when open, so there is nothing to pop. ? What is the anchor in multi-selection? - The first item in the list, where every Shift+click range starts - The item under the mouse when the button was pressed + The last item clicked without Shift; Shift+click selects from it to the clicked item in display order A plain click or a Ctrl+click moves the anchor; a Shift+click does not. ? How do you open a tree node from code to reveal a selected object? + Call SetNextItemOpen(true) before drawing each of its ancestors - Add ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_DefaultOpen to the selected object's node - Call TreePush with the object's ID after drawing the tree Every ancestor must be open for the object to appear. DefaultOpen only applies the first time a node is seen. ? What does ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_OpenOnArrow change? + Only clicking the arrow opens the node, so clicking the label can select it - The node is always open and has no arrow - The node opens when the mouse hovers over its arrow It separates opening from selecting; check IsItemToggledOpen so the arrow click does not also select. ? The anchor is item 3 and the user Shift+clicks item 7. What is selected? - Only item 7, replacing the previous selection - Items 3 and 7, added to the previous selection + Items 3 to 7, replacing the previous selection Shift+click selects the range from the anchor in display order; Ctrl+Shift+click would add it to the existing selection instead. ? Why store selected items by ID rather than by row number? - IDs take less memory than row numbers do in a set + Rows change with sorting, filtering and opening nodes; IDs do not - ImGui's TreeNodeEx only accepts IDs, never row numbers The selection must survive changes to what is shown.

title: Rows of a tree
body: A scene is a flat list of objects, each knowing its parent ( -1 for a root). Write the order the tree's rows appear on screen: cpp struct Object { int id; int parent; std::string name; }; std::vector<int displayOrder(const std::vector<Object & objects, const std::set<int & open); - Roots come first-to-last in the order they appear in objects ; so do the children of each object. - A row is shown for every root, and for every child of an open object whose own row is shown (depth first: an object's children come right after it, before its next sibling). - Return the ids in row order. objects: 1 "Level" (root), 2 "Props" (parent 1), 3 "Rock" (parent 2), 4 "Lights" (parent 1), 5 "UI" (root) open {1} - 1, 2, 4, 5 open {1, 2} - 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 open {2} - 1, 5 (2 is open but its parent is closed, so it is not shown)

title: Click, Ctrl+click, Shift+click
body: Implement selection that behaves like every desktop program, over rows in display order (as produced above): cpp class Selection { public: void click(const std::vector<int & rows, int id, bool ctrl, bool shift); bool isSelected(int id) const; std::vector<int selected() const; // sorted by id int anchor() const; // -1 when there is none }; Action Result --- --- Click Select only id ; it becomes the anchor Ctrl+click Toggle id , keep the rest; it becomes the anchor Shift+click Replace the selection with every row from the anchor to id , inclusive, in rows order Ctrl+Shift+click Add that range to the current selection - With Shift but no anchor (or an anchor not in rows ), behave like a plain click (or a Ctrl+click, if Ctrl is held too). - Shift+click does not move the anchor, so the user can Shift+click again to change the range end.

title: 3.05  Tabs, Collapsing Headers and Tooltips
body: Tools have more settings than fit on one screen. This lesson covers the ways to organise them - collapsing headers, tab bars, and the old Columns API you will meet in existing code - plus tooltips and help markers, so every setting can explain itself. Collapsing headers A collapsing header is a full-width bar that hides or shows the section below it. Inspectors are usually a stack of them: cpp-norun if (ImGui::CollapsingHeader("Transform", ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_DefaultOpen)) { ImGui::DragFloat3("Position", &t.pos.x, 0.1f); ImGui::DragFloat3("Rotation", &t.rot.x, 1.0f); } if (ImGui::CollapsingHeader("Physics")) { ImGui::DragFloat("Mass", &body.mass, 0.1f, 0.0f, 1000.0f); } It is a tree node that does not push to the ID stack and needs no TreePop . Pass a bool as a second argument and it also gets a close button, handy for "remove this component" in an inspector. Tab bars cpp-norun if (ImGui::BeginTabBar("settings", ImGuiTabBarFlags_Reorderable)) { if (ImGui::BeginTabItem("Graphics")) { drawGraphics(); ImGui::EndTabItem(); } if (ImGui::BeginTabItem("Audio")) { drawAudio(); ImGui::EndTabItem(); } if (ImGui::BeginTabItem("Controls")) { drawControls(); ImGui::EndTabItem(); } ImGui::EndTabBar(); } Both pairs follow the "End only if Begin returned true" rule. A bool open on BeginTabItem gives the tab a close button (an editor with one tab per open file). To switch to a tab from code, pass ImGuiTabItemFlags_SetSelected on that frame. The old Columns API Older code uses ImGui::Columns(2) , NextColumn() and Columns(1) to split a window into columns. It still works but is legacy : tables (lesson 3.03) do everything it did and more. When you meet Columns in an existing tool, consider converting it to a two-column table with ImGuiTableFlags_SizingStretchProp . Tooltips cpp-norun ImGui::DragFloat("Drag", &body.drag, 0.01f); ImGui::SetItemTooltip("Air resistance. 0 = none, 1 = moves through syrup."); // shown when the last item is hovered if (ImGui::IsItemHovered(ImGuiHoveredFlags_DelayNormal)) // a richer tooltip after a short delay { ImGui::BeginTooltip(); ImGui::Text("Drag curve"); ImGui::PlotLines(" curve", samples, IM_ARRAYSIZE(samples)); ImGui::EndTooltip(); } SetItemTooltip covers most cases. With BeginTooltip / EndTooltip you can put any widgets inside. The help marker A common pattern from the demo window: a small greyed "(?)" after a setting that shows an explanation when hovered: cpp-norun static void HelpMarker(const char text) { ImGui::SameLine(); ImGui::TextDisabled("(?)"); if (ImGui::BeginItemTooltip()) { ImGui::PushTextWrapPos(ImGui::GetFontSize() 30.0f); // wrap at about 30 characters wide ImGui::TextUnformatted(text); ImGui::PopTextWrapPos(); ImGui::EndTooltip(); } } Wrapping long help text matters: an unwrapped tooltip can be wider than the screen. The practice writes a word-wrap function like the one ImGui uses for TextWrapped . Common mistakes !warning Calling EndTabItem for a tab that is not selected BeginTabItem returns true only for the visible tab. EndTabItem goes inside the if. !warning Tooltips with very long unwrapped text Push a text wrap position, or use TextWrapped. Check yourself quiz ? Which pairs follow the "End only if Begin returned true" rule in this lesson? - Only BeginTabBar/EndTabBar; EndTabItem is always called, like End + BeginTabBar/EndTabBar, BeginTabItem/EndTabItem, and BeginItemTooltip/EndTooltip - None of them; tabs and tooltips follow the window rule BeginTabItem returns true only for the visible tab, so EndTabItem goes inside the if. Only windows and child windows always need their End. ? How do you select a tab from code? - Call BeginTabItem for that tab first, before the others - Set the tab bar's ImGuiTabBarFlags_Reorderable flag and move the tab to the front + Pass ImGuiTabItemFlags_SetSelected to its BeginTabItem on that frame The flag applies on the frame you pass it; the order you submit tabs in does not choose the selected one. ? Why wrap tooltip text? - Because tooltips cannot show more than one line otherwise + Long unwrapped text makes the tooltip wider than the screen - Because ImGui cuts off tooltip text past 80 characters Pushing a wrap position keeps it readable: PushTextWrapPos(GetFontSize() 30) wraps at about 30 characters wide. ? What is the difference between CollapsingHeader and TreeNode? + CollapsingHeader does not push the ID stack and needs no TreePop - CollapsingHeader cannot be closed or reopened by the user - TreeNode is always full width, CollapsingHeader is not It is a full-width, header-style section toggle; TreeNode pushes the ID stack while open and needs TreePop. ? Which call shows a simple tooltip for the widget just drawn? - ImGui::BeginTooltip() with no checks + ImGui::SetItemTooltip("...") - ImGui::Text("...") on the same line It shows only when the last item is hovered. An unchecked BeginTooltip would show all the time. ? You find ImGui::Columns(2) in old code. What should you consider? - Deleting it; it no longer compiles - Nothing; it is the recommended API + Converting it to a two-column table Columns is legacy and still works; tables do everything it did and more.

title: Wrap tooltip text
body: Long help text in a tooltip must wrap. Write the word wrap TextWrapped does, with widths counted in characters: cpp std::vector<std::string wrapText(const std::string& text, int width); - Words are separated by spaces. Put as many words on a line as fit in width characters, with one space between words. - A word longer than width goes on a line of its own, cut into pieces of width characters. - A newline \n in the text always starts a new line (an empty line between two \n stays as an empty line). - Several spaces in a row count as one. No line starts or ends with a space. - width below 1 is treated as 1. wrapText("Air resistance. 0 means none.", 12) == { "Air", "resistance.", "0 means", "none." }

title: Flow layout
body: Place tags on lines, wrapping when the next one does not fit, like SameLine with wrapping. width 120, spacing 8 line 1: player 50 enemy 45 line 2: boss 35 npc 30 item 30 line 3: very long tag name 110

title: Sorting a table
body: Sort table rows when a column header is clicked, the way ImGuiTableSortSpecs asks you to. click Name - sorted by name ascending click Name - descending click Level - level ascending, equal levels by name

title: Tabs that close
body: Manage open document tabs: open, close, reorder, and choose which tab to show after closing. open a.txt b.txt c.txt, select b.txt close b.txt - select c.txt (the one to the right) close c.txt - select a.txt (no tab to the right) open a.txt again - just selects it

title: A filtered tree
body: Show a tree where a search keeps matching nodes and their parents, and opens the path to them. filter "sword": Items Weapons Iron sword Fire sword (Armour and Potions hidden; Items and Weapons opened)

title: An entity browser
body: Combine the milestone into the model behind a real tool window: a table of entities with a filter box, sortable columns, multi-selection and a clipped, scrolling body. cpp struct Entity { int id; std::string name; std::string team; int hp; }; struct SortSpec { int column; bool ascending; }; // 0 name, 1 team, 2 hp class EntityBrowser { public: explicit EntityBrowser(std::vector<Entity entities); void setFilter(const std::string& filter); // lesson 2.03's word matching on name and team void setSort(const std::vector<SortSpec & specs); // lesson 3.03 std::vector<int rows() const; // ids of visible entities, filtered and sorted void click(int id, bool ctrl, bool shift); // lesson 3.04's rules over rows() std::vector<int selected() const; // sorted ids std::vector<int visibleRows(float scrollY, float viewHeight, float rowHeight) const; // lesson 3.02, ids void removeSelected(); // deletes the selected entities int count() const; // entities left }; Rules: - rows() holds the entities whose name or team match the filter, sorted by the specs (stable; with no specs, in the original order). - The selection is by id and survives filtering and sorting. Selected entities that the filter hides stay selected. - click uses the current rows() as display order for Shift ranges. - visibleRows returns the ids of the rows the clipper would draw for that scroll position. - removeSelected deletes every selected entity, including hidden ones, and clears the selection and the anchor.

title: 4.01  Menus and Shortcuts
body: A main menu bar turns a pile of windows into an application - File, Edit, View, Tools. This lesson covers menu bars in the main viewport and in windows, menu items with checkmarks and shortcut text, the Begin/End rule for menus, and wiring the shortcuts so they actually work. The main menu bar cpp-norun if (ImGui::BeginMainMenuBar()) // across the top of the screen { if (ImGui::BeginMenu("File")) { if (ImGui::MenuItem("New level", "Ctrl+N")) newLevel(); if (ImGui::MenuItem("Open...", "Ctrl+O")) openDialog(); if (ImGui::MenuItem("Save", "Ctrl+S", false, level.dirty)) save(); // disabled when nothing changed ImGui::Separator(); if (ImGui::MenuItem("Quit", "Alt+F4")) running = false; ImGui::EndMenu(); } if (ImGui::BeginMenu("View")) { ImGui::MenuItem("Stones", nullptr, &showStones); // a checkmark bound to a bool ImGui::MenuItem("Log", nullptr, &showLog); ImGui::EndMenu(); } ImGui::EndMainMenuBar(); } This is the pair rule you met in lesson 1.04: BeginMainMenuBar / EndMainMenuBar and BeginMenu / EndMenu are only ended if their Begin returned true . A closed menu returns false , so its EndMenu is skipped. MenuItem has two useful forms: - MenuItem(label, shortcut, selected, enabled) returns true when clicked; selected draws a checkmark, enabled = false greys it out. - MenuItem(label, shortcut, bool selected) toggles the bool when clicked: the standard "show window" switch. Menus can nest: a BeginMenu inside another opens a sub-menu. A menu bar inside a window cpp-norun ImGui::Begin("Level editor", nullptr, ImGuiWindowFlags_MenuBar); if (ImGui::BeginMenuBar()) { if (ImGui::BeginMenu("Edit")) { / ... / ImGui::EndMenu(); } ImGui::EndMenuBar(); } // window contents ImGui::End(); Shortcut text is only text The second argument of MenuItem ("Ctrl+S") is only displayed . Clicking the menu item works; pressing Ctrl+S does nothing unless you also check the keys. Do that once, outside the menu code, so the shortcut works even when the menu is closed: cpp-norun if (ImGui::Shortcut(ImGuiMod_Ctrl ImGuiKey_S, ImGuiInputFlags_RouteGlobal)) save(); A tidy approach is a table of commands : each has a name, a shortcut, an "is it available" check and an action. The menu draws from the table, the shortcut handler checks the table, and a command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P, like editors have) can list it too. The practice builds that table, including detecting two commands that claim the same shortcut. Keyboard navigation in menus With ImGuiConfigFlags_NavEnableKeyboard , pressing Alt focuses the menu bar, arrow keys move through it, Enter activates and Escape closes, the way desktop applications behave. Common mistakes !warning Calling EndMenu when BeginMenu returned false ImGui asserts. EndMenu goes inside the if. !warning Expecting the shortcut text to work by itself It is a label. Check the keys with Shortcut or IsKeyPressed. !warning Two commands on the same shortcut Only one will ever run, depending on which is checked first. Detect clashes when you build the command table. Check yourself quiz ? Which menu functions follow the "End only if Begin returned true" rule? - Only BeginMenu/EndMenu; the menu bars always need their End call - None of them; menus always need their End call, like windows + BeginMainMenuBar/EndMainMenuBar, BeginMenuBar/EndMenuBar and BeginMenu/EndMenu - Only BeginMainMenuBar/EndMainMenuBar All three menu pairs are ended only when their Begin returned true. Begin / End for windows is the exception that always calls End . ? How do you make a menu's shortcut actually work? - Pass the shortcut text as MenuItem's second argument, and ImGui detects the keys + Check the key chord yourself, for example with ImGui::Shortcut , once per frame outside the menu code - Check the keys inside the BeginMenu block, next to the MenuItem - Enable ImGuiConfigFlags_NavEnableKeyboard The shortcut text is only a label. Checking the keys inside the menu block would only work while the menu is open. ? Why build menus from a command table? - Because ImGui can only draw menus from an array of items - Because a table makes the menu draw faster than separate calls - So that each command can be given more than one shortcut key + One list drives the menu, shortcuts and palette, and catches shortcut clashes The table is your own design, not something ImGui needs; its value is that everything about a command, including when it is available, lives in one place. ? BeginMenu("File") returns false because the menu is closed. What do you do? - Call EndMenu anyway, so the Begin/End calls stay balanced + Skip its items and do not call EndMenu - Call BeginMenu again next frame with a different label Menus follow the "End only if Begin returned true" rule; calling EndMenu after a false Begin makes ImGui assert. ? What does the "Ctrl+S" argument of MenuItem do? - It registers a global shortcut for that item - It sends Ctrl+S to the window when the item is clicked + It is shown next to the item; it does not detect the keys It is display text only. Detect the shortcut separately. ? Which MenuItem form toggles a bool when clicked? + MenuItem(label, shortcut, &flag) - MenuItem(label, shortcut, flag, true) - MenuItem(label, shortcut, false, flag) The bool form flips the bool for you, which is ideal for showing and hiding windows. The bool forms only draw a checkmark or enable the item.

title: A command table
body: Menus, shortcuts and a command palette work best from one table of commands. Write it: cpp struct Command { std::string name; // "File/Save" std::string shortcut; // "Ctrl+S", or "" for none (already in a normal form: modifiers Ctrl, Shift, Alt in that order) std::function<bool() enabled; // may be empty: always enabled std::function<void() run; }; class Commands { public: void add(Command c); std::vector<std::string clashes() const; // "Ctrl+S: File/Save, Edit/Select" for each shortcut used twice or more bool press(const std::string& shortcut); // run the command with this shortcut, if any is enabled std::vector<std::string menu(const std::string& top) const; // items under a top-level menu }; - clashes : one line per shortcut used by two or more commands, in alphabetical order of shortcut; the command names in the order they were added, joined with ", " . - press : among commands with this shortcut, run the first added one that is enabled and return true ; return false if none is enabled or none has it. - menu("File") : for each command whose name starts with File/ , in order added, the text after File/ , followed by " " and the shortcut if it has one, and (disabled) if its enabled returns false right now.

title: 4.02  Popups, Context Menus and Modals
body: Popups are small windows that appear on request and close when you click elsewhere - right-click menus, pickers, confirmations. This lesson explains ImGui's popup model (open by ID, draw every frame while open), context menus on items and windows, modal dialogs that block the rest of the interface, and the classic "unsaved changes" confirmation. Opening and drawing are separate A popup has an ID, like a widget. You open it once, in reaction to something, and you draw it every frame with BeginPopup , which returns true only while it is open: cpp-norun if (ImGui::Button("Pick a stone")) ImGui::OpenPopup("stone picker"); // once, on click if (ImGui::BeginPopup("stone picker")) // every frame { for (const char s : { "Granite", "Basalt", "Slate" }) if (ImGui::Selectable(s)) chosen = s; // a Selectable closes the popup ImGui::EndPopup(); // only if BeginPopup returned true } The popup closes by itself when the user clicks outside it, presses Escape, or clicks a Selectable / MenuItem inside it. Close it from code with ImGui::CloseCurrentPopup() inside the popup. Both calls must be made with the same ID stack : an OpenPopup inside a PushID(i) opens a popup that BeginPopup can only find inside the same PushID(i) . This is the most common popup bug, and a direct consequence of lesson 1.05. Context menus Right-click menus have shortcuts that do the opening for you: cpp-norun ImGui::Selectable(stone.name.c_str()); if (ImGui::BeginPopupContextItem()) // right-click on the item just drawn { if (ImGui::MenuItem("Rename")) startRename(stone); if (ImGui::MenuItem("Delete")) deleteStone(stone); ImGui::EndPopup(); } if (ImGui::BeginPopupContextWindow(nullptr, ImGuiPopupFlags_MouseButtonRight ImGuiPopupFlags_NoOpenOverItems)) { // right-click on empty space in the window if (ImGui::MenuItem("Add stone")) addStone(); ImGui::EndPopup(); } Modals A modal popup blocks interaction with everything behind it until it is closed, and dims the background. Use it for decisions that must be made before continuing: cpp-norun if (wantsToQuit && level.dirty) ImGui::OpenPopup("Unsaved changes"); ImGui::SetNextWindowPos(ImGui::GetMainViewport()- GetCenter(), ImGuiCond_Appearing, ImVec2(0.5f, 0.5f)); if (ImGui::BeginPopupModal("Unsaved changes", nullptr, ImGuiWindowFlags_AlwaysAutoResize)) { ImGui::Text("Save changes to %s before quitting?", level.name.c_str()); if (ImGui::Button("Save", ImVec2(100, 0))) { save(); quit(); ImGui::CloseCurrentPopup(); } ImGui::SameLine(); if (ImGui::Button("Don't save", ImVec2(100, 0))) { quit(); ImGui::CloseCurrentPopup(); } ImGui::SameLine(); if (ImGui::Button("Cancel", ImVec2(100, 0))) { wantsToQuit = false; ImGui::CloseCurrentPopup(); } ImGui::EndPopup(); } SetNextWindowPos with the pivot (0.5, 0.5) and ImGuiCond_Appearing centres the dialog each time it appears. Passing a bool as the second argument gives the modal a close button. The unsaved-changes flow "Quit", "New level" and "Open level" all have the same shape: if there are unsaved changes, ask first; then do the action only if the user saved or chose not to. A small state machine keeps it correct: remember the pending action , open the modal, and when a button is pressed run (or drop) the pending action. The practice builds it. Common mistakes !warning OpenPopup and BeginPopup under different ID stacks The popup is opened but never found. Call both at the same PushID level. !warning Calling OpenPopup every frame The popup reopens and resets constantly. Open it once, in response to an event. !warning Using a modal for information Modals interrupt. Use them for decisions only; show information in a tooltip or a log. Check yourself quiz ? Describe ImGui's popup model. - You call OpenPopup every frame while the popup should be visible, and BeginPopup draws it + A popup has an ID; OpenPopup marks it open once, and BeginPopup, called every frame, returns true and draws it while it is open - BeginPopup opens the popup and keeps it open until you call EndPopup - A popup is a separate window you create once and destroy with CloseCurrentPopup Opening is an event, drawing happens every frame. The popup closes on outside clicks, Escape, a Selectable or MenuItem inside it, or CloseCurrentPopup. ? What do BeginPopupContextItem and BeginPopupContextWindow do? - They open a popup when the item or window is hovered, then wait for a click inside it - They draw a tooltip next to the item or the window + They open and begin a popup when the item just drawn, or empty space in the window, is right-clicked They do the OpenPopup call for you on a right-click, then work like BeginPopup, so EndPopup still goes inside the if. ? How do you centre a modal each time it appears? - SetNextWindowPos at the viewport's centre with ImGuiCond_Always and the default pivot - SetNextWindowPos at the viewport's centre with ImGuiCond_Once - Pass ImGuiWindowFlags_AlwaysAutoResize to BeginPopupModal + SetNextWindowPos at the main viewport's centre, with pivot (0.5, 0.5) and ImGuiCond_Appearing The pivot puts the window's middle, not its corner, on the point, and ImGuiCond_Appearing applies it each time it opens while still letting the user move it. ? How often do you call OpenPopup and BeginPopup? - Both every frame + OpenPopup once when it should open; BeginPopup every frame - Both once, when the popup should open Calling OpenPopup every frame keeps reopening and resetting the popup; BeginPopup must run every frame to draw it. ? OpenPopup("menu") is called inside PushID(3), BeginPopup("menu") outside it. What happens? - It works normally, because both use the label "menu" - ImGui opens two popups + The popup never appears, because the IDs differ Popup IDs follow the ID stack, so both calls must be made at the same PushID level. ? When should you use a modal popup? - For every message the user should read, such as a log line - For hints shown when the mouse rests on a widget + For a decision needed before continuing, such as unsaved changes Modals block everything else until answered. Information belongs in a tooltip or a log.

title: The unsaved-changes dialog
body: "New level", "Open level" and "Quit" must all ask about unsaved changes first. Write the state machine behind the modal: cpp class Guard { public: explicit Guard(std::function<bool() save); // save returns false if saving failed void setDirty(bool dirty); void request(const std::string& action); // "new", "open" or "quit" bool dialogOpen() const; // should the modal be open this frame? void answer(const std::string& choice); // "save", "discard" or "cancel" std::vector<std::string done() const; // actions that went ahead, in order }; - request while not dirty : the action goes ahead at once (added to done ). - request while dirty: the action becomes pending and the dialog opens. A second request while the dialog is already open replaces the pending action. - answer("save") : call save . If it succeeds, the document is no longer dirty and the pending action goes ahead. If it fails, the dialog stays open and nothing happens. - answer("discard") : the pending action goes ahead; the document is treated as not dirty any more. - answer("cancel") : the pending action is dropped; still dirty. - Every answer except a failed save closes the dialog. Answers while the dialog is closed do nothing.

title: 4.03  Drag and Drop
body: Dragging an asset onto a slot, reordering a list, moving an object to another parent in a tree - ImGui's drag and drop works between any two items with a typed payload . This lesson covers sources, targets, payload types, reordering a list by dragging, and re-parenting in a tree without creating loops. Source and target Any item can be a drag source and any item a drop target . They talk through a payload : a small block of bytes with a type name. cpp-norun // The source: an asset in the browser ImGui::Selectable(asset.name.c_str()); if (ImGui::BeginDragDropSource()) { ImGui::SetDragDropPayload("ASSET", &asset.id, sizeof(asset.id)); // copied by ImGui ImGui::Text("%s", asset.name.c_str()); // drawn under the mouse while dragging ImGui::EndDragDropSource(); } // The target: a texture slot in the inspector ImGui::Button(material.texture.empty() ? "(drop a texture)" : material.texture.c_str(), ImVec2(-FLT_MIN, 0)); if (ImGui::BeginDragDropTarget()) { if (const ImGuiPayload p = ImGui::AcceptDragDropPayload("ASSET")) // non-null on the frame of the drop { const int id = static_cast<const int (p- Data); material.texture = assets.byId(id).name; } ImGui::EndDragDropTarget(); } Both Begin... functions follow the "End only if Begin returned true" rule. The type string (up to 32 characters) lets a target accept only what it understands: a texture slot accepts "ASSET" , ignores "ENTITY" . While dragging, matching targets highlight automatically. The payload is copied , so pass small, stable things: an id, an index, never a pointer to something that may move or be deleted during the drag. Reordering a list A list where each row is both a source and a target can be reordered by dragging: cpp-norun for (int i = 0; i < (int)layers.size(); ++i) { ImGui::PushID(i); ImGui::Selectable(layers i .name.c_str()); if (ImGui::BeginDragDropSource()) { ImGui::SetDragDropPayload("LAYER", &i, sizeof(i)); ImGui::Text("%s", layers i .name.c_str()); ImGui::EndDragDropSource(); } if (ImGui::BeginDragDropTarget()) { if (const ImGuiPayload p = ImGui::AcceptDragDropPayload("LAYER")) pendingMove = { static_cast<const int (p- Data), i }; // apply after the loop ImGui::EndDragDropTarget(); } ImGui::PopID(); } if (pendingMove) { moveItem(layers, pendingMove- from, pendingMove- to); pendingMove.reset(); } Apply the move after the loop: changing the vector while iterating over it would skip or repeat rows. "Move item from from to to " means: take the item out, and insert it so it ends up at index to . The practice writes moveItem . Re-parenting in a tree Dropping a tree node on another node makes it a child of that node. One rule protects the data: a node may not be dropped onto itself or onto any of its own descendants , which would make a loop (the node would become its own ancestor) and detach that whole branch from the tree. Check the ancestry before accepting: cpp-norun bool isAncestor(const Scene& s, int maybeAncestor, int node) // walk up the parent links ImGui can help the user too: AcceptDragDropPayload with ImGuiDragDropFlags_AcceptBeforeDelivery lets you peek at the payload while hovering and show a "not allowed" cursor or tooltip before the drop. The practice implements the re-parenting rule. Dragging from outside The Win32 back end does not deliver files dragged from Explorer as ImGui payloads. Handle WM_DROPFILES (after DragAcceptFiles(hwnd, TRUE) ) in your window procedure, and act on the files directly, for example importing them into the asset browser. Common mistakes !warning A pointer in the payload The data may move or be deleted during the drag. Use ids or indexes. !warning Changing a container while drawing it Record the move and apply it after the loop. !warning Allowing a node to become its own descendant Check ancestry before re-parenting, or part of the tree disappears into a loop. Check yourself quiz ? What does SetDragDropPayload do with the data you pass? + It copies the bytes, so pass values such as ids rather than pointers - It keeps a pointer to it, so the variable must stay alive until the drop - It moves it out of your variable, leaving the variable empty The copy stays valid even if the source changes. A copied pointer still points at the original object, which is why you pass ids or indexes. ? When does AcceptDragDropPayload return non-null? - Every frame the mouse is over the target while something is being dragged + On the frame the mouse button is released over the target with a payload of the accepted type - On the frame the drag starts, if the payload type matches Without extra flags it only delivers on the drop. ImGuiDragDropFlags_AcceptBeforeDelivery lets you peek while hovering. ? What check must re-parenting by drag and drop make? - That the new parent has no children yet - That the dragged node is a leaf - That the new parent is not the dragged node's current parent + That the new parent is not the dragged node itself or any of its descendants Otherwise the node becomes its own ancestor, a loop that detaches the whole branch from the tree. ? What is a drag-and-drop payload's type string for? - To choose the cursor shown while dragging + So a target only accepts payloads it understands - To name the tooltip drawn under the mouse A texture slot accepts "ASSET" and ignores "ENTITY", and only matching targets highlight while dragging. ? Why apply a list reorder after the loop that draws the list? - ImGui only allows drops to be handled at the end of the frame - It is faster to move items outside the loop + Changing the vector while iterating over it skips or repeats items Record the move during the loop, then apply it once the loop is done. ? Node A is the parent of B, and B the parent of C. Can A be dropped onto C? - Yes, any node can be dropped onto any other node - Only if C has no children + No; A would become a descendant of itself C is A's descendant, so making C A's parent creates a loop.

title: Move an item in a list
match: Move an item in a list
body: Dragging a row of a reorderable list onto another row moves it there. Write cpp template <typename T void moveItem(std::vector<T & items, int from, int to); Take the item at from out and insert it so that it ends up at index to (counted in the final list). Indexes outside the list, or from == to , change nothing. { A, B, C, D, E }, from 1 to 3 - { A, C, D, B, E } { A, B, C, D, E }, from 4 to 0 - { E, A, B, C, D }

title: Re-parent without loops
body: Dropping a scene object onto another in the tree makes it a child of that object. Write cpp bool isAncestor(const std::map<int, int & parentOf, int ancestor, int node); bool reparent(std::map<int, int & parentOf, int node, int newParent); parentOf maps every object to its parent; roots map to -1 . - isAncestor(a, n) : is a the parent of n , or its parent's parent, and so on up to the root? An object is not its own ancestor. - reparent(node, newParent) : refuse (return false , change nothing) if newParent is node itself or a descendant of node , or if either is not in the map (except newParent == -1 , which makes node a root). Otherwise set the parent and return true .

title: 4.04  Docking and Multiple Viewports
body: With the docking branch, windows snap into each other as tabs and splits - the layout of every modern editor - and with multiple viewports they can leave the main window and become real operating-system windows. This lesson turns both on, builds a dockspace over the whole screen, creates a default layout from code, and explains how dock nodes split space. Turning it on Docking lives on Dear ImGui's docking branch (lesson 1.02). Enable it once after creating the context: cpp-norun ImGuiIO& io = ImGui::GetIO(); io.ConfigFlags = ImGuiConfigFlags_DockingEnable; io.ConfigFlags = ImGuiConfigFlags_ViewportsEnable; // optional: windows may leave the main window Now drag any window by its title bar onto another: a docking overlay appears with targets for "as a tab", "split left", "split right", "split top", "split bottom". Hold Shift while dragging to dock only when you want to (set io.ConfigDockingWithShift = true ). A dockspace over the whole screen Editors fill the application window with one big dockspace that other windows dock into: cpp-norun ImGui::NewFrame(); ImGui::DockSpaceOverViewport(0, ImGui::GetMainViewport(), ImGuiDockNodeFlags_PassthruCentralNode); drawMenuBar(); // a main menu bar sits above the dockspace drawSceneWindow(); drawInspector(); drawLog(); ImGuiDockNodeFlags_PassthruCentralNode leaves the empty central area transparent, so your 3D scene drawn behind ImGui shows through it and receives clicks there. How docking splits space A dockspace is a tree of dock nodes . Each node is either a leaf , holding one or more windows as tabs, or a split , holding two child nodes side by side (horizontal) or one above the other (vertical) with a ratio : root (split left/right, ratio 0.2) ├── left: Scene tree 20% of the width └── right (split top/bottom, ratio 0.75) ├── top: Viewport Game tabs, 75% of the height └── bottom: Log Profiler tabs, 25% Every node's rectangle is computed from its parent's: the first child gets ratio of the size along the split axis, the second gets the rest. The practice computes these rectangles, which is exactly the arithmetic ImGui does every frame. A default layout from code The first time a user opens your editor, it should not be a pile of floating windows. The DockBuilder API (in imgui_internal.h ) builds a layout: cpp-norun include "imgui_internal.h" void buildDefaultLayout(ImGuiID dockspace) { ImGui::DockBuilderRemoveNode(dockspace); ImGui::DockBuilderAddNode(dockspace, ImGuiDockNodeFlags_DockSpace); ImGui::DockBuilderSetNodeSize(dockspace, ImGui::GetMainViewport()- Size); ImGuiID left, right; ImGui::DockBuilderSplitNode(dockspace, ImGuiDir_Left, 0.2f, &left, &right); ImGuiID bottom, centre; ImGui::DockBuilderSplitNode(right, ImGuiDir_Down, 0.25f, &bottom, &centre); ImGui::DockBuilderDockWindow("Scene", left); ImGui::DockBuilderDockWindow("Viewport", centre); ImGui::DockBuilderDockWindow("Log", bottom); ImGui::DockBuilderFinish(dockspace); } Call it when the dockspace has no saved layout yet ( ImGui::DockBuilderGetNode(id) == nullptr before the first DockSpace call), and from a "Reset layout" menu item. After that, imgui.ini remembers whatever the user arranged (lesson 4.06). Multiple viewports With ViewportsEnable , dragging a window outside the application window turns it into a real operating-system window, so tools can spread over several monitors. Your loop needs two more calls after rendering the main window: cpp-norun ImGui::Render(); ImGui_ImplDX11_RenderDrawData(ImGui::GetDrawData()); if (io.ConfigFlags & ImGuiConfigFlags_ViewportsEnable) { ImGui::UpdatePlatformWindows(); // create, move, resize OS windows ImGui::RenderPlatformWindowsDefault(); // render and present each one } g_swapChain- Present(1, 0); Coordinates then become desktop coordinates rather than window coordinates, which matters if you place windows yourself: use ImGui::GetMainViewport()- Pos as the origin. Common mistakes !warning Using docking functions on the master branch They do not exist there. Use the docking branch, as most tools do. !warning Rebuilding the default layout every frame The user's arrangement is wiped every frame. Build it only when there is none, or on request. Check yourself quiz ? What two config flags turn on docking and multiple viewports? - ImGuiConfigFlags_DockingEnable and ImGuiConfigFlags_NavEnableKeyboard - ImGuiDockNodeFlags_DockSpace and ImGuiDockNodeFlags_PassthruCentralNode + ImGuiConfigFlags_DockingEnable and ImGuiConfigFlags_ViewportsEnable Both go into io.ConfigFlags once after creating the context, on the docking branch. The ImGuiDockNodeFlags are for individual dock nodes. ? What extra calls does the loop need with multiple viewports? + ImGui::UpdatePlatformWindows and ImGui::RenderPlatformWindowsDefault after rendering the main window - A second ImGui::NewFrame and ImGui::Render for each extra window - ImGui::DockSpaceOverViewport once for each monitor - None; the back end creates and draws the extra windows by itself The first creates, moves and resizes the OS windows; the second renders and presents each one. ? How do you give first-time users a sensible layout? - Call the DockBuilder functions every frame, so the layout is always correct - Ship an imgui.ini next to the executable and tell users not to move windows + Build it with the DockBuilder API when the dockspace has no saved layout, and offer it again from a reset menu item Rebuilding it every frame would wipe whatever the user arranged; after the first run, imgui.ini remembers their layout. ? What is a dock node? - A separate operating-system window created by the viewports feature + Either a leaf holding windows as tabs, or a split holding two child nodes with a ratio - A single docked window together with its tab A dockspace is a tree of dock nodes, and the splits divide the space. ? A split node 1000 pixels wide is split left/right with ratio 0.2. How wide is the left child? - 800 pixels - 20 pixels + 200 pixels - 500 pixels The first child gets ratio times the size along the split axis: 0.2 x 1000 = 200. The second child gets the remaining 800. ? What does ImGuiDockNodeFlags_PassthruCentralNode do? - Docks every new window into the central node automatically - Hides the tab bars of all windows docked in the dockspace + Keeps the empty centre see-through so the scene shows and gets clicks Editors draw their 3D view behind ImGui, visible through that empty central area.

title: Where each dock node goes
body: A dockspace is a tree of nodes. Compute every leaf's rectangle, as ImGui does each frame: cpp struct Rect { float x, y, w, h; }; struct DockNode { std::string name; // for a leaf: the window docked there; for a split: unused char split{ 0 }; // 0 for a leaf; 'x' = left/right, 'y' = top/bottom float ratio{ 0.5f }; // share of the first child along the split axis std::vector<DockNode children; // exactly 2 for a split }; std::vector<std::pair<std::string, Rect layout(const DockNode& root, const Rect& area, float splitterSize); - A leaf takes its whole rectangle. - A split 'x' gives the first child the left part and the second the right part; 'y' gives the first the top and the second the bottom. - Between the two children is a splitter of splitterSize pixels. The space shared out is size along the axis - splitterSize : the first child gets ratio of it (rounded down to a whole pixel with floor ), the second gets the rest. - Return every leaf, depth first, first child before second, with its rectangle. root: split x, ratio 0.2, children leaf "Scene", split y ratio 0.75 leaf "Viewport", leaf "Log" area {0, 0, 1004, 704}, splitter 4 Scene {0, 0, 200, 704} Viewport {204, 0, 800, 525} Log {204, 529, 800, 175}

title: 4.05  Styling, Fonts and Icons
body: The default look is fine for debug views, but a tool people use all day deserves care. This lesson covers the style object, colours and sizes, temporary style changes with Push/Pop, loading fonts at the right size for the display's scale, and merging an icon font so buttons can show symbols. The style All sizes and colours live in one ImGuiStyle : cpp-norun ImGuiStyle& style = ImGui::GetStyle(); ImGui::StyleColorsDark(); // start from a built-in theme: Dark, Light or Classic style.WindowRounding = 4.0f; style.FrameRounding = 3.0f; style.FramePadding = ImVec2(8, 5); style.ItemSpacing = ImVec2(8, 6); style.ScrollbarSize = 12.0f; style.Colors ImGuiCol_WindowBg = ImVec4(0.09f, 0.10f, 0.12f, 1.0f); style.Colors ImGuiCol_Header = ImVec4(0.95f, 0.70f, 0.27f, 0.35f); style.Colors ImGuiCol_HeaderHovered = ImVec4(0.95f, 0.70f, 0.27f, 0.55f); There are about 55 colours ( ImGuiCol_Text , Button , ButtonHovered , ButtonActive , FrameBg , CheckMark , SliderGrab ...) and dozens of sizes. Tune them live with the style editor (lesson 1.06), then press "Export" to copy the code. A good theme usually comes from a small palette: a background, a slightly lighter panel, an accent, and the same accent at three strengths for normal, hovered and active. The practice generates such a theme from one accent colour. Temporary changes cpp-norun ImGui::PushStyleColor(ImGuiCol_Button, ImVec4(0.8f, 0.2f, 0.2f, 1.0f)); ImGui::PushStyleVar(ImGuiStyleVar_FrameRounding, 8.0f); if (ImGui::Button("Delete level")) confirmDelete(); ImGui::PopStyleVar(); ImGui::PopStyleColor(); Every Push needs a Pop (with a count: PopStyleColor(2) pops two). Scaling for the display On a 4K laptop at 200% scale, a 13-pixel font is unreadable. Get the window's scale and apply it to both the font size and the style: cpp-norun const float scale = ImGui_ImplWin32_GetDpiScaleForHwnd(hwnd); // 1.0 at 96 DPI, 1.5 at 144, 2.0 at 192 style.ScaleAllSizes(scale); // paddings, roundings, spacing io.Fonts- AddFontFromFileTTF("fonts/Inter-Regular.ttf", 15.0f scale); Load the font at the real size rather than scaling a small font up, which looks blurry. (ImGui 1.92 added dynamic font sizes, which handles much of this for you; the idea is the same.) Fonts cpp-norun ImFont body = io.Fonts- AddFontFromFileTTF("fonts/Inter-Regular.ttf", 16.0f); ImFont mono = io.Fonts- AddFontFromFileTTF("fonts/JetBrainsMono-Regular.ttf", 15.0f); // ... ImGui::PushFont(mono); ImGui::TextUnformatted(logText); ImGui::PopFont(); The first font added becomes the default. Fonts are rasterised into the font atlas texture (lesson 1.03) when the back end builds it; add them before the first NewFrame . Icon fonts Icon fonts such as Font Awesome or Material Symbols put pictures in Unicode's "private use" area. Merge one into your text font so a single label can mix words and icons: cpp-norun io.Fonts- AddFontFromFileTTF("fonts/Inter-Regular.ttf", 16.0f); ImFontConfig config; config.MergeMode = true; // add these glyphs to the previous font config.GlyphMinAdvanceX = 16.0f; // icons all the same width static const ImWchar iconRange = { 0xE000, 0xF8FF, 0 }; // the private use area io.Fonts- AddFontFromFileTTF("fonts/fa-solid-900.ttf", 14.0f, &config, iconRange); ImGui::Button("\xef\x83\x87 Save"); // U+F0C7 (a floppy disk in Font Awesome) as UTF-8 ImGui strings are UTF-8 . A code point above U+007F is written as two to four bytes; U+F0C7 becomes EF 83 87 . Projects usually use a header with named constants ( ICON_FA_FLOPPY_DISK ) generated for the icon font. The practice has you write the UTF-8 encoder. Common mistakes !warning Scaling a small font up instead of loading it at the right size The text is blurry. Load fonts at the size they will be drawn. !warning Mismatched Push and Pop counts ImGui asserts at the end of the frame. Pop as many as you pushed. !warning Writing non-ASCII text in a source file without UTF-8 Save source files as UTF-8 (and compile with /utf-8) or write the bytes as escapes. Check yourself quiz ? How do you change a style value for just one widget? - Change ImGui::GetStyle() before the widget; ImGui restores it at the end of the frame + PushStyleColor or PushStyleVar before it and the matching Pop after it - Pass the colour as an extra argument to the widget function The Push/Pop pair limits the change to what is drawn in between; changing the style object directly changes it for everything until you change it back. ? How should a tool handle a 200% display scale? - Load the font at its normal size and scale the whole ImGui window up by two - Call ScaleAllSizes(2.0f) only; it scales the fonts too - Set every font to twice its size and leave the style alone + Multiply the style sizes with ScaleAllSizes and load fonts at the scaled pixel size ScaleAllSizes covers paddings, spacing and roundings but not fonts, and a small font scaled up looks blurry, so load fonts at the real size. ? Why are ImGui labels UTF-8, and what does that mean for icons? - ImGui reads strings as UTF-16, so icons are written as wchar_t literals + ImGui reads strings as UTF-8, so icons are written as their UTF-8 byte sequences - ImGui reads strings as ASCII, so icons need their own IconText function Icon code points sit in the private use area: U+F0C7, for example, is written as the three bytes EF 83 87 . A header of named constants usually does this for you. ? What does style.ScaleAllSizes(2.0f) change? - Only the font size, leaving paddings and spacings alone + Paddings, spacings, roundings and other sizes, but not the font - Every size including the font, which it reloads at 2x Load the font at the scaled size separately. ? Why merge an icon font into the text font? - To make the font atlas smaller - Because icon fonts cannot be loaded on their own + So one string can mix words and icons without switching fonts MergeMode adds the icon glyphs to the previously added font, so "\xef\x83\x87 Save" draws an icon and a word. ? How many bytes does the code point U+F0C7 take in UTF-8? - Two - Four + Three Code points from U+0800 to U+FFFF use three bytes; four bytes start at U+10000.

title: UTF-8 for icons
body: ImGui labels are UTF-8. To put an icon's code point into a label, encode it. Write cpp std::string utf8(char32_t codePoint); std::vector<char32_t decodeUtf8(const std::string& text); utf8 encodes one code point: Code point Bytes --- --- U+0000 to U+007F 0xxxxxxx U+0080 to U+07FF 110xxxxx 10xxxxxx U+0800 to U+FFFF 1110xxxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx U+10000 to U+10FFFF 11110xxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx The x bits are the code point's bits, highest first. Surrogates (U+D800 to U+DFFF) and anything above U+10FFFF are not valid: encode them as U+FFFD (the replacement character) instead. decodeUtf8 turns a string back into code points. A byte that does not start a valid sequence (or a sequence cut short) decodes as U+FFFD and decoding continues with the next byte. utf8(U'A') == "A" utf8(0xF0C7) == "\xEF\x83\x87" (Font Awesome's floppy disk)

title: A theme from one colour
body: A good theme uses one accent colour at three strengths. Write cpp struct Color { float r, g, b, a; }; Color withAlpha(Color c, float a); Color lighten(Color c, float amount); // move each channel towards 1 by amount (0..1) Color darken(Color c, float amount); // move each channel towards 0 by amount (0..1) std::vector<Color accentStates(Color accent); // { normal, hovered, active } - lighten(c, t) : each of r, g, b becomes x + (1 - x) t ; darken(c, t) : x (1 - t) . Alpha is unchanged. - accentStates : normal is the accent at alpha 0.40; hovered is the accent at alpha 0.60; active is the accent lightened by 0.15 at alpha 1.0.

title: 4.06  Saving Settings and Layouts
body:
ImGui saves window positions, sizes, docking and table layouts to imgui.ini by itself. This lesson explains that file, how to move it, how to store your own tool's settings in the same file with a settings handler , and how to save and restore named layouts. imgui.ini By default ImGui writes imgui.ini in the working directory a few seconds after something changes, and reads it at start-up: ini Window Stones Pos=60,40 Size=320,260 Collapsed=0 DockId=0x00000002,0 Table 0x8A4C2B11,4 Column 0 Weight=1.0000 Visible=1 Order=0 Sort=0v Column 1 Width=60 Visible=1 Order=1 Docking Data DockSpace ID=0x3BC79352 Window=0x4647B76E Pos=0,19 Size=1280,701 Split=X DockNode ID=0x00000001 Parent=0x3BC79352 SizeRef=256,701 Selected=0x8B1D2D3A DockNode ID=0x00000002 Parent=0x3BC79352 SizeRef=1022,701 CentralNode=1 It is a simple text format: Type Name section headers, then Key=Value lines. Where it goes The working directory is a bad place: it changes with how the program is started. Put it in the user's settings folder: cpp-norun static std::string iniPath = settingsFolder() + "\xenon_editor_imgui.ini"; // e.g. under %APPDATA% io.IniFilename = iniPath.c_str(); // the string must outlive ImGui: keep it static or global io.IniSavingRate = 2.0f; // seconds of quiet before saving Set io.IniFilename = nullptr to turn saving off, and save or load yourself with ImGui::SaveIniSettingsToMemory() and ImGui::LoadIniSettingsFromMemory(text) , for example to keep the layout inside your own project file. Your own settings in the same file A settings handler lets your tool save its own data as more sections of imgui.ini , so window layout and tool settings live and load together: cpp-norun ImGuiSettingsHandler handler; handler.TypeName = "XenonEditor"; handler.TypeHash = ImHashStr("XenonEditor"); handler.ReadOpenFn = (ImGuiContext , ImGuiSettingsHandler , const char name) - void { return std::strcmp(name, "Options") == 0 ? &g_options : nullptr; // which object receives the lines }; handler.ReadLineFn = (ImGuiContext , ImGuiSettingsHandler , void entry, const char line) { auto o = static_cast<Options (entry); int v; if (std::sscanf(line, "GridSize=%d", &v) == 1) o- gridSize = v; else if (std::sscanf(line, "Snap=%d", &v) == 1) o- snap = v != 0; }; handler.WriteAllFn = (ImGuiContext , ImGuiSettingsHandler h, ImGuiTextBuffer out) { out- appendf(" %s Options 
", h- TypeName); out- appendf("GridSize=%d
Snap=%d

", g_options.gridSize, g_options.snap ? 1 : 0); }; ImGui::AddSettingsHandler(&handler); // before the first NewFrame (the ini is read then) When your settings change, call ImGui::MarkIniSettingsDirty() so ImGui saves soon. Because the format is so simple, reading and writing it yourself is easy too. The practice writes a small reader that turns the file into sections of key-value pairs, and a writer that puts them back, keeping sections it does not understand untouched. Named layouts Editors often let users save layouts by name: "Level design", "Animation", "Debugging". With SaveIniSettingsToMemory and LoadIniSettingsFromMemory , a layout is just a string: cpp-norun layouts "Animation" = ImGui::SaveIniSettingsToMemory(); // save the current arrangement ImGui::LoadIniSettingsFromMemory(layouts "Animation" .c_str()); // switch to it (at the start of a frame) Common mistakes !warning A temporary string for io.IniFilename ImGui keeps the pointer. A temporary dies and ImGui reads freed memory. Keep it in a static or global. !warning Adding a settings handler after the first frame The ini file has already been read, so your section is ignored. Add handlers before the first NewFrame. Check yourself quiz ? Describe the format of imgui.ini. - A JSON object with one key per window and its settings + Type Name section headers, each followed by Key=Value lines - A binary file that only ImGui itself can read back - One line per window, holding its position and size separated by commas Sections cover windows, tables, docking and any custom handlers. It is a simple text format, which is why a custom settings handler can add its own sections. ? What must be true of the string assigned to io.IniFilename ? - It must be an absolute path, or ImGui refuses to save - It may be a temporary, because ImGui copies it when you assign it + It must stay valid for as long as ImGui uses it, because ImGui stores only the pointer A temporary std::string 's c_str() dies at the end of the statement and ImGui would read freed memory, so keep the string static or global. ? When must custom settings handlers be added? + Before the first NewFrame , because that is when the ini file is read - At any time; ImGui reads the ini file again when a handler is added - After the first frame, once the ini file has been loaded Added later, the ini file has already been read and your section is ignored. ? Why should imgui.ini not stay in the working directory? - ImGui cannot write files in the working directory + The working directory depends on how the program is started, so settings appear lost - Saving there is slower than saving in the user's folder Started from Visual Studio, a shortcut or a terminal, the program can get different working directories.
