body: Problem Usual cause Fix Lesson --- --- --- --- Reading a child's output never finishes the parent still holds the pipe's write end close your copy right after CreateProcessW 1.04 Parent and child both hang both blocked writing to full pipes read each output pipe on its own thread or with overlapped I/O 1.04 A child keeps a file or pipe open unexpectedly it inherited every inheritable handle use PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST 1.02 Helper processes survive the main program not in a kill-on-close job add them to a job with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE 1.03 Messages arrive merged or cut in half a byte stream has no boundaries frame messages with a length prefix 2.03 Client gets ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND the server is not running, or a different pipe name start the server; compare names 2.02 Client gets ERROR_PIPE_BUSY every instance is in use WaitNamedPipeW and retry; create more instances 2.04 Memory corruption with overlapped I/O the OVERLAPPED or buffer went out of scope while pending keep them alive until completion 2.05 Shared data is garbage in the other process a pointer or std::string was stored in shared memory store offsets and fixed-size data 3.02 A reader sees half-updated state torn read seqlock or double buffering 3.05 CreateMutexW fails with ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE another kind of object already has that name use distinct names 4.01 A consumer sleeps although data is waiting lost wakeup; event reset after the data arrived drain all work after each wake; time out waits 4.02 A wait returns WAIT_ABANDONED the mutex's owner died while holding it validate or repair the shared data 4.03 WM_COPYDATA never arrives the receiver runs elevated (UIPI) ChangeWindowMessageFilterEx in the receiver, or use a pipe 4.04 Two processes hang waiting for each other lock-order or request-reply deadlock global lock order; no locks held across IPC; timeouts 4.05 Firewall prompt when the app starts the server bound to 0.0.0.0 bind to 127.0.0.1 5.01 A web page can trigger your local API localhost has no access control token, Host and Origin checks 5.05 A worker restarts hundreds of times no backoff on a crash loop exponential backoff and give up 6.02

title: Glossary
body: Abandoned mutex : a mutex whose owning thread ended while holding it; the next wait returns WAIT_ABANDONED . (4.03) Anonymous pipe : an unnamed one-way pipe, shared by inheritance or duplication. (2.01) Auto-reset event : an event that resets itself when it releases one waiter. (4.02) Backoff : waiting longer after each failure before retrying. (6.02) Correlation id : a number in a request that its response carries back. (5.04) Deadlock : processes or threads each waiting for something another of them holds. (4.05) Envelope : the common outer structure of every message in a protocol. (5.02) Environment block : a child's environment variables as NAME=value strings ending in zeros. (1.02) Event (kernel) : a kernel object that is set or reset, used to signal. (4.02) Exit code : the number a process leaves when it ends. (1.03) File mapping : a kernel object that maps the same memory into several processes. (3.01) Framing : marking where each message begins and ends in a byte stream. (2.03) Handshake : the first exchange of a connection, agreeing on protocol and version. (5.02) Heartbeat : a regular "still alive" signal from a worker. (6.02) Idempotent : safe to perform twice with the same effect as once. (5.04) Instance (pipe) : one connection slot of a named pipe. (2.02) I/O completion port : a queue collecting completions of overlapped operations. (2.05) Job object : a group of processes managed and limited together. (1.03) Manual-reset event : an event that stays set until explicitly reset. (4.02) Message mode : a named pipe mode where each write is one message. (2.02) Named pipe : a pipe any process can open by name. (2.02) Overlapped I/O : starting an operation that completes later, without blocking. (2.05) Pipe squatting : creating another program's pipe name first to intercept its clients. (5.05) Ring buffer : a fixed array used as a circular queue. (3.03) Semaphore : a kernel object with a count, allowing up to N at once. (4.03) Seqlock : a sequence counter that lets readers detect concurrent writes and retry. (3.05) Single-instance application : a program whose later launches hand their work to the running copy. (6.01) Supervisor : a process that starts, watches and restarts workers. (6.02) Tag-length-value : a field encoding that lets readers skip unknown fields. (5.03) Torn read : reading part of an old state and part of a new one. (3.05) UIPI : User Interface Privilege Isolation, blocking messages to higher-integrity windows. (4.04) Varint : a variable-length integer encoding using 7 bits per byte. (5.03) WM_COPYDATA : the window message that copies a block of data to another process. (4.04)

title: 1.01  Java and the JDK: Your First Program
match: 1.01 Java and the JDK: Your First Program
body: What Java is and how it runs - source code, the compiler, bytecode and the JVM - installing the JDK, the shape of a Java program with a class and a main method, printing with System.out, comments, compiling and running from the command line, and reading compiler errors. Java Java is one of the most widely used programming languages: university courses, Android apps, banking and business systems, big-data tools and many game servers are written in it. It is statically typed (every variable has a fixed type, checked before the program runs) and object-oriented (programs are built from classes and objects, milestone 3). How Java runs The compiler javac turns your source code into bytecode : instructions for the Java Virtual Machine (JVM), not for any real processor. The JVM runs that bytecode on whatever computer it is installed on, compiling the busiest parts to fast machine code while the program runs. That is Java's motto: write once, run anywhere . The JDK (Java Development Kit) contains the compiler, the JVM and the standard library. Install a current LTS version (Java 21 or 25) from adoptium.net or oracle.com. The practice editor here compiles and runs your code on Java 25 for you. Your first program java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { System.out.println("Hello, Xenon!"); System.out.println(2 + 3); } } Every part matters: - public class Main declares a class named Main . All Java code lives inside classes. A public class must be in a file with the same name: Main.java . - public static void main(String args) is the main method , where the program starts. args holds any command-line arguments. - System.out.println(...) prints a line. System.out.print(...) prints without moving to a new line. - Statements end with ; , and braces { } group code into blocks. - Java is case-sensitive : system.out.println does not exist. Compiling and running bash javac Main.java creates Main.class java Main runs it (class name, without .class) java Main.java since Java 11: compile and run a single file in one step IDEs such as IntelliJ IDEA, VS Code with the Java extensions, and Eclipse do this for you with a Run button, and underline errors as you type. Java 25 also accepts a shorter form for small programs, with no class written out: java-norun void main() { IO.println("Hello from a compact source file"); } This course uses the full form, which every Java version and every course you will meet uses. Comments java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { // A comment to the end of the line. / A comment that can span lines. / System.out.println("Comments are ignored by the compiler."); } / A Javadoc comment: tools turn these into documentation pages. / static void documented() { } } Compiler errors The compiler checks the whole program before it runs. An error names the file, line and problem: text Main.java:3: error: ';' expected System.out.println("Hello") ^ Main.java:4: error: cannot find symbol System.out.printn("Hi"); ^ symbol: method printn(String) Fix the first error first: the others are often caused by it. "cannot find symbol" almost always means a typo or a missing import. Check yourself quiz ? What does javac produce, and what runs it? - Machine code for your processor, which the operating system runs directly - A .exe file that only runs on the computer it was compiled on + Bytecode in .class files, which the Java Virtual Machine (JVM) runs - Bytecode in .java files, which the compiler then runs javac turns source code into bytecode in .class files: instructions for the JVM, not for any real processor, which is why the same file runs on any system. ? What must the file containing public class Greeter be called? + Greeter.java - greeter.java - Main.java - Greeter.class A public class must be in a file with exactly its name plus .java . Java is case-sensitive, so greeter.java does not match, and Greeter.class is what the compiler produces. ? Which line starts a Java program? - public class Main { - System.out.println("start"); - import java.util.Scanner; + public static void main(String args) { The JVM starts by calling the main method. The class only holds it.

title: Input and output
where: 1.01 Java and the JDK: Your First Program
body: Write a program that asks for a name and a birth year with a Scanner , then greets the person and says how old they turn in 2026: Name? Ada Birth year? 1990 Hello, Ada! In 2026 you turn 36. The prompts are printed with System.out.print (no line break). The starter already reads the answers for you: name holds the name and year the birth year as a number ( Scanner , variables and Integer.parseInt are explained in lessons 1.02 to 1.04). Your job is the output: add the print statements where the comments say.

title: 1.02  Variables and Primitive Types
body: Declaring and assigning variables, the eight primitive types and their ranges, literals, var, constants with final, primitive versus reference types, widening and narrowing conversions with casts, integer overflow, and naming conventions. Variables A variable is a named place that holds a value of one type , fixed when it is declared: java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { int count = 3; double price = 2.50; boolean done = false; char grade = 'A'; // one character, in single quotes String name = "Ada"; // text, in double quotes (a class, not a primitive) count = count + 1; // fine: still an int // count = "four"; // error: incompatible types: String cannot be converted to int var total = count price; // var: the compiler infers double final int MAX_PLAYERS = 4; // final: cannot be assigned again System.out.println(name + ": " + count + " x " + price + " = " + total + ", max " + MAX_PLAYERS + ", " + grade + " " + done); } } A local variable must be assigned before it is read; reading an unassigned one is a compile error ("variable might not have been initialized"). The primitive types Type Size Range / precision Literal --- --- --- --- byte 8 bits -128 to 127 (byte) 10 short 16 bits -32 768 to 32 767 (short) 10 int 32 bits about ±2.1 billion 42 , 1_000_000 , 0xFF long 64 bits about ±9.2 × 10¹⁸ 42L float 32 bits about 7 digits 3.14f double 64 bits about 15 digits 3.14 , 1e-9 char 16 bits one UTF-16 character 'a' , '\n' boolean true or false true Use int for whole numbers, long when they may exceed two billion (milliseconds, file sizes, populations), double for measurements, and boolean for yes/no. For money, use long cents or java.math.BigDecimal : double cannot store 0.1 exactly. java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { System.out.println(0.1 + 0.2); // 0.30000000000000004 System.out.println(Integer.MAX_VALUE); int big = Integer.MAX_VALUE; big = big + 1; // overflows silently System.out.println(big); // -2147483648 System.out.println(Math.addExact(5, 6)); // throws ArithmeticException on overflow instead long population = 8_100_000_000L; // too big for int: needs long and the L suffix System.out.println(population); } } Primitive and reference types The eight primitives hold their value directly. Every other type (String, arrays, your own classes) is a reference type : the variable holds a reference to an object. Assigning a reference copies the reference, so both variables see the same object: java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { int a = 1; int b = a; // a copy of the value b = 2; System.out.println(a); // 1 int x = {1, 2, 3}; int y = x; // the same array y 0 = 99; System.out.println(x 0 ); // 99 } } A reference variable can also be null : no object at all. Using it then throws a NullPointerException . Conversions Converting to a wider type is automatic (no information can be lost); converting to a narrower type needs a cast and may lose information: java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { int i = 42; long l = i; // widening: automatic double d = i; // widening: automatic int back = (int) 3.99; // narrowing: cast, cuts off to 3 byte small = (byte) 300; // wraps around: 44 char c = (char) ('a' + 1); int code = 'A'; // a char is a number: 65 System.out.println(l + " " + d + " " + back + " " + small + " " + c + " " + code); System.out.println(Integer.parseInt("123") + 1); // text to number System.out.println(Double.parseDouble("2.5") 2); System.out.println(String.valueOf(42) + "!"); // number to text } } Names Java naming conventions: camelCase for variables and methods ( totalPrice ), PascalCase for classes ( ShoppingCart ), and UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for constants ( MAX_PLAYERS ). Choose names that say what a value means: secondsElapsed , not s . Check yourself quiz ? Why does long population = 8100000000; not compile? - A long cannot hold numbers above about 2.1 billion + The number is an int literal and too big for int ; write 8_100_000_000L - Large numbers must be written with underscores, like 8_100_000_000 - A long variable must be declared with var when its value is large A whole number with no suffix is an int literal, and 8 100 000 000 does not fit in an int even though it fits in a long. The L suffix makes it a long literal; underscores only help readability. ? What is (int) 7.9 ? - 8 + 7 - 7.9 - A compile error: a double cannot become an int Casting a double to int cuts off the fraction; it does not round. The cast is exactly what makes this narrowing conversion allowed. ? What does int x = Integer.MAX_VALUE; x = x + 1; leave in x ? - Integer.MAX_VALUE - An ArithmeticException at run time - 2147483648 + Integer.MIN_VALUE , -2147483648 int arithmetic wraps around silently on overflow; 2147483648 does not fit in an int. Math.addExact throws an exception instead.

title: Types and conversions
body: Complete the static methods in Solution : java static double toCelsius(double fahrenheit) // (F - 32) 5 / 9 static double average(int a, int b, int c) // the exact average: average(1, 2, 2) is 1.666... static int parseOrDefault(String text, int fallback) // the whole number in text (spaces around allowed), or fallback static long toCents(double euros) // euros as whole cents, rounded: 19.99 gives 1999, 0.29 gives 29

title: 1.03  Operators and Math
body: Arithmetic with integer division and remainder, compound assignment and increment, comparison and logical operators with short-circuiting, the ternary operator, precedence, the Math class, and comparing doubles safely. Arithmetic java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { int a = 17, b = 5; System.out.println(a + b); // 22 System.out.println(a - b); // 12 System.out.println(a b); // 85 System.out.println(a / b); // 3: int / int is integer division System.out.println(a % b); // 2: the remainder System.out.println(a / 5.0); // 3.4: a double operand makes it a double division System.out.println((double) a / b); System.out.println(-17 / 5); // -3: rounds toward zero System.out.println(-17 % 5); // -2: the sign follows the left side System.out.println(Math.floorMod(-17, 5)); // 3: always 0 to 4 } } minutes / 60 and minutes % 60 split minutes into hours and the rest. n % 2 == 0 tests for even numbers. Integer division by zero throws ArithmeticException ; double division by zero gives Infinity or NaN . Watch out for + with strings: once a String is involved, + joins text. "Total: " + 2 + 3 is "Total: 23" ; write "Total: " + (2 + 3) . Assignment shortcuts java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { int score = 10; score += 5; // 15 score = 2; // 30 score -= 1; // 29 score++; // 30 score--; // 29 System.out.println(score); int i = 5; System.out.println(i++); // prints 5, then i becomes 6 System.out.println(++i); // i becomes 7, then prints 7 } } Comparisons and logic Operator Meaning --- --- == , != Equal, not equal (for primitives) < , <= , , = Ordering && And (short-circuit) \ \ Or (short-circuit) ! Not java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { int age = 20; boolean hasTicket = true; boolean canEnter = age = 18 && hasTicket; boolean discount = age < 12 age = 65; System.out.println(canEnter + " " + discount + " " + !canEnter); String name = null; if (name != null && name.length() 3) System.out.println("long name"); // safe: && stops early System.out.println(age = 18 ? "adult" : "minor"); // the ternary operator } } && and short-circuit : the right side is only evaluated when needed, which makes the null check above safe. Conditions must be boolean : if (count) does not compile in Java. For objects, == compares references (is it the same object?), not contents. Strings are compared with equals (lesson 1.04). Precedence , / , % before + , - ; then comparisons; then && ; then ; then ?: ; then assignment. Use parentheses when in doubt. Math java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { System.out.println(Math.sqrt(16)); // 4.0 System.out.println(Math.pow(2, 10)); // 1024.0 System.out.println(Math.abs(-3.5)); // 3.5 System.out.println(Math.max(3, 9)); // 9 System.out.println(Math.round(2.5)); // 3: rounds halves up, returns long System.out.println(Math.round(-2.5)); // -2 System.out.println(Math.floor(-2.5) + " " + Math.ceil(2.1)); // -3.0 3.0 System.out.println(Math.clamp(15, 0, 10)); // 10 (Java 21+) System.out.println(Math.PI); System.out.println((int) (Math.random() 6) + 1 0); // true: (int) (Math.random() 6) + 1 is a dice roll 1-6 } } Comparing doubles Because of rounding, 0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3 is false . Compare floating-point numbers with a tolerance: java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { double x = 0.1 + 0.2; System.out.println(x == 0.3); // false System.out.println(Math.abs(x - 0.3) < 1e-9); // true } } Check yourself quiz ? What are 23 / 4 and 23 % 4 when both are ints? - 5.75 and 3 - 6 and 3 + 5 and 3 - 5 and 0.75 int / int is integer division, so the fraction is cut off: 23 / 4 is 5. The remainder 23 % 4 is 3, because 4 5 = 20 and 23 - 20 = 3. ? What does "Sum: " + 1 + 2 produce? - "Sum: 3" + "Sum: 12" - "Sum: 1 2" - A compile error: a String cannot be added to an int + works left to right, and once a String is involved it joins text: "Sum: " + 1 is "Sum: 1", then + 2 gives "Sum: 12". Write "Sum: " + (1 + 2) to get Sum: 3. ? What does 7 / 2 2.0 evaluate to? + 6.0 - 7.0 - 7 - 6 7 / 2 is integer division (3) and happens first; 3 2.0 is the double 6.0.

title: Operators
body: Complete the methods: java static boolean isLeapYear(int year) // divisible by 4, except centuries, except every 400 years static String clock(int minutes) // minutes after midnight as "h:mm": 125 is "2:05" static int coins(int cents, int coin) // how many coins of that size fit into cents static boolean canVote(int age, boolean isCitizen, boolean isRegistered) // 18 or over, citizen and registered clock wraps around the day: 1440 is "0:00" again, and negative minutes count back from midnight ( -30 is "23:30" ).

title: 1.04  Strings and Input
body: Working with String - its common methods, immutability, comparing with equals instead of ==, escapes and text blocks, formatting with printf and String.format - and reading keyboard input with Scanner, including the nextInt/nextLine trap. Strings A String is a sequence of characters. Strings are immutable : methods return new strings and never change the original. java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { String s = " Ada Lovelace "; String t = s.trim(); System.out.println(" " + t + " " + t.length()); System.out.println(t.toUpperCase() + " " + t.toLowerCase()); System.out.println(t.charAt(0) + " " + t.charAt(t.length() - 1)); System.out.println(t.substring(4) + " " + t.substring(0, 3)); // from 4 / from 0 up to 3 System.out.println(t.indexOf("Love") + " " + t.indexOf('z')); // position, or -1 System.out.println(t.contains("Love") + " " + t.startsWith("Ada") + " " + t.endsWith("x")); System.out.println(t.replace("Ada", "Augusta")); System.out.println(String.join("-", t.split(" "))); System.out.println("ha".repeat(3) + " " + "".isEmpty() + " " + " ".isBlank()); } } Method Gives --- --- length() , charAt(i) Number of characters, the character at index i (from 0) substring(start) , substring(start, end) Part of the string (end excluded) indexOf(x) , lastIndexOf(x) Position, or -1 toUpperCase() , toLowerCase() , trim() , strip() New strings contains , startsWith , endsWith , isEmpty , isBlank Tests replace(a, b) , split(regex) , String.join(sep, parts) Change, split, join equals , equalsIgnoreCase , compareTo Comparisons equals, not == == on objects asks "is this the same object ?". Two strings with the same text can be different objects, so always compare text with equals : java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { String a = "hello"; String b = new String("hello"); System.out.println(a == b); // false: different objects System.out.println(a.equals(b)); // true: same text System.out.println("Hello".equalsIgnoreCase(a)); System.out.println("apple".compareTo("banana") < 0); // alphabetical order } } "hello" == "hello" sometimes happens to be true (Java reuses identical literals), which makes the bug hard to notice. Use equals every time. Escapes and text blocks java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { System.out.println("Tab:\tQuote:\" Backslash:\\ Newline:\nnext line"); String json = """ { "name": "Ada", "langs": "Java", "C" } """; // a text block (Java 15+): no escaping needed System.out.print(json); } } Formatting printf and String.format use format specifiers : java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { String name = "Tea"; double price = 2.5; int qty = 3; System.out.printf("%s x%d = %.2f%n", name, qty, price qty); // %n: a new line System.out.printf(" %-10s %8.2f %05d %n", name, price, 42); // left-aligned, width 8, zero-padded String line = String.format("%,d people", 1234567); System.out.println(line); System.out.println("%s is %d".formatted("Ada", 36)); } } Specifier For --- --- %s Any value as text %d Whole numbers %.2f Decimals with 2 places %10s , %-10s Right / left aligned in 10 characters %05d , %,d Zero-padded, thousands separators %n A line break Reading input with Scanner java import java.util.Scanner; public class Main { public static void main(String args) { Scanner in = new Scanner(System.in); System.out.print("What is your name? "); String name = in.nextLine(); System.out.print("Your age? "); int age = in.nextInt(); System.out.println("Hello, " + name + "! Next year you will be " + (age + 1) + "."); } } import java.util.Scanner; at the top of the file makes the Scanner class available. nextLine() reads a whole line, nextInt() and nextDouble() read the next number, and hasNextInt() / hasNextLine() check what comes next. The classic trap : nextInt() reads the number but leaves the line break after it. A nextLine() right after returns that empty rest of the line. Either call an extra nextLine() after the number, or read every line with nextLine() and convert it with Integer.parseInt(line.trim()) , which is what this course does. Check yourself quiz ? Why can a == b print false for two strings that both contain "hello"? - == compares strings with case sensitivity, and equals does not - == only works for strings created with new String(...) - The strings have different lengths in memory + == compares references, and they are two different objects; equals compares the text On objects, == asks "is this the same object?". Two strings with the same text can be different objects, so compare text with equals ( equalsIgnoreCase is the one that ignores case). ? What is "programming".substring(3, 7) ? - "gramm" - "ogra" + "gram" - "ramm" The characters from index 3 up to, but not including, index 7: g, r, a, m. Indexes start at 0, and the end index is excluded. ? After int n = in.nextInt(); String s = in.nextLine(); with the input "5" then "Ada" on the next line, what is s ? - "Ada" + "" (the empty rest of the line after 5) - "5" - It throws an exception nextInt reads the number but leaves the line break; nextLine then reads the empty rest of that line, not "Ada".

body: Complete the methods, using the String methods from the lesson (no loops needed): java static String initials(String fullName) // first and last initial: "ada king lovelace" gives "A.L." static int countWord(String text, String word) // how many times word appears in text, ignoring case static String censor(String text, String word) // word in lower case, UPPER CASE or Capitalized replaced by of the same length static String priceLine(String item, double price) // item left in 12 characters, price right in 8 with 2 decimals - initials ignores spaces around the name, and a single name gives one initial: "plato" gives "P." . - countWord("The cat and the hat. THE end", "the") is 3. Matches inside other words count too: countWord("theme", "the") is 1. - censor("Darn, DARN it", "darn") gives " , it" , and "darned Darn" becomes " ed " . The word can be given in any case. - priceLine("Tea", 2.5) is "Tea 2.50" . Use String.format(Locale.ROOT, ...) , with import java.util.Locale; at the top of the file, so the decimal point is . everywhere.

title: 1.05  Control Flow
body: Making decisions with if and else, the classic switch statement and the modern switch expression with arrows, loops with while, do-while, for and the enhanced for, break and continue, labelled breaks for nested loops, and input loops with a sentinel. if and else java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { int temperature = 23; if (temperature = 30) { System.out.println("Hot"); } else if (temperature = 18) { System.out.println("Pleasant"); } else { System.out.println("Cold"); } } } Always use braces, even for one statement: without them, only the first line belongs to the if , however it is indented. switch The modern switch expression (Java 14+) uses arrows, needs no break , and produces a value: java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { int day = 6; String kind = switch (day) { case 6, 7 - "weekend"; case 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 - "weekday"; default - "not a day"; }; System.out.println(kind); String command = "stop"; switch (command) { case "go", "start" - System.out.println("Starting"); case "stop" - System.out.println("Stopping"); default - System.out.println("Unknown command"); } } } You will also meet the classic form with colons. There, each case falls through into the next unless it ends with break , a frequent source of bugs: java-norun switch (command) { case "go": System.out.println("Starting"); break; // without this, "Stopping" would print too case "stop": System.out.println("Stopping"); break; default: System.out.println("Unknown"); } Prefer the arrow form in new code. while and do-while java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { int n = 27, steps = 0; while (n != 1) { n = (n % 2 == 0) ? n / 2 : 3 n + 1; steps++; } System.out.println(steps + " steps"); int tries = 0; do { tries++; // runs at least once } while (tries < 3); System.out.println(tries); } } for loops java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) { System.out.print(i + " "); } System.out.println(); String names = {"Ada", "Grace", "Linus"}; for (String name : names) { // the enhanced for: every item System.out.println(name.toUpperCase()); } for (int row = 1; row <= 3; row++) { // nested loops: a times table for (int col = 1; col <= 4; col++) { System.out.printf("%4d", row col); } System.out.println(); } } } Use the classic for when you need the index or count; the enhanced for ( for (Type x : collection) ) when you just need every item. break and continue java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { int numbers = {4, 7, -1, 12, 0, 9}; int sum = 0; for (int x : numbers) { if (x < 0) continue; // skip this one if (x == 0) break; // stop the loop sum += x; } System.out.println(sum); // 23 outer: for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) { for (int j = 0; j < 5; j++) { if (i j == 6) { System.out.println("found " + i + " x " + j); break outer; // leaves both loops } } } } } Input loops A common pattern reads until a special sentinel value or the end of input: java import java.util.Scanner; public class Main { public static void main(String args) { Scanner in = new Scanner(System.in); int total = 0; while (in.hasNextLine()) { String line = in.nextLine().trim(); if (line.equals("done")) break; try { total += Integer.parseInt(line); } catch (NumberFormatException e) { System.out.println("Not a number: " + line); } } System.out.println("Total: " + total); } } try / catch handles text that is not a number; exceptions are covered fully in lesson 4.04. Check yourself quiz ? What happens in a classic (colon) switch when a case has no break ? + Execution falls through into the next case's statements - The compiler reports a missing break - The switch jumps straight to default - The switch stops after that case anyway In the classic form, cases fall through until a break (or the end of the switch), and the compiler allows it. The arrow form never falls through. ? What does break outer; do inside two nested loops, where the outer loop is labelled outer: ? - Leaves only the inner loop, like a plain break - Skips to the next round of the outer loop + Leaves the loop labelled outer , including the loop nested inside it - Ends the whole program A labelled break leaves the labelled loop and everything nested in it. Skipping to the next round of the outer loop would be continue outer; . ? How many times does for (int i = 10; i 0; i -= 4) run its body? - 2 - 4 - 10 + 3 i takes the values 10, 6 and 2; the next value, -2, fails the test i 0 .

Any other line prints Skipping: <the line as typed and is ignored. - Each student line is the name left-aligned in 12 characters, the score right-aligned in 3, two spaces and the grade: 90 and above A , 80 B , 70 C , 60 D , below 60 F . - After the input: the count, the average with 2 decimals (with a . : use Locale.ROOT ), the highest and lowest (the first one on a tie) and how many of each grade. - With no valid students, print only No students. - Do it without arrays or lists (they come in milestone 2): keep running totals as you read.

title: 2.01  Methods
body: Defining static methods with parameters and return types, void methods, calling methods, pass-by-value for primitives and references, overloading, variable-length arguments, local variables and scope, returning early, and designing small methods that do one thing. Defining methods A method is a named block of code with parameters and a return type . Until classes and objects arrive in milestone 3, our methods are static : they belong to the class and are called by name. java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { System.out.println(area(3, 4)); System.out.println(describe("Ada", 36)); greet("Grace"); System.out.println(isEven(10) + " " + isEven(7)); } static double area(double width, double height) { return width height; } static String describe(String name, int age) { return name + " (" + age + ")"; } static void greet(String name) { // void: returns nothing System.out.println("Hello, " + name + "!"); } static boolean isEven(int n) { return n % 2 == 0; } } Every path through a non-void method must return a value of the declared type; the compiler checks this ("missing return statement"). A return can come early to stop the method at once: java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { System.out.println(grade(95) + grade(72) + grade(-5)); } static String grade(int score) { if (score < 0 score 100) return "?"; if (score = 90) return "A"; if (score = 70) return "C"; return "F"; } } Pass by value Java always passes copies of values . For a primitive, the method gets a copy of the number; changing the parameter does not change the caller's variable. For an object, the method gets a copy of the reference : it can change the object the reference points to, but not make the caller's variable point somewhere else. java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { int n = 1; addOne(n); System.out.println(n); // 1: addOne changed its own copy int numbers = {1, 2, 3}; doubleAll(numbers); System.out.println(numbers 0 ); // 2: the array itself was changed replace(numbers); System.out.println(numbers 0 ); // 2: replacing the parameter does not affect the caller } static void addOne(int x) { x = x + 1; } static void doubleAll(int values) { for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) values i = 2; } static void replace(int values) { values = new int {100, 200}; } } Overloading Methods may share a name when their parameter lists differ. The compiler picks the closest match: java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { System.out.println(max(3, 9)); System.out.println(max(2.5, 1.5)); System.out.println(max(4, 8, 6)); System.out.println(sum() + " " + sum(1, 2, 3) + " " + sum(new int {10, 20})); } static int max(int a, int b) { return a b ? a : b; } static double max(double a, double b) { return a b ? a : b; } static int max(int a, int b, int c) { return max(max(a, b), c); } static int sum(int... numbers) { // varargs: any number of ints, as an array int total = 0; for (int n : numbers) total += n; return total; } } Scope A variable exists from its declaration to the end of the block { } it is declared in. Parameters and variables of one method are invisible to other methods; the only way to share values is to pass them as arguments and return results. Good methods - One method, one job, named with a verb: calculateTotal , isValid , printReport . - Prefer methods that return results over methods that print them: a returned value can be tested, printed, or used in further calculations. - Keep methods short. If you need a comment to explain a section of a method, that section probably wants to be its own method. Check yourself quiz ? A method sets its int parameter to 5. Has the caller's variable changed afterwards? - Yes: the parameter and the caller's variable are the same variable + No: Java passed a copy of the value - Only if the method also returns the new value - Only if the caller's variable was declared final Java always passes copies of values. Changing the copy inside the method leaves the caller's variable as it was; returning a value only helps if the caller assigns it. ? Can a method change the contents of an array passed to it? - No: Java passes a copy of the array - Only if the method returns the array afterwards + Yes: it gets a copy of the reference, which points to the same array The method receives a copy of the reference, not a copy of the array, so values 0 = 9 changes the caller's array. Making the parameter point to a new array does not affect the caller, though. ? Which pair of methods can NOT both exist in one class? - int f(int x) and int f(double x) - int f(int x) and int f(int x, int y) - void f() and void f(String s) + int f(int x) and double f(int x) Overloads must differ in their parameter lists; a different return type alone is not enough.

title: Writing methods
body: Complete the static methods in Solution : java static boolean isPrime(int n) // true for 2, 3, 5, 7, ...; false for anything below 2 static int gcd(int a, int b) // greatest common divisor (Euclid's algorithm); gcd(0, 0) is 0 static int digitSum(long n) // sum of the decimal digits, ignoring a minus sign static double area(double radius) // a circle static double area(double width, double height) // a rectangle (an overload) static String repeat(String s, int times, String separator) // "ab", 3, "-" gives "ab-ab-ab" isPrime should only try divisors up to the square root of n . gcd works for negative numbers too and always returns a value of 0 or more.

title: 2.02  Arrays
body: Creating arrays with new and initializers, indexing and length, default values, looping over arrays, ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, the java.util.Arrays helpers (toString, sort, fill, copyOf, equals, binarySearch), copying versus sharing, two-dimensional arrays, and classic array algorithms. Creating arrays An array holds a fixed number of values of one type. Its length is set when it is created and never changes: java import java.util.Arrays; public class Main { public static void main(String args) { int scores = new int 5 ; // five zeros scores 0 = 90; scores 4 = 75; String days = {"Mon", "Tue", "Wed"}; // an initializer double prices = new double {2.5, 4.0}; System.out.println(scores.length + " " + days.length); System.out.println(days days.length - 1 ); System.out.println(Arrays.toString(scores)); // 90, 0, 0, 0, 75 System.out.println(scores); // I@1b6d3586: not the contents! } } Indexes run from 0 to length - 1 . Using any other index throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException . New arrays are filled with default values : 0 , 0.0 , false , '\u0000' , or null for objects. Printing an array directly shows its type and an identity code; use Arrays.toString . Looping java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { int data = {4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42}; int sum = 0, max = data 0 ; for (int x : data) { // every value sum += x; if (x max) max = x; } System.out.println(sum + " " + max + " " + (double) sum / data.length); for (int i = data.length - 1; i = 0; i--) { // with indexes: backwards System.out.print(data i + " "); } System.out.println(); } } The Arrays class java import java.util.Arrays; public class Main { public static void main(String args) { int a = {5, 2, 9, 1}; Arrays.sort(a); System.out.println(Arrays.toString(a)); System.out.println(Arrays.binarySearch(a, 5)); // index 2: needs a sorted array int longer = Arrays.copyOf(a, 6); // copy, padded with zeros int part = Arrays.copyOfRange(a, 1, 3); // indexes 1 and 2 int sevens = new int 3 ; Arrays.fill(sevens, 7); System.out.println(Arrays.toString(longer) + Arrays.toString(part) + Arrays.toString(sevens)); System.out.println(Arrays.equals(a, new int {1, 2, 5, 9}) + " " + (a == new int {1, 2, 5, 9})); System.out.println(Arrays.stream(a).sum()); } } == on arrays compares references; Arrays.equals compares contents. Copying versus sharing Arrays are objects: assigning one array variable to another shares the same array. java import java.util.Arrays; public class Main { public static void main(String args) { int a = {1, 2, 3}; int same = a; // the same array int copy = a.clone(); // a new array with the same values same 0 = 99; System.out.println(Arrays.toString(a) + " " + Arrays.toString(copy)); } } Two dimensions java import java.util.Arrays; public class Main { public static void main(String args) { int grid = new int 3 4 ; // 3 rows of 4 grid 1 2 = 7; for (int row : grid) System.out.println(Arrays.toString(row)); int triangle = {{1}, {1, 1}, {1, 2, 1}}; // rows may have different lengths System.out.println(triangle 2 .length + " " + Arrays.deepToString(triangle)); } } A 2D array is an array of arrays: grid.length is the number of rows and grid r .length the length of row r . Classic algorithms Many exam questions are small array algorithms. Two examples: java import java.util.Arrays; public class Main { public static void main(String args) { int values = {3, 8, 1, 9, 4}; reverse(values); System.out.println(Arrays.toString(values)); System.out.println(indexOf(values, 1) + " " + indexOf(values, 7)); } static void reverse(int a) { for (int i = 0, j = a.length - 1; i < j; i++, j--) { int tmp = a i ; a i = a j ; a j = tmp; } } static int indexOf(int a, int target) { // linear search for (int i = 0; i < a.length; i++) { if (a i == target) return i; } return -1; } } Check yourself quiz ? What are the valid indexes of an array of length 5? + 0 to 4 - 1 to 5 - 0 to 5 - 1 to 4 Indexes start at 0, so the last one is length - 1 , which is 4. Index 5 throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException . ? Why does System.out.println(array) not show the values? - The values are only printed after the array is sorted - println prints only the first element of an array + Arrays have no readable toString ; use Arrays.toString(array) - The array must be converted with String.valueOf first Printing an array directly gives its type and an identity code, something like I@1b6d3586 . Arrays.toString (or Arrays.deepToString for 2D arrays) shows the contents. ? After int b = a; b 0 = 5; , what is a 0 ? - Unchanged - 0 + 5 - An error a and b refer to the same array, so a change through one is seen through the other; use a.clone() for a copy.

title: Array algorithms
body: Complete the methods. None of them may change the arrays they are given. java static int rotate(int values, int k) // every item k places to the right, wrapping around; k may be negative or large static int secondLargest(int values) // the second-largest distinct value static int runningTotals(int values) // {1, 2, 3} gives {1, 3, 6} static int transpose(int m) // rows become columns static int mergeSorted(int a, int b) // two sorted arrays into one sorted array, in one pass - secondLargest({5, 9, 9, 2}) is 5. With fewer than two distinct values it throws IllegalArgumentException . - transpose of a 2 × 3 matrix is 3 × 2. You may assume every row has the same length (and that there is at least one row).

title: 2.03  ArrayList and Wrapper Types
body: The growable ArrayList - adding, getting, setting, removing, searching and sorting - the List interface, wrapper classes like Integer and Double, autoboxing and its traps (remove by index or value, == on Integers, null unboxing), List.of, and iterating while removing safely. ArrayList An ArrayList is a list that grows and shrinks as needed. The type in angle brackets says what it holds: java import java.util.ArrayList; import java.util.Collections; import java.util.List; public class Main { public static void main(String args) { List<String names = new ArrayList< (); names.add("Grace"); names.add("Ada"); names.add(0, "Ken"); // insert at index 0 names.set(1, "Linus"); // replace index 1 System.out.println(names + " " + names.size()); System.out.println(names.get(0) + " " + names.contains("Ada") + " " + names.indexOf("Ada")); names.remove("Ken"); // by value names.remove(0); // by index Collections.addAll(names, "Barbara", "Margaret"); Collections.sort(names); System.out.println(names); System.out.println(names.isEmpty()); } } Declare variables with the interface type List<String and create an ArrayList< () : the rest of the code then works with any kind of list. < (the diamond) lets the compiler fill in the type. Array ArrayList --- --- int a = new int 5 ; List<Integer list = new ArrayList< (); a.length list.size() a i , a i = x list.get(i) , list.set(i, x) fixed size add , remove , grows as needed holds primitives holds objects only Wrapper types Collections hold objects, not primitives. Each primitive has a wrapper class : Integer , Double , Boolean , Character , Long ... Java converts automatically between them ( autoboxing and unboxing ): java import java.util.ArrayList; import java.util.List; public class Main { public static void main(String args) { List<Integer numbers = new ArrayList< (); numbers.add(5); // int 5 is boxed into an Integer numbers.add(10); int first = numbers.get(0); // unboxed back to int int total = 0; for (int n : numbers) total += n; System.out.println(first + " " + total); System.out.println(Integer.parseInt("42") + Integer.MAX_VALUE % 10 + " " + Character.isDigit('7')); } } Three traps to know: java import java.util.ArrayList; import java.util.List; public class Main { public static void main(String args) { List<Integer list = new ArrayList< (List.of(10, 20, 30)); list.remove(1); // removes INDEX 1 (the 20), not the value 1 list.remove(Integer.valueOf(30)); // removes the VALUE 30 System.out.println(list); Integer a = 1000, b = 1000; System.out.println(a == b); // false: two different Integer objects System.out.println(a.equals(b)); // true: compare wrapper values with equals Integer missing = null; try { int n = missing; // unboxing null throws NullPointerException } catch (NullPointerException e) { System.out.println("cannot unbox null"); } } } Fixed lists and copies List.of(1, 2, 3) makes an unmodifiable list: add and set throw UnsupportedOperationException . It is ideal for constants and test data. To get a list you can change, copy it: new ArrayList< (List.of(1, 2, 3)) . Removing while looping Removing items inside an enhanced for over the same list usually throws ConcurrentModificationException (and at best skips items). Loop backwards with indexes, or use removeIf : java import java.util.ArrayList; import java.util.List; public class Main { public static void main(String args) { List<Integer values = new ArrayList< (List.of(4, 7, 10, 13, 16)); for (int i = values.size() - 1; i = 0; i--) { if (values.get(i) % 2 == 1) values.remove(i); } System.out.println(values); values.removeIf(v - v 12); // a lambda (lesson 6.01): remove what matches System.out.println(values); } } Check yourself quiz ? Why can you not write List<int ? - int values are too small to store in a list - You can, but only with new ArrayList<int () instead of < + Generic collections hold objects only; use the wrapper type List<Integer - Lists can only hold String and other classes from java.lang Collections hold objects, not primitives. Each primitive has a wrapper class, and autoboxing converts between int and Integer for you. ? On a List<Integer , what does list.remove(1) remove? + The item at index 1 - The first item equal to 1 - Every item equal to 1 - The first item, because lists count from 1 With an int argument, remove picks the by-index version. To remove the value 1, call list.remove(Integer.valueOf(1)) . ? What happens when you call add on List.of(1, 2) ? - The item is added - Nothing - It does not compile + UnsupportedOperationException is thrown List.of returns an unmodifiable list. It compiles, because the type is still List , but changing it fails at run time; copy it with new ArrayList< (...) to get a list you can change.

title: 2.04  Recursion
body: Methods that call themselves - base cases and recursive cases, how the call stack works, tracing factorial and Fibonacci, recursion on arrays and strings, the cost of naive recursion and memoization, StackOverflowError, and when to prefer a loop. A method that calls itself A recursive method solves a problem by calling itself on a smaller version of the same problem. Every recursive method needs: 1. a base case that is answered directly, without recursion; 2. a recursive case that moves toward the base case. java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { System.out.println(factorial(5)); System.out.println(sumTo(100)); System.out.println(power(2, 10)); } static long factorial(int n) { if (n <= 1) return 1; // base case return n factorial(n - 1); // recursive case: a smaller problem } static int sumTo(int n) { return n == 0 ? 0 : n + sumTo(n - 1); } static long power(long base, int exp) { if (exp == 0) return 1; long half = power(base, exp / 2); // halves the problem each time return exp % 2 == 0 ? half half : half half base; } } The call stack Each call gets its own stack frame holding its parameters and local variables. factorial(4) waits for factorial(3) , which waits for factorial(2) , and so on; when the base case returns, the waiting calls finish in reverse order: text factorial(4) 4 factorial(3) 3 factorial(2) 2 factorial(1) 1 <- base case 2 1 = 2 3 2 = 6 4 6 = 24 Without a base case (or with one that is never reached), calls pile up until the stack runs out of space and Java throws StackOverflowError . Recursion on arrays and strings Recursion fits problems that contain smaller copies of themselves. Pass indexes to work on part of an array without copying it: java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { System.out.println(reverse("recursion")); System.out.println(isPalindrome("racecar") + " " + isPalindrome("java")); int sorted = {2, 5, 8, 12, 16, 23, 38, 56, 72, 91}; System.out.println(binarySearch(sorted, 23, 0, sorted.length - 1)); System.out.println(countDigits(90210)); } static String reverse(String s) { if (s.length() <= 1) return s; return reverse(s.substring(1)) + s.charAt(0); } static boolean isPalindrome(String s) { if (s.length() <= 1) return true; return s.charAt(0) == s.charAt(s.length() - 1) && isPalindrome(s.substring(1, s.length() - 1)); } static int binarySearch(int a, int target, int lo, int hi) { if (lo hi) return -1; // nothing left: not found int mid = (lo + hi) / 2; if (a mid == target) return mid; if (a mid < target) return binarySearch(a, target, mid + 1, hi); return binarySearch(a, target, lo, mid - 1); } static int countDigits(int n) { return n < 10 ? 1 : 1 + countDigits(n / 10); } } Repeated work and memoization The direct recursive Fibonacci is elegant and terribly slow: fib(n) calls fib(n-1) and fib(n-2) , which recompute the same values again and again, roughly 1.6ⁿ calls in total. Memoization stores each answer the first time it is computed: java import java.util.HashMap; import java.util.Map; public class Main { static int calls = 0; static final Map<Integer, Long memo = new HashMap< (); public static void main(String args) { System.out.println(slowFib(25) + " after " + calls + " calls"); calls = 0; System.out.println(fastFib(90) + " after " + calls + " calls"); } static long slowFib(int n) { calls++; return n < 2 ? n : slowFib(n - 1) + slowFib(n - 2); } static long fastFib(int n) { calls++; if (n < 2) return n; Long known = memo.get(n); if (known != null) return known; long result = fastFib(n - 1) + fastFib(n - 2); memo.put(n, result); return result; } } Recursion or a loop? Anything recursive can be written with a loop, and vice versa. Use recursion when the problem is naturally recursive: trees (lesson 5.05), nested structures, divide-and-conquer algorithms like merge sort and quicksort (lesson 5.02), and exploring all combinations. Use a loop for simple repetition such as summing an array: it is clearer and cannot overflow the stack. Check yourself quiz ? What two parts does every recursive method need? - A loop, and a counter that stops it after n steps - A static field and a return statement - A parameter and a stack frame of its own + A base case, and a recursive case that moves toward it The base case stops the recursion; the recursive case calls the method on a smaller problem so the base case is eventually reached. Without that, the calls pile up until StackOverflowError . ? Why is the plain recursive Fibonacci slow? - Recursive calls are always much slower than loops + It recomputes the same smaller values again and again - It uses long , which is much slower than int - Each call copies the whole call stack first fib(n) calls fib(n-1) and fib(n-2) , which compute the same smaller values again and again, so the number of calls grows exponentially (roughly 1.6ⁿ). Memoization stores each answer once. ? What does f(3) print for static void f(int n) { if (n == 0) return; f(n - 1); System.out.print(n); } ? - 321 - 3210 + 123 - 0123 The print happens after the recursive call returns, so the deepest call (n = 1) prints first; f(0) returns without printing.

title: Recursion
body: Write these with recursion (no loops): java static String toBinary(int n) // 10 gives "1010", 0 gives "0"; n is 0 or more static int countPaths(int rows, int cols) // paths from the top-left to the bottom-right of a grid, moving only right or down static List<String permutations(String s) // every ordering of the characters, sorted, without repeats static List<String hanoi(int n, char from, char to, char via) // the moves to shift n discs, like "A- C" - countPaths(3, 3) is 6. It must be fast for countPaths(16, 16) (155117520): remember answers you have already worked out. - permutations("aba") is "aab", "aba", "baa" . - hanoi(2, 'A', 'C', 'B') is "A- B", "A- C", "B- C" .

title: 2.05  Strings in Depth
body: Characters as numbers and the Character class, walking through strings, why repeated concatenation is slow and how StringBuilder fixes it, string comparison and sorting, splitting with regular expressions, a first look at Pattern and Matcher, and converting between strings, chars and numbers. Characters A char is a 16-bit number that stands for a character. Arithmetic on chars works on those numbers: java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { char c = 'b'; System.out.println((int) c); // 98 System.out.println((char) (c + 1)); // c System.out.println('7' - '0'); // 7: a digit character to its value System.out.println(Character.isLetter(c) + " " + Character.isDigit('7') + " " + Character.isWhitespace(' ')); System.out.println(Character.toUpperCase(c) + " " + Character.isUpperCase('Q')); System.out.println((char) ('a' + 25)); // z } } c - 'a' gives a letter's position in the alphabet (0 for a ), which is the trick behind Caesar ciphers and letter counts. Walking through a string java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { String text = "Hello, World 2026!"; int letters = 0, digits = 0, upper = 0; for (int i = 0; i < text.length(); i++) { char ch = text.charAt(i); if (Character.isLetter(ch)) letters++; if (Character.isDigit(ch)) digits++; if (Character.isUpperCase(ch)) upper++; } System.out.println(letters + " letters, " + digits + " digits, " + upper + " capitals"); int counts = new int 26 ; for (char ch : text.toLowerCase().toCharArray()) { if (ch = 'a' && ch <= 'z') counts ch - 'a' ++; } System.out.println("l appears " + counts 'l' - 'a' + " times"); } } StringBuilder Strings are immutable, so s += x creates a brand-new string and copies everything each time. In a loop that is slow (quadratic). A StringBuilder is a mutable buffer: java public class Main { public static void main(String args) { StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder(); for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) { sb.append(i); if (i < 5) sb.append(", "); } System.out.println(sb); sb.insert(0, " ").append(" "); sb.reverse(); System.out.println(sb + " " + sb.length()); sb.setLength(0); // clear it sb.append("caesar").setCharAt(0, 'C'); System.out.println(sb.toString()); } } Method Does --- --- append(x) Add to the end (returns the builder, so calls chain) insert(i, x) , deleteCharAt(i) , delete(a, b) Insert and remove setCharAt(i, c) , reverse() Change in place length() , charAt(i) , toString() Read Comparing and sorting compareTo orders strings by character codes: all capitals come before all lower-case letters ( "Zoe" before "adam" ). For human ordering ignore case: java import java.util.ArrayList; import java.util.List; public class Main { public static void main(String args) { List<String names = new ArrayList< (List.of("bob", "Alice", "carol", "Bob")); names.sort(null); // natural (code) order System.out.println(names); names.sort(String.CASE_INSENSITIVE_ORDER); System.out.println(names); System.out.println("apple".compareTo("apricot") < 0); } } Regular expressions split , matches and replaceAll take regular expressions , a small language for text patterns: Pattern Matches --- --- \\d , \\s , \\w A digit, a white-space character, a word character aeiou , ^0-9 One of these / anything but these + , , ? , {2,4} One or more, zero or more, optional, 2 to 4 times ^ , $ Start, end In Java source, each backslash is written twice: the regex \d+ is the string "\\d+" . java import java.util.regex.Matcher; import java.util.regex.Pattern; public class Main { public static void main(String args) { System.out.println(String.join(" ", "a, b;c d".split(" ,;\\s +"))); System.out.println("2026-03-14".matches("\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}")); System.out.println("call 555-1234 or 555-9876".replaceAll("\\d{3}-\\d{4}", "<number ")); Matcher m = Pattern.compile("(\\w+)@(\\w+\\.\\w+)").matcher("ada@math.org, grace@navy.mil"); while (m.find()) System.out.println(m.group(1) + " at " + m.group(2)); } } Converting From To Code --- --- --- String int / double Integer.parseInt(s) , Double.parseDouble(s) number String String.valueOf(n) , Integer.toString(n) , "" + n String char s.toCharArray() char String new String(chars) , String.valueOf(chars) char String String.valueOf(c) , Character.toString(c) int binary / hex text Integer.toBinaryString(n) , Integer.toHexString(n) Check yourself quiz ? Why build a long string in a loop with StringBuilder rather than += ? - += cannot join a char to a String + Strings are immutable, so += copies the whole string every time; StringBuilder appends in place - += changes the original string, which other variables may still use - StringBuilder sorts the pieces as it adds them Each += creates a brand-new string and copies everything so far, which is quadratic in a loop. A StringBuilder is a mutable buffer you append to. ? What is '7' - '0' , and why? - '7' , because subtracting '0' changes nothing - 55, the character code of '7' - A compile error: you cannot subtract characters + 7, because the codes of '0' to '9' are consecutive Arithmetic on chars works on their codes, and the digit codes are in order. '7' is 55 and '0' is 48, so the difference is the digit's value, 7. ? What does "a1b22c333".split("\\d+") return? - "a1", "b22", "c333" - "1", "22", "333" + "a", "b", "c" - "a", "1", "b", "22", "c", "333" The runs of digits are the separators and are not kept; the trailing empty piece after "333" is dropped.

title: Tic-tac-toe
body: Write a two-player game of tic-tac-toe on a 3 × 3 board. Players type their moves as row column (each 1 to 3): X to move: 2 2 . . . ---+---+--- . X . ---+---+--- . . . O to move: 1 1 O . . ---+---+--- . X . ---+---+--- . . . X to move: ... Rules: - X moves first; players alternate. Print X to move: (or O to move: ) before reading each line. - A line that is not two whole numbers prints Enter row and column, like 2 3 ; numbers outside 1 to 3 print Out of range ; a square that is already used prints Taken . After any of these, the same player tries again. - After each valid move, print the board as shown: each row is a b c , rows are separated by ---+---+--- , and empty squares are . . - When a player gets three in a row (across, down or diagonally), print X wins!
