title: The model behind a virtual list
match: The model behind a virtual list
body: A virtual list view (lesson 3.05) stores nothing: it asks your code for the number of rows and the text of each cell. Write the model behind such a list of files: sorting by any column with Explorer's ordering, filtering as the user types, selection that survives sorting and filtering, and the status bar text. The milestone 6 file finder uses it. cpp struct Item { int id; std::string name; std::uint64_t size; std::string modified; }; // modified: "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM" class ResultList { public: void setItems(std::vector<Item items); void setFilter(const std::string& text); void clickColumn(int column); // 0 name, 1 size, 2 modified int sortColumn() const; bool ascending() const; int count() const; // visible rows int idAt(int row) const; std::string cellText(int row, int column) const; void click(int row); void ctrlClick(int row); void shiftClick(int row); std::vector<int selectedIds() const; // in display order std::string status() const; }; Sorting : the list starts sorted by name, ascending. Clicking the sorted column again reverses the direction; clicking another column sorts by it, ascending. Names compare with practice 3.05's naturalLess ; sizes as numbers; dates as text (the format sorts correctly). Ties are broken by name (natural order) and then by id, so the order is always fully defined. Descending is exactly the reverse of ascending. Filtering : the filter keeps the items whose name contains the text, ignoring case (empty shows everything). Hidden items are removed from the selection. setItems replaces everything, clears the filter and the selection, and keeps the sort. Cells : column 0 is the name, column 1 the size formatted by practice 3.05's formatSize , column 2 the date as stored. Selection works by item id , so it survives sorting and filtering: - click selects only that row and makes it the anchor ; - ctrlClick toggles that row and makes it the anchor; - shiftClick selects exactly the rows from the anchor to that row (both included, in display order), keeping the anchor; without a visible anchor it acts like click . Status , with N items in total, V shown and S selected: "N items" without a filter, or "V of N items shown" with one; then ", S selected" when S 0 . Use item instead of items when N is 1.

title: 4.01  Flicker-Free Drawing
body: Why windows flicker when they repaint, and the fixes - not erasing the background, drawing into an off-screen bitmap first, the buffered-paint API, painting only what changed, and scrolling content efficiently. Where flicker comes from Flicker is the screen briefly showing a half-finished picture. With GDI it happens in two ways: 1. Erasing : before WM_PAINT , Windows sends WM_ERASEBKGND , and the default handling fills the area with the class background. For a moment the screen shows an empty window, then your drawing appears on top. 2. Overdraw : your own paint code fills a rectangle, then draws over it. Each step is visible for a moment. Resizing makes both happen dozens of times a second. Step 1: do not erase If your WM_PAINT covers the whole area anyway, tell Windows not to erase: cpp-norun case WM_ERASEBKGND: return 1; // "done", without doing anything (and pass FALSE as the last argument of InvalidateRect ). A class with no background brush ( hbrBackground = nullptr ) has the same effect. Step 2: draw off-screen Double buffering draws the whole frame into a bitmap in memory, then copies it to the window in one operation. Nobody ever sees the intermediate steps: cpp-norun case WM_PAINT: { PAINTSTRUCT ps; HDC dc = BeginPaint(hwnd, &ps); RECT rc; GetClientRect(hwnd, &rc); HDC mem = CreateCompatibleDC(dc); HBITMAP bmp = CreateCompatibleBitmap(dc, rc.right, rc.bottom); HGDIOBJ old = SelectObject(mem, bmp); FillRect(mem, &rc, m_background); drawEverything(mem); // all drawing goes to the memory DC BitBlt(dc, 0, 0, rc.right, rc.bottom, mem, 0, 0, SRCCOPY); // one copy to the screen SelectObject(mem, old); DeleteObject(bmp); DeleteDC(mem); EndPaint(hwnd, &ps); return 0; } Creating the bitmap on every paint is fine for small windows; for large ones, keep it between paints and re-create it only when the window becomes larger than the bitmap. The buffered-paint API Windows has this pattern built in, with the bitmap cached for you: cpp-norun BufferedPaintInit(); // once, at start-up (uxtheme.h, uxtheme.lib) PAINTSTRUCT ps; HDC dc = BeginPaint(hwnd, &ps); HDC mem = nullptr; HPAINTBUFFER buffer = BeginBufferedPaint(dc, &ps.rcPaint, BPBF_COMPATIBLEBITMAP, nullptr, &mem); if (buffer) { drawEverything(mem); EndBufferedPaint(buffer, TRUE); // TRUE: copy to the screen } EndPaint(hwnd, &ps); It buffers only rcPaint , the area that actually needs painting. Step 3: paint less Two habits make painting cheaper and smoother: - Invalidate precisely : when one item changes, invalidate its rectangle, not the whole window. - Skip what is outside rcPaint : test each item's rectangle against it ( IntersectRect ) and do not draw items that do not intersect. A list of 10 000 rows then draws only the 30 that are visible and changed. Scrolling To scroll content up by 40 pixels, there is no need to redraw everything: the window can move the existing pixels and repaint only the strip that became visible: cpp-norun ScrollWindowEx(hwnd, 0, -40, nullptr, nullptr, nullptr, nullptr, SW_INVALIDATE); // move pixels, invalidate the new strip UpdateWindow(hwnd); Combined with scroll bars ( SetScrollInfo , WM_VSCROLL ), this is how long documents scroll smoothly even with GDI. Working out exactly which strip needs repainting after a scroll is the practice. When GDI is not enough GDI has no antialiasing (jagged diagonal lines and circles), no transparency in most operations, and runs mostly on the CPU. For anything more than simple controls and text, use Direct2D (lesson 4.02), which draws on the GPU with antialiasing and is flicker-free by design. Check yourself quiz ? What is the first cause of flicker and how do you stop it? - Drawing too slowly; draw on a timer instead of in WM_PAINT + Background erasing before WM_PAINT ; return 1 from WM_ERASEBKGND - Calling EndPaint too early; call it before BeginPaint returns - Invalidating a rectangle; always invalidate the whole window instead The default WM_ERASEBKGND fills the area with the class background, so for a moment the window looks empty. When your paint covers everything, returning 1 says "done" without erasing. ? What does double buffering do? - It paints every frame twice, so missed pixels are filled in - It keeps two windows and shows one while the other is drawn - It halves the number of WM_PAINT messages the window gets + It draws into an off-screen bitmap, then copies it to the window at once All drawing goes to a memory DC, and one BitBlt copies the finished frame, so no half-drawn state is visible. The buffered-paint API does the same with a cached bitmap. ? What does ScrollWindowEx save? + It moves the drawn pixels and invalidates only the newly exposed strip - It saves the window's contents to a bitmap so they can be restored later - It stops WM_PAINT from being sent while the user scrolls - It moves the scroll bar thumb without changing the content Only the strip that became visible needs painting; scroll bars themselves are set with SetScrollInfo .

title: Painting less
body: Write the arithmetic behind lesson 4.01's "paint only what changed": cpp struct RECT { long left, top, right, bottom; }; RECT exposedAfterScroll(RECT client, int dy); // the strip to repaint after ScrollWindowEx(0, dy) void rowsToPaint(RECT paint, int scrollY, int rowHeight, int rowCount, int& first, int& last); class BackBuffer { public: bool ensure(int width, int height); // true if the bitmap had to be (re)created int width() const; int height() const; }; - exposedAfterScroll : scrolling the content by dy pixels (negative = content moves up) leaves a strip of dy pixels at the bottom (dy < 0) or top (dy 0) to repaint. If dy is at least the client height, the whole client area is exposed. dy == 0 exposes nothing: {0, 0, 0, 0} . - rowsToPaint : rows of rowHeight pixels are laid out from document y = 0; the window shows document y scrollY at its top. Give the first and last row (inclusive) that intersect the paint rectangle, clamped to 0 .. rowCount - 1 ; if none, first = 0 and last = -1 . - BackBuffer::ensure keeps the current bitmap if it is at least as large as asked on both axes. Otherwise it is re-created with each side rounded up to a multiple of 256, and never smaller than before on either axis (so a window that grows and shrinks does not keep re-creating it).

title: 4.02  Drawing with Direct2D
body: Direct2D draws antialiased shapes, gradients and bitmaps on the GPU. This lesson creates the factory and a render target for a window, separates device-independent and device-dependent resources, handles device loss, and uses transforms to move, rotate and scale drawings. The pieces Direct2D is a COM-based API (lesson 3.02): Object What Lifetime --- --- --- ID2D1Factory Creates everything else Whole program ID2D1HwndRenderTarget Draws into a window Until the device is lost Brushes, bitmaps, layers Belong to one render target Same as the render target Geometries, stroke styles Device-independent Whole program The distinction matters: device-dependent resources (the render target, brushes, bitmaps) live on the GPU and must be re-created if the device is lost; device-independent ones (geometries) do not. cpp-norun include <d2d1.h pragma comment(lib, "d2d1.lib") ComPtr<ID2D1Factory g_factory; D2D1CreateFactory(D2D1_FACTORY_TYPE_SINGLE_THREADED, g_factory.GetAddressOf()); // once Creating the render target lazily cpp-norun HRESULT createDeviceResources(HWND hwnd) { if (m_target) return S_OK; RECT rc; GetClientRect(hwnd, &rc); HRESULT hr = g_factory- CreateHwndRenderTarget( D2D1::RenderTargetProperties(D2D1_RENDER_TARGET_TYPE_DEFAULT, D2D1::PixelFormat(), 96.0f, 96.0f), D2D1::HwndRenderTargetProperties(hwnd, D2D1::SizeU(rc.right, rc.bottom)), m_target.ReleaseAndGetAddressOf()); if (SUCCEEDED(hr)) hr = m_target- CreateSolidColorBrush(D2D1::ColorF(0.2f, 0.4f, 0.8f), m_brush.ReleaseAndGetAddressOf()); if (SUCCEEDED(hr)) m_target- SetDpi(float(GetDpiForWindow(hwnd)), float(GetDpiForWindow(hwnd))); return hr; } SetDpi makes Direct2D work in device-independent pixels (DIPs, 1/96 inch): you draw at 96-DPI sizes and it scales to the monitor, which removes most of lesson 3.04's arithmetic. Drawing cpp-norun case WM_PAINT: { PAINTSTRUCT ps; BeginPaint(hwnd, &ps); if (SUCCEEDED(createDeviceResources(hwnd))) { m_target- BeginDraw(); m_target- Clear(D2D1::ColorF(D2D1::ColorF::White)); m_target- FillEllipse(D2D1::Ellipse(D2D1::Point2F(150, 120), 80, 50), m_brush.Get()); m_target- DrawLine(D2D1::Point2F(20, 20), D2D1::Point2F(300, 200), m_brush.Get(), 3.0f); m_target- DrawRoundedRectangle(D2D1::RoundedRect(D2D1::RectF(20, 220, 300, 300), 8, 8), m_brush.Get(), 1.5f); const HRESULT hr = m_target- EndDraw(); if (hr == D2DERR_RECREATE_TARGET) discardDeviceResources(); // device lost: re-create next time } EndPaint(hwnd, &ps); return 0; } case WM_SIZE: if (m_target) m_target- Resize(D2D1::SizeU(LOWORD(lParam), HIWORD(lParam))); return 0; The device can be lost when the graphics driver is updated, the GPU resets, or a remote desktop session starts. EndDraw then returns D2DERR_RECREATE_TARGET ; release every device-dependent resource and let the next paint re-create them. Programs that skip this go blank after a driver update until restarted. Colours in Direct2D are floats from 0 to 1 ( D2D1::ColorF(r, g, b, a) ), and coordinates are floats: a 1-pixel line on a whole coordinate is drawn across two pixel rows, half intensity each. To get crisp 1-pixel lines, put them at half coordinates ( 10.5 ). Geometry Complex shapes are path geometries , built from lines and curves once and drawn many times: cpp-norun ComPtr<ID2D1PathGeometry path; g_factory- CreatePathGeometry(&path); ComPtr<ID2D1GeometrySink sink; path- Open(&sink); sink- BeginFigure(D2D1::Point2F(0, 0), D2D1_FIGURE_BEGIN_FILLED); sink- AddLine(D2D1::Point2F(40, 0)); sink- AddBezier(D2D1::BezierSegment(D2D1::Point2F(60, 0), D2D1::Point2F(60, 40), D2D1::Point2F(40, 40))); sink- AddLine(D2D1::Point2F(0, 40)); sink- EndFigure(D2D1_FIGURE_END_CLOSED); sink- Close(); // m_target- FillGeometry(path.Get(), brush); geometries can also hit-test: path- FillContainsPoint(...) Transforms Every drawing call goes through the render target's transform , a 3 × 2 matrix ( D2D1::Matrix3x2F ). Draw a shape around the origin once, then place it anywhere: cpp-norun m_target- SetTransform(D2D1::Matrix3x2F::Rotation(angle, D2D1::Point2F(0, 0)) D2D1::Matrix3x2F::Translation(200, 150)); m_target- FillGeometry(path.Get(), m_brush.Get()); // rotated, then moved to (200, 150) m_target- SetTransform(D2D1::Matrix3x2F::Identity()); Order matters: with Direct2D's row-vector convention, A B means "first A, then B". Rotating then translating spins the shape in place and moves it; translating then rotating swings it around the origin. Zooming and panning a whole drawing (a map, a diagram) is one scale-and-translate transform, and its inverse turns mouse positions back into drawing coordinates. The practice implements these matrices. Check yourself quiz ? Which Direct2D resources must be re-created when the device is lost? - The factory and every resource it has created - Path geometries and stroke styles, but not brushes + The render target and everything created from it, such as brushes - None: Direct2D re-creates them itself after D2DERR_RECREATE_TARGET Those are the device-dependent resources, bitmaps included. Geometries are device-independent and survive; on D2DERR_RECREATE_TARGET you release the render target and its resources and let the next paint re-create them. ? Why does SetDpi on the render target simplify high-DPI support? - It makes Windows stretch the drawing like a DPI-unaware program + Drawing is then in device-independent pixels, and Direct2D scales to the monitor's DPI - It turns every float coordinate into a whole pixel - It changes the monitor's scaling to 100 % while the program draws One DIP is 1/96 inch, so you draw at 96-DPI sizes and Direct2D does lesson 3.04's arithmetic, without the blur of stretching. ? What does the matrix product Rotation Translation mean in Direct2D? - Translate first, then rotate, so the shape swings around the origin - The order does not matter: matrix products are commutative + Rotate first, then translate, because Direct2D multiplies row vectors from the left - Rotate and translate at the same time, around the shape's centre With the row-vector convention A B means "first A, then B", so the shape spins in place and then moves. Matrix products are not commutative.

title: Direct2D's matrices
body: Write D2D1::Matrix3x2F yourself. A point (x, y) is a row vector transformed as x' = x·m11 + y·m21 + dx , y' = x·m12 + y·m22 + dy : cpp struct Point { float x, y; }; struct Matrix { float m11, m12, m21, m22, dx, dy; }; Matrix identity(); Matrix translation(float x, float y); Matrix scale(float sx, float sy, Point centre); Matrix rotation(float degrees, Point centre); // clockwise on screen (y points down), like Direct2D Matrix multiply(const Matrix& a, const Matrix& b); // a b: first a, then b Point apply(const Matrix& m, Point p); bool invert(const Matrix& m, Matrix& out); // false if not invertible Matrix zoomAt(const Matrix& view, float factor, Point screenPoint); - scale and rotation about a centre are: translate the centre to the origin, scale or rotate, translate back. - rotation by a degrees about the origin is m11 = cos a, m12 = sin a, m21 = -sin a, m22 = cos a . - zoomAt : view maps drawing coordinates to the screen. Return a view that is also scaled by factor around screenPoint , so the drawing point under screenPoint stays there.

title: 4.03  Text with DirectWrite
body: DirectWrite lays out and renders text with proper font fallback, ligatures, colour emoji and ClearType. This lesson creates text formats and layouts, draws them with Direct2D, measures them, and uses hit-testing to place a caret and select text with the mouse. Why not just DrawText? GDI's DrawTextW handles simple text, but modern text needs more: font fallback (a Latin font does not contain Chinese characters or emoji, so another font must be found for them), shaping (Arabic letters change form, "fi" can become one ligature), colour emoji, and subpixel positioning. DirectWrite does all of that and draws through Direct2D. Formats and layouts cpp-norun include <dwrite.h pragma comment(lib, "dwrite.lib") ComPtr<IDWriteFactory dw; DWriteCreateFactory(DWRITE_FACTORY_TYPE_SHARED, __uuidof(IDWriteFactory), reinterpret_cast<IUnknown (dw.GetAddressOf())); ComPtr<IDWriteTextFormat format; // font, size, style: like a CSS class dw- CreateTextFormat(L"Segoe UI", nullptr, DWRITE_FONT_WEIGHT_NORMAL, DWRITE_FONT_STYLE_NORMAL, DWRITE_FONT_STRETCH_NORMAL, 14.0f / DIPs /, L"en-us", &format); format- SetWordWrapping(DWRITE_WORD_WRAPPING_WRAP); A text format describes how text should look. A text layout is a particular string laid out in a particular box: line breaks done, every glyph positioned. Create the layout when the text or the width changes, then draw and query it as often as needed: cpp-norun ComPtr<IDWriteTextLayout layout; dw- CreateTextLayout(m_text.c_str(), UINT32(m_text.size()), format.Get(), width, height, &layout); layout- SetFontWeight(DWRITE_FONT_WEIGHT_BOLD, DWRITE_TEXT_RANGE{ 0, 5 }); // formatting for a range m_target- DrawTextLayout(D2D1::Point2F(10, 10), layout.Get(), m_textBrush.Get()); For one-off labels, m_target- DrawText(text, length, format, rect, brush) creates a temporary layout internally. Measuring cpp-norun DWRITE_TEXT_METRICS m; layout- GetMetrics(&m); // m.width, m.height: the size actually used; m.lineCount GetMetrics is how a control sizes itself to its text, or a label is centred. GetLineMetrics gives each line's length (in UTF-16 units) and height. Hit-testing: from a point to text and back An editor needs two conversions: - Where is the caret? From a text position to a point: HitTestTextPosition(index, isTrailing, &x, &y, &metrics) . - Where did the user click? From a point to a text position: HitTestPoint(x, y, &isTrailing, &isInside, &metrics) ; metrics.textPosition plus 1 if isTrailing is the caret index. "Trailing" means the click was on the right half of a character, so the caret goes after it. Text positions are UTF-16 indices, so a caret must never land between the two halves of a surrogate pair (lesson 1.02): DirectWrite's hit-testing respects clusters for you. A selection is drawn by asking for the rectangles covering a range, one per line, with HitTestTextRange , and filling them before drawing the text. The practice computes exactly these: caret positions, hit-testing and selection rectangles, from the widths of the characters. Font fallback and emoji DirectWrite chooses fallback fonts automatically. For colour emoji, pass D2D1_DRAW_TEXT_OPTIONS_ENABLE_COLOR_FONT to DrawTextLayout (on a render target that supports it, such as an ID2D1DeviceContext ). Text in right-to-left scripts needs SetReadingDirection ; DirectWrite then handles mixed-direction lines. Rendering quality m_target- SetTextAntialiasMode(D2D1_TEXT_ANTIALIAS_MODE_CLEARTYPE) gives ClearType on opaque backgrounds; on transparent or animated surfaces use GRAYSCALE . Snap the text's origin to whole DIPs for the sharpest result. Check yourself quiz ? What is the difference between a text format and a text layout? + A format describes how text looks; a layout is one string laid out in a box - A format is for drawing with GDI and a layout is for Direct2D - A layout describes the font; a format holds the string and its line breaks - They are the same object under two names, kept for history Like a CSS class, a format holds font, size and style; the layout has the line breaks done and every glyph positioned, so you can measure and hit-test it. ? What does "trailing" mean in a hit-test result? - The point is past the end of the whole text - The point is below the last line + The point is on the right half of the character - The character is the second half of a surrogate pair On the left half the caret goes before the character; on the right half (trailing) it goes after it. ? Why should text layouts be cached? - A layout can only be drawn once and must be kept to draw it again + Laying text out is expensive; it only needs redoing when the text, format or box size changes - Layouts are device-dependent and are lost with the render target - DirectWrite limits each program to a few layouts Create the layout when the text or width changes, then draw and query it as often as needed. Layouts are not GPU resources, so device loss does not affect them.

title: Carets, clicks and selections
body: Write a small text layout like DirectWrite's, from the width of each character, with the hit-testing an editor needs: cpp struct Caret { float x, y; }; struct Box { float left, top, right, bottom; }; class TextLayout { public: TextLayout(std::string text, std::vector<float widths, float maxWidth, float lineHeight); int lineCount() const; int lineStart(int line) const; Caret caretAt(int index) const; // 0 .. text.size() int hitTest(float x, float y) const; // the caret index nearest to the point std::vector<Box selection(int start, int end) const; // one box per line, start < end }; Line breaking : widths i is the width of character i . Lines break only after a space: the line takes as many whole words (with the space after each) as fit within maxWidth , where the trailing spaces do not count towards the width. A word wider than maxWidth alone is broken at the last character that fits (at least one character per line). \n always ends a line (it belongs to the line it ends and has no width). Carets : the caret before character i is at the sum of the widths before it on its line, at y = line × lineHeight . The index at the very start of a line belongs to that line (so the end of a wrapped line and the start of the next line is the same index, shown at the start of the next line); the end of the text is on the last line. hitTest : clamp y to a line ( floor(y / lineHeight) , limited to existing lines), then find the caret position on that line nearest to x : inside a character, the left half gives the index before it, the right half the index after it (a "trailing" hit). Points left of the line give its start; points right of it give its end (before a \n , or for a wrapped line, the index after its last character that is not a trailing space). selection : for each line the range touches, a box from the caret x of the range's start on that line (or 0) to the caret x of the range's end on that line (or the line's full width, trailing spaces included), from line × lineHeight to (line + 1) × lineHeight .

title: 4.04  Images with WIC
body: The Windows Imaging Component decodes and encodes PNG, JPEG, GIF, TIFF and more. This lesson loads an image file, converts it to the pixel format Direct2D wants, draws it scaled with good quality, makes thumbnails, and explains premultiplied alpha. WIC WIC (Windows Imaging Component) is the system's image codec library: PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, TIFF, ICO, HEIF and WebP (with the store extensions), and camera RAW formats. Like Direct2D it is COM: cpp-norun include <wincodec.h pragma comment(lib, "windowscodecs.lib") ComPtr<IWICImagingFactory wic; CoCreateInstance(CLSID_WICImagingFactory, nullptr, CLSCTX_INPROC_SERVER, IID_PPV_ARGS(&wic)); Loading an image for Direct2D cpp-norun HRESULT loadBitmap(ID2D1RenderTarget target, const wchar_t path, ComPtr<ID2D1Bitmap & out) { ComPtr<IWICBitmapDecoder decoder; HRESULT hr = wic- CreateDecoderFromFilename(path, nullptr, GENERIC_READ, WICDecodeMetadataCacheOnDemand, &decoder); ComPtr<IWICBitmapFrameDecode frame; if (SUCCEEDED(hr)) hr = decoder- GetFrame(0, &frame); // GIF and TIFF can have several frames ComPtr<IWICFormatConverter converter; if (SUCCEEDED(hr)) hr = wic- CreateFormatConverter(&converter); if (SUCCEEDED(hr)) hr = converter- Initialize(frame.Get(), GUID_WICPixelFormat32bppPBGRA, WICBitmapDitherTypeNone, nullptr, 0.0, WICBitmapPaletteTypeMedianCut); if (SUCCEEDED(hr)) hr = target- CreateBitmapFromWicBitmap(converter.Get(), nullptr, out.ReleaseAndGetAddressOf()); return hr; } The decoder reads the file's format from its contents, not its extension. The format converter turns whatever the file contains (8-bit palette, 24-bit RGB, 48-bit, CMYK) into the one format Direct2D draws directly: 32bppPBGRA , 8 bits each of blue, green, red and alpha, with alpha premultiplied . The ID2D1Bitmap is a device-dependent resource (lesson 4.02): keep the decoded WIC data, or the path, so it can be re-created after a device loss. Premultiplied alpha In straight alpha, a pixel stores its colour and, separately, how opaque it is: half-transparent red is (255, 0, 0, 128) . In premultiplied alpha, the colour channels are already multiplied by the alpha: the same pixel is (128, 0, 0, 128) . Premultiplied is what GPUs prefer, for two reasons: blending becomes one multiply-add ( result = source + destination × (1 - source alpha) ), and filtering (scaling, blurring) mixes neighbouring pixels correctly; with straight alpha, a fully transparent pixel's "invisible" colour bleeds into the edges as dark or coloured fringes. The practice converts between the two and blends. Drawing scaled cpp-norun const D2D1_SIZE_F size = bitmap- GetSize(); const D2D1_RECT_F dest = fitInto(size, box); // keep the aspect ratio m_target- DrawBitmap(bitmap.Get(), dest, 1.0f, D2D1_BITMAP_INTERPOLATION_MODE_LINEAR); Fitting ("contain") scales the image to the largest size that fits inside the box with the same aspect ratio, leaving bars; filling ("cover") scales it so it covers the box, cropping the overflow. Image viewers use fit; thumbnails in a grid often use fill. For pixel art, use NEAREST_NEIGHBOR interpolation; for photos, linear. Shrinking a large photo to a small thumbnail with plain linear filtering looks grainy, because each output pixel samples only a few input pixels. Make thumbnails with WIC's scaler instead ( IWICBitmapScaler with WICBitmapInterpolationModeFant or HighQualityCubic ), which averages all the input pixels; many cameras' JPEGs also contain a ready-made thumbnail ( GetThumbnail ). Saving Encoding is the reverse: create an encoder for a container format ( GUID_ContainerFormatPng ), initialise it on a stream, create a frame, set its size and pixel format, write the pixels and commit. Screenshots of a Direct2D drawing are made by drawing into a WIC bitmap render target ( CreateWicBitmapRenderTarget ) and encoding that. Orientation Phones store photos sideways and record the intended orientation in the EXIF metadata. Read it from the frame's metadata ( /app1/ifd/{ushort=274} for JPEG) and rotate with IWICBitmapFlipRotator , or photos show up sideways. Check yourself quiz ? Why convert images to 32bppPBGRA? - It is the format PNG files store their pixels in on disk - It makes the image file smaller when it is saved again + It is the pixel format Direct2D draws directly, with premultiplied alpha - It removes the alpha channel, which Direct2D cannot draw It is 8-bit blue, green, red and premultiplied alpha. Files hold all kinds of formats (palettes, 24-bit, 48-bit, CMYK); the format converter turns them into the one Direct2D wants. ? What does premultiplied alpha store? - The alpha already multiplied by the colour channels, so alpha is always 255 - The colour and, separately, how opaque the pixel is - Only the alpha; the colour is computed when blending + The colour channels already multiplied by the alpha, which makes blending and filtering correct and fast Half-transparent red is (128, 0, 0, 128) premultiplied and (255, 0, 0, 128) straight. Storing colour and opacity separately is straight alpha. ? What is the difference between fitting and filling an image into a box? - Fitting stretches the image to the box; filling keeps its aspect ratio + Fitting shows the whole image with bars; filling covers the box and crops - Fitting crops the image to the box; filling adds bars around it - Fitting uses nearest-neighbour interpolation, filling uses linear Both keep the aspect ratio. Image viewers fit ("contain"); grid thumbnails often fill ("cover").

title: Pixels and alpha
body: Work with 32-bit BGRA pixels like WIC and Direct2D do: cpp struct Pixel { std::uint8_t b, g, r, a; }; struct RectF { float left, top, right, bottom; }; Pixel premultiply(Pixel straight); // c a / 255, rounded to nearest Pixel unpremultiply(Pixel p); // c 255 / a, rounded to nearest, capped at 255; a == 0 gives all zero Pixel over(Pixel src, Pixel dst); // premultiplied "source over": src + dst (255 - src.a) / 255, rounded RectF fit(float w, float h, RectF box); // contain: largest same-shape rectangle inside box, centred RectF fill(float w, float h, RectF box); // cover: smallest same-shape rectangle covering box, centred std::vector<Pixel halve(const std::vector<Pixel & image, int w, int h); // 2x2 box filter; w and h even Rounding to nearest for integer division by d : (x + d / 2) / d . halve averages each 2 × 2 block channel by channel (premultiplied pixels, so alpha is averaged like the others), rounding to nearest: (sum + 2) / 4 .

title: A line chart's geometry
body: Write everything a Direct2D line chart computes before it draws: round-number axis ticks, the mapping between data and screen (with y pointing up for data and down on screen), the data point nearest the mouse for a tooltip, and a simplified polyline so thousands of points draw quickly. The drawing itself is then a few DrawLine and DrawText calls. cpp struct Point { double x, y; }; std::vector<double niceTicks(double lo, double hi, int maxTicks); std::string tickLabel(double v); class Chart { public: Chart(std::vector<Point data, double width, double height, double margin); // data sorted by x, at least one point const std::vector<double & yTicks() const; Point toScreen(Point p) const; Point toData(Point s) const; int nearestIndex(double screenX) const; std::vector<Point polyline(double tolerance) const; }; niceTicks uses Heckbert's "nice numbers". nice(x, round) writes x = f × 10^e with 1 <= f < 10 ; rounded, f becomes 1 if below 1.5, 2 if below 3, 5 if below 7, else 10; not rounded, 1 if at most 1, 2 if at most 2, 5 if at most 5, else 10. Then: - range = nice(hi - lo, false) , step = nice(range / (maxTicks - 1), true) ; - the ticks run from floor(lo / step) × step to ceil(hi / step) × step in steps of step ; compute the k-th tick as k × step (not by adding repeatedly) to avoid drift. - If hi <= lo , use hi = lo + 1 . tickLabel prints with up to 6 decimals and no trailing zeros or trailing dot; a value that prints as -0 is 0 . Chart : the plot area runs from margin to width - margin and from margin to height - margin . The x range is the data's smallest to largest x (if they are equal, every point is at the centre of the plot horizontally). The y range is from the first to the last of niceTicks(min y, max y, 6) , which are also yTicks() . Data y grows upwards: the lowest tick is at the bottom of the plot area. nearestIndex returns the index of the data point whose x is nearest to the data x under screenX (binary search; on a tie, the lower index). polyline returns the data as screen points simplified with the Ramer-Douglas-Peucker algorithm: keep the first and last points; find the point between them farthest from the line through them (perpendicular distance, in pixels); if it is farther than tolerance , keep it and simplify the two halves the same way, otherwise drop everything in between.

title: 5.01  Files and Directories
body:
Reading and writing files with CreateFileW, sharing modes and why "the file is in use", listing directories with FindFirstFileW, Windows paths and their traps (drive letters, UNC, long paths, reserved names), known folders, and watching a folder for changes. CreateFileW CreateFileW opens (or creates) files, and also pipes, devices and directories: cpp-norun HANDLE h = CreateFileW(L"C:\Notes\today.txt", GENERIC_READ, // what we want to do FILE_SHARE_READ, // what others may do while we have it open nullptr, OPEN_EXISTING, // what to do if it exists / does not exist FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL, nullptr); if (h == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) { / GetLastError: 2 not found, 5 access denied, 32 in use / } LARGE_INTEGER size; GetFileSizeEx(h, &size); std::string data(static_cast<size_t (size.QuadPart), '\0'); DWORD read = 0; ReadFile(h, data.data(), static_cast<DWORD (data.size()), &read, nullptr); CloseHandle(h); Creation If the file exists If not --- --- --- CREATE_NEW Fails (80) Creates CREATE_ALWAYS Truncates to empty Creates OPEN_EXISTING Opens Fails (2) OPEN_ALWAYS Opens Creates TRUNCATE_EXISTING Truncates Fails For ordinary reading and writing, std::ifstream , std::ofstream and std::filesystem work fine on Windows (with std::filesystem::path holding wide strings). CreateFileW is for the cases they do not cover: share modes, overlapped (asynchronous) I/O, file attributes, and opening directories. Sharing and "the file is in use" The share mode says what other programs may do with the file while you have it open. Windows enforces it: if you open a file without FILE_SHARE_WRITE , nobody else can open it for writing, and they get error 32, ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION . That is the "file is open in another program" message. An editor that keeps files open blocks other programs; good editors read the file and close it straight away. Antivirus scanners and backup tools often open files briefly, so a save that fails with a sharing violation should be retried a few times with a short delay before giving up. Saving safely The pattern from the raylib course's saves applies here, with Windows functions: write to a temporary file in the same folder, then ReplaceFileW (which also keeps the original's attributes and permissions) or MoveFileExW(temp, target, MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH) . Listing a directory cpp-norun WIN32_FIND_DATAW fd; HANDLE find = FindFirstFileExW(L"C:\Notes\ ", FindExInfoBasic, &fd, FindExSearchNameMatch, nullptr, FIND_FIRST_EX_LARGE_FETCH); if (find != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) { do { if (wcscmp(fd.cFileName, L".") == 0 wcscmp(fd.cFileName, L"..") == 0) continue; const bool isDir = fd.dwFileAttributes & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DIRECTORY; const ULONGLONG size = (ULONGLONG(fd.nFileSizeHigh) << 32) fd.nFileSizeLow; // ... } while (FindNextFileW(find, &fd)); FindClose(find); // not CloseHandle } Every directory lists . and .. , which must be skipped or a recursive search loops forever. Also skip directories with FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT when recursing: junctions and symbolic links can point back up the tree. Paths Windows paths have more forms than people expect: Form Example --- --- Drive absolute C:\Users\Sam
otes.txt Drive relative (current directory of that drive) C:notes.txt Root relative (current drive) \Users\Sam Relative ..
otes.txt UNC (network) \server\share older ile.txt Long-path prefix \?\C:\very\long\path... Both \ and / work as separators in most APIs; . and .. are resolved by the system. Names are case-insensitive (but case-preserving). The classic MAX_PATH limit is 260 characters; longer paths need the \?\ prefix or the longPathAware manifest setting. The reserved names CON , NUL , COM1 and so on (practice 3.01) cannot be used as file names in any folder. Combining and normalising paths correctly (joining with exactly one separator, resolving .. without going above the root, keeping UNC roots intact) is the practice. Known folders Never hard-code C:\Users\... or Documents : the folder can be redirected, renamed in another language, or on another drive. Ask the system: cpp-norun PWSTR path = nullptr; if (SUCCEEDED(SHGetKnownFolderPath(FOLDERID_RoamingAppData, 0, nullptr, &path))) { std::filesystem::path settings = std::filesystem::path(path) / L"Xenon"; CoTaskMemFree(path); } FOLDERID_RoamingAppData (settings), FOLDERID_LocalAppData (caches, large data), FOLDERID_Documents (the user's documents), FOLDERID_Downloads . Watching for changes An editor should notice when the open file changes on disk; a file list should refresh when files are added. ReadDirectoryChangesW reports each change (added, removed, modified, renamed) in a folder, optionally with its subfolders. Use it on a worker thread or with overlapped I/O, and expect bursts: one save in another editor can produce several notifications, so wait a moment and re-check rather than reloading on every one. Check yourself quiz ? What does error 32 mean, and what should a program do about it? - The file does not exist; create it and then try again - The program lacks permission; ask the user to run it as administrator + A sharing violation: another program has it open; retry briefly - The disk is full; report it to the user straight away Error 32 is ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION . Scanners and backup tools often hold files for a moment, so a few short retries before reporting it usually succeed. "Not found" is error 2 and "access denied" is error 5. ? Why must a recursive directory search skip . , .. and reparse points? + They lead back to the folder or up the tree, so the search never ends - They are hidden system entries that FindNextFileW cannot open - They only appear on network drives and slow the search down - Opening them needs administrator rights, so the search would fail . is the folder itself, .. its parent, and junctions or symbolic links can point back up the tree. Following any of them makes the search revisit folders without end. ? Why use SHGetKnownFolderPath instead of building paths like C:\Users
ame\Documents ? - It is faster than reading the user's name and joining the path - Hard-coded paths do not work with W functions such as CreateFileW - Only the paths it returns are allowed to be longer than MAX_PATH + Known folders can be redirected or renamed; the system knows where they are The Documents folder may be on another drive, redirected to a network share or named differently in another language, so only the system can say where it is.

title: Windows paths
body: Write the path handling of lesson 5.01 (on std::string , with \ as the separator; / is accepted as one too): cpp std::string pathRoot(const std::string& path); // "C:\", "C:", "\", "\\server\share\" or "" bool isAbsolute(const std::string& path); // "C:\..." or "\\server\share..." std::string normalize(const std::string& path); std::string join(const std::string& base, const std::string& more); std::string withLongPrefix(const std::string& path); - pathRoot : C:\x → C:\ (drive absolute), C:x → C: (drive relative), \x → \ (root relative), \\server\share\x → \\server\share\ , a relative path → "" . Drive letters may be either case; returned roots use \ . - normalize : turn / into \ , collapse repeated separators (except the two at the start of a UNC root), remove . parts, and let .. remove the previous part; a .. that would go above the root is dropped when there is a root, and kept for a relative path ( ..\..\x stays). A trailing separator is removed, except for the root itself. An empty result of a relative path is "." . - join : if more has any root ( pathRoot(more) is not empty), it replaces base ... except a root-relative more ( \x ) keeps base 's drive ( C:\a + \x = C:\x ). Otherwise base + "\" + more . The result is normalized. - withLongPrefix : paths of 260 characters or more get \\?\ ( \\?\C:\... ), and UNC paths get \\?\UNC\server\share\... ; shorter paths and relative paths are returned unchanged. Normalize first.

title: 5.02  The Registry and Settings
body: The registry is Windows' hierarchical settings database. This lesson explains its structure, the per-user and per-machine hives, reading and writing values with RegGetValueW and RegSetValueExW, value types, and when a settings file in AppData is the better choice. Keys, values and hives The registry is a tree. Keys are like folders and contain subkeys and values ; each value has a name, a type and data. The roots are hives : Root Holds Writable by a normal program --- --- --- HKEY_CURRENT_USER (HKCU) The current user's settings Yes HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE (HKLM) Settings for all users, installed programs, drivers No (needs administrator) HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT File associations and COM classes (a merged view of HKCU and HKLM) Through HKCU A program's own settings go under HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\<Company \<Program . Writing to HKLM from a normal program fails with "access denied", which is how it should be: the installer (lesson 6.02) writes machine-wide keys once, with administrator rights. Value types Type Holds --- --- REG_SZ A string (UTF-16, null-terminated) REG_EXPAND_SZ A string with %VARIABLES% to expand REG_MULTI_SZ A list of strings, each null-terminated, with an extra null at the end REG_DWORD A 32-bit number REG_QWORD A 64-bit number REG_BINARY Raw bytes Reading RegGetValueW reads a value in one call, checks its type, and guarantees string termination: cpp-norun DWORD readDword(const wchar_t name, DWORD fallback) { DWORD value = 0, size = sizeof(value); const LSTATUS st = RegGetValueW(HKEY_CURRENT_USER, L"Software\\Xenon\\Notes", name, RRF_RT_REG_DWORD, nullptr, &value, &size); return st == ERROR_SUCCESS ? value : fallback; } std::wstring readString(const wchar_t name, const std::wstring& fallback) { DWORD bytes = 0; if (RegGetValueW(HKEY_CURRENT_USER, L"Software\\Xenon\\Notes", name, RRF_RT_REG_SZ, nullptr, nullptr, &bytes) != ERROR_SUCCESS) return fallback; std::wstring s(bytes / sizeof(wchar_t), L'\0'); if (RegGetValueW(HKEY_CURRENT_USER, L"Software\\Xenon\\Notes", name, RRF_RT_REG_SZ, nullptr, s.data(), &bytes) != ERROR_SUCCESS) return fallback; s.resize(bytes / sizeof(wchar_t) - 1); // drop the terminating null return s; } Registry functions return the error code directly (an LSTATUS ) instead of setting GetLastError . A missing value ( ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND ) is normal on first run: use the default, exactly like lesson 6.01's settings file in the raylib course. Writing cpp-norun HKEY key; if (RegCreateKeyExW(HKEY_CURRENT_USER, L"Software\\Xenon\\Notes", 0, nullptr, 0, KEY_SET_VALUE, nullptr, &key, nullptr) == ERROR_SUCCESS) { const DWORD wrap = 1; RegSetValueExW(key, L"WordWrap", 0, REG_DWORD, reinterpret_cast<const BYTE (&wrap), sizeof(wrap)); const std::wstring font = L"Cascadia Mono"; RegSetValueExW(key, L"Font", 0, REG_SZ, reinterpret_cast<const BYTE (font.c_str()), static_cast<DWORD ((font.size() + 1) sizeof(wchar_t))); // size in BYTES, including the null RegCloseKey(key); } The size of a REG_SZ is in bytes and includes the terminating null: passing the character count is the most common registry bug, and stores half the string. Registry or file? Registry Settings file in AppData --- --- Built in, typed values, atomic per value Easy to back up, copy, diff and edit Needed for file associations, autostart, COM Works the same on every platform Awkward for large or structured data Any structure (JSON, TOML, INI) Left behind if uninstall forgets it Deleting the folder removes everything A good rule: use the registry for what Windows itself reads (file associations, "open with", uninstall information, autostart under ...\CurrentVersion\Run ), and a file in %APPDATA% for your program's own preferences. Watching settings RegNotifyChangeKeyValue signals an event when a key changes, which is how a program notices that the user switched the system to dark mode: the setting AppsUseLightTheme under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Personalize changes, and top-level windows also receive WM_SETTINGCHANGE . Check yourself quiz ? Why should a program write its own settings to HKEY_CURRENT_USER , not HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE ? - HKLM is read-only for every program, including installers + HKLM is shared by all users and needs administrator rights to write - HKCU is faster because it is always kept in memory - Values in HKLM are deleted when the user signs out A normal program writing to HKLM gets "access denied", as it should. The installer writes machine-wide keys once with administrator rights; the program's preferences go under HKCU\Software\<Company \<Program . ? What size do you pass to RegSetValueExW for a REG_SZ string font ? - The number of characters, font.size() - The number of characters plus one, for the terminating null - The size in bytes without the null, font.size() sizeof(wchar_t) + The size in bytes including the terminating null, (font.size() + 1) sizeof(wchar_t) The size is always in bytes and includes the null. Passing the character count is the most common registry bug and stores only half of a UTF-16 string. ? How do registry functions such as RegGetValueW report errors? - They return FALSE , and you call GetLastError for the code + They return the error code (an LSTATUS ) directly - They throw a C++ exception - They return INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE Registry functions return the code itself, ERROR_SUCCESS or for example ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND , instead of setting GetLastError . A missing value on first run is normal: use the default.

title: A little registry
body: Write an in-memory model of the registry API from lesson 5.02, with its real error codes: cpp constexpr long ERROR_SUCCESS = 0, ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND = 2, ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPE = 1630; enum class Type { String, Dword, MultiString }; class Registry { public: long setString(const std::string& key, const std::string& name, const std::string& value); long setDword(const std::string& key, const std::string& name, std::uint32_t value); long setMulti(const std::string& key, const std::string& name, const std::vector<std::string & values); long getString(const std::string& key, const std::string& name, std::string& out) const; long getDword(const std::string& key, const std::string& name, std::uint32_t& out) const; long getMulti(const std::string& key, const std::string& name, std::vector<std::string & out) const; long deleteValue(const std::string& key, const std::string& name); long deleteTree(const std::string& key); std::vector<std::string subkeys(const std::string& key) const; }; std::string encodeMulti(const std::vector<std::string & values); // REG_MULTI_SZ bytes (one byte per character) std::vector<std::string decodeMulti(const std::string& data); - Keys are paths like Software\Xenon\Notes ; key and value names are case-insensitive but keep the case they were first created with. Setting a value creates the key and all its parents. - Reading a value that is missing, or from a key that does not exist, is ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND ; reading with the wrong type is ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPE (and out is left unchanged in both cases). - Setting a value of another type replaces it. - deleteTree removes a key with all its subkeys ( ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND if it does not exist). subkeys lists the direct subkeys of a key in their stored case, sorted ignoring case (an unknown key has none). - encodeMulti : each string followed by a null, then one more null; an empty list is two nulls. Empty strings cannot be stored in a multi-string (they would end it early), so they are skipped. decodeMulti reads up to the first empty string.

title: 5.03  Processes
body: Starting other programs from yours - CreateProcessW and its mutable command line, quoting arguments correctly, waiting for a child and reading its exit code, capturing its output through pipes, and opening documents with ShellExecuteExW. CreateProcessW Programs often run other programs: an editor runs a compiler, a launcher runs a game, a tool runs git . The base function is CreateProcessW : cpp-norun std::wstring commandLine = L"\"C:\\Tools\\formatter.exe\" --in-place \"C:\\My Notes\\today.md\""; STARTUPINFOW si{ sizeof(si) }; PROCESS_INFORMATION pi{}; if (!CreateProcessW(nullptr, commandLine.data(), // MUTABLE buffer: CreateProcessW may write to it nullptr, nullptr, FALSE, CREATE_NO_WINDOW, nullptr, nullptr, &si, &pi)) { const DWORD error = GetLastError(); // 2: program not found } else { WaitForSingleObject(pi.hProcess, INFINITE); DWORD exitCode = 0; GetExitCodeProcess(pi.hProcess, &exitCode); // 0 usually means success CloseHandle(pi.hThread); CloseHandle(pi.hProcess); } Things that surprise everyone: - The command line must be a writable buffer; passing a string literal crashes. - pi returns two handles, the process and its main thread, and both must be closed. - Waiting with INFINITE on the UI thread freezes the window until the child ends. Wait on a worker thread (lesson 5.04), or register a callback with RegisterWaitForSingleObject . - CREATE_NO_WINDOW stops a console program from flashing up a black console window. Quoting arguments On Windows, a program receives its command line as one string , and each program splits it into arguments itself (the C runtime and CommandLineToArgvW follow the same rules). So the caller must quote arguments so that they split back correctly: - An argument with spaces or tabs (or an empty argument) must be wrapped in double quotes. - A " inside an argument is written as \" . - Backslashes are literal, except before a " : then each backslash must be doubled. So C:\My Folder\ as one argument is written "C:\My Folder\\" : otherwise the final \" would be read as an escaped quote and swallow the rest of the line. Getting this wrong makes paths with spaces fail, and, worse, lets an argument containing quotes inject extra arguments. The practice writes both the splitting and the quoting functions, and checks that one undoes the other. Capturing output To read what a console program prints, give it a pipe as its standard output: cpp-norun SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES sa{ sizeof(sa), nullptr, TRUE }; // TRUE: the handle can be inherited HANDLE readEnd, writeEnd; CreatePipe(&readEnd, &writeEnd, &sa, 0); SetHandleInformation(readEnd, HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT, 0); // the child gets only the write end STARTUPINFOW si{ sizeof(si) }; si.dwFlags = STARTF_USESTDHANDLES; si.hStdOutput = writeEnd; si.hStdError = writeEnd; si.hStdInput = GetStdHandle(STD_INPUT_HANDLE); CreateProcessW(nullptr, cmd.data(), nullptr, nullptr, TRUE / inherit /, CREATE_NO_WINDOW, nullptr, nullptr, &si, &pi); CloseHandle(writeEnd); // our copy: otherwise ReadFile never sees the end char buffer 4096 ; DWORD n; std::string output; while (ReadFile(readEnd, buffer, sizeof(buffer), &n, nullptr) && n 0) output.append(buffer, n); Closing our copy of the write end is essential: the pipe only reports end-of-file when every write handle is closed, and if we keep one, the read loop waits forever after the child exits. If the child can also wait on input, or output is very large, read on a separate thread so neither side blocks the other. Console programs usually print in the console's code page or UTF-8; decode the bytes with lesson 1.02's conversion and normalise \r\n . Opening documents To open a file with the user's default program ("open this PDF", "show this folder"), do not start a specific .exe : let the shell decide. cpp-norun SHELLEXECUTEINFOW sei{ sizeof(sei) }; sei.fMask = SEE_MASK_NOASYNC; sei.lpVerb = L"open"; // or "edit", "print"; nullptr = the default verb sei.lpFile = L"C:\\Notes\\report.pdf"; sei.nShow = SW_SHOWNORMAL; ShellExecuteExW(&sei); Opening a web page is the same call with a URL. To show a file selected in Explorer, run explorer.exe /select,"path" or use SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems . Your own process GetCommandLineW and CommandLineToArgvW give your program's own arguments; GetModuleFileNameW(nullptr, ...) its own .exe path; ExitProcess ends it (prefer returning from wWinMain ). A job object groups child processes so they are all ended when your program exits, which keeps helper processes from being left behind. Check yourself quiz ? Why must CreateProcessW 's command line be a writable buffer? - The function writes the child's exit code into it + It may write into the buffer, and a string literal is read-only - Windows frees the buffer when the child process ends - It lets the child process change its own arguments later CreateProcessW may write into the command line while splitting off the program name, so a literal makes it crash. Pass commandLine.data() of a std::wstring . ? How is the single argument C:\My Folder\ written on a command line? - C:\My Folder\ with no quotes, because backslashes are literal - "C:\My Folder\" - "C:\\My Folder\\" , doubling every backslash + "C:\My Folder\\" , doubling only the backslash before the closing quote It contains a space, so it needs quotes. Backslashes are literal except before a " , so only the trailing one is doubled; a lone \" would be read as an escaped quote and swallow the rest of the line. ? Why must the parent close its own copy of the pipe's write end after starting the child? - The child cannot write to the pipe while the parent holds the write end - Otherwise the child's output appears twice in the pipe - An open write end makes CreateProcessW fail + End-of-file only comes once every write handle is closed ReadFile reports the end only when no write handle is left. If the parent keeps one, the loop waits forever after the child has exited.

title: Splitting and quoting command lines
body: Write both halves of lesson 5.03's quoting rules, so that a program you start receives exactly the arguments you meant: cpp std::vector<std::string splitCommandLine(const std::string& line); std::string quoteArgument(const std::string& arg); std::string buildCommandLine(const std::vector<std::string & args); splitCommandLine follows the C runtime's rules: - Spaces and tabs outside quotes separate arguments (several in a row count as one); they are not part of any argument. - A " switches quoting on or off and is not part of the argument. An argument can be partly quoted: a" b"c is one argument, a bc . "" alone is an empty argument. - Backslashes are literal, except directly before a " : then 2n backslashes become n backslashes and the " switches quoting; 2n + 1 backslashes become n backslashes and a literal " . quoteArgument returns the argument unchanged if it is not empty and contains no space, tab or " . Otherwise it wraps it in quotes, writing each " as \" with the backslashes before it doubled, and doubling the backslashes at the very end (before the closing quote). buildCommandLine quotes each argument and joins them with single spaces. For every list of arguments, splitCommandLine(buildCommandLine(args)) == args .

title: 5.04  Threads and Synchronisation
body: Keeping the interface responsive while long work runs - worker threads, posting results back to the UI thread, protecting shared data with SRW locks and critical sections, events and condition variables, cancellation, and the thread pool. The UI thread must not block All of a window's messages are processed on the thread that created it. While a message handler runs, that thread cannot paint, react to input or even be moved. Anything slower than about 50 ms (reading a big file, searching a folder, a network request, waiting for a process) belongs on another thread. Starting a worker std::thread (or std::jthread , which joins automatically and supports stop requests) works on Windows; CreateThread is the raw API underneath. cpp-norun std::jthread m_worker; void startSearch(HWND hwnd, std::wstring folder, std::wstring pattern) { m_worker = std::jthread( hwnd, folder, pattern (std::stop_token stop) { std::vector<std::wstring found; searchFolder(folder, pattern, found, stop); // checks stop.stop_requested() often auto result = new std::vector<std::wstring (std::move(found)); if (!PostMessageW(hwnd, WM_APP_SEARCH_DONE, 0, reinterpret_cast<LPARAM (result))) delete result; // the window is gone }); } case WM_APP_SEARCH_DONE: { std::unique_ptr<std::vector<std::wstring result{ reinterpret_cast<std::vector<std::wstring (lParam) }; showResults( result); return 0; } The rules: - A worker never touches windows directly (no SetWindowTextW , no drawing). It posts a message, and the UI thread updates the window. PostMessageW is safe from any thread; SendMessageW to the UI thread can deadlock if the UI thread is waiting for the worker. - Data passed with the message must outlive the worker: allocate it, pass the pointer, and let the receiver own it. If PostMessageW fails (the window was destroyed), free it yourself. - Before the window is destroyed, stop and join the worker, so it does not post to a dead window or use freed data. Progress and cancellation Long work should report progress and be cancellable. Post a progress message now and then (at most every 50-100 ms, or the queue fills with thousands), and check a stop flag ( std::stop_token , or an std::atomic<bool ) between steps. Cancellation is cooperative: the worker must look at the flag; nothing stops a thread safely from outside. Shared data When two threads use the same data and at least one writes, the access must be synchronised , or the result is a data race: torn values, corrupted containers, crashes that appear once a week. Tool Use --- --- std::mutex / SRWLOCK Mutual exclusion: one thread at a time in a critical section SRWLOCK shared mode Many readers at once, or one writer CRITICAL_SECTION Older recursive lock; still common in existing code std::atomic<T A single value: flags, counters std::condition_variable / CONDITION_VARIABLE Wait until something becomes true Event ( CreateEventW ) A signal that can be waited on together with other handles cpp-norun SRWLOCK m_lock = SRWLOCK_INIT; std::vector<Result m_results; void add(Result r) { AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&m_lock); m_results.push_back(std::move(r)); ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&m_lock); } In C++, std::mutex with std::lock_guard (or std::scoped_lock ) does the same and cannot forget to unlock. Hold locks briefly, never call out to unknown code (or SendMessageW ) while holding one, and always take several locks in the same order, or two threads can deadlock each holding what the other needs. A work queue A common structure is one or more workers taking jobs from a queue : the UI thread pushes jobs, the workers pop them, and a condition variable wakes a worker when a job arrives. Stopping it cleanly means: set a "closing" flag, wake everyone, let the workers finish (or abandon) the queue, and join them. The practice builds such a queue; the file finder of milestone 6 uses it. The thread pool Starting a thread costs some time and memory (1 MB of stack reserved by default). For many small jobs, use the system thread pool : TrySubmitThreadpoolCallback , or the full CreateThreadpoolWork API, which runs callbacks on a set of threads Windows manages. std::async on MSVC also uses the pool. Waiting on several things WaitForMultipleObjects waits until one (or all) of several handles is signalled: processes ending, events set, timers expiring. In a UI thread, MsgWaitForMultipleObjectsEx waits for handles or new messages, so the window stays responsive while waiting. Check yourself quiz ? Why must a worker thread not call SetWindowTextW on the program's window? - SetWindowTextW only works inside the WM_PAINT handler + A window belongs to the thread that created it; post a message instead - Worker threads cannot call any Windows API function at all - It works the same, but is slower than posting a message A window's messages are processed on the thread that created it. The worker posts a message ( PostMessageW is safe from any thread) and the UI thread changes the window; sending to the UI thread can deadlock if it is waiting for the worker. ? A worker posts a new -allocated result to a window with the pointer in lParam . Who owns that data? - The worker, which deletes it right after PostMessageW returns - Nobody; Windows frees it once the message has been processed + The receiver frees it, unless PostMessageW fails and the worker must - The message queue, which copies the data and frees the copy PostMessageW only copies the pointer value. The receiver wraps it in a std::unique_ptr and frees it; if posting fails because the window is gone, nobody will receive it, so the sender deletes it. ? How do two threads deadlock with locks, and what prevents it? - They both read the same variable at once; std::atomic prevents it - One thread holds a lock for too long; a shorter critical section prevents it - They use different kinds of lock; using only std::mutex prevents it + Each holds one lock and waits for the lock the other holds; always taking locks in the same order prevents it Thread A holds lock 1 and waits for lock 2 while thread B holds lock 2 and waits for lock 1, so neither can continue. Taking several locks in one fixed order makes that cycle impossible.

title: A work queue
body: Write lesson 5.04's work queue, safe to use from several threads at once: cpp template <typename T class WorkQueue { public: bool push(T item); // false once the queue is closed std::optional<T pop(); // waits for an item; nullopt when closed and empty std::optional<T tryPop(); // never waits void close(); // no more pushes; waiting pops wake up std::size_t size() const; }; - Items come out in the order they went in. - After close , pop still returns the items that are left, and then nullopt without waiting. - Use a std::mutex and a std::condition_variable ; size must be safe to call from any thread too. The tests run real threads: several producers pushing numbers and several consumers adding them up.

title: Searching a folder tree
body: Write the search engine of the file finder (lesson 6.03): wildcard patterns that match like Windows, a recursive walk that skips . , .. and links, depth and size limits, and cancellation through a callback that the UI's stop button controls. The tree is given in memory here; in the real program it comes from FindFirstFileExW (lesson 5.01), and the walk runs on a worker thread (lesson 5.04). cpp struct Entry { std::string name; bool dir{ false }; std::uint64_t size{ 0 }; bool reparse{ false }; // a junction or symbolic link std::vector<Entry children; }; struct Options { std::string patterns; bool recurse{ true }; std::uint64_t minSize{ 0 }; bool includeDirs{ false }; int maxDepth{ -1 }; }; struct Found { std::string path; std::uint64_t size; bool dir; }; bool wildcardMatch(const std::string& pattern, const std::string& name); bool matchesAny(const std::string& patterns, const std::string& name); std::vector<Found search(const Entry& root, const std::string& rootPath, const Options& options, const std::function<bool(int) & keepGoing); wildcardMatch ignores case; matches any run of characters (also none) and ? exactly one. One Windows rule: the pattern . matches every name, with or without a dot. matchesAny takes patterns separated by ; (spaces around them ignored); an empty pattern list matches everything. search walks the tree depth first: - In each directory, entries are visited in name order ignoring case (ties in plain order). Entries called . or .. are skipped entirely. - Each visited entry counts one towards the visit count . A file is found if it matches the patterns and its size is at least minSize ; a directory is found if includeDirs is set and its name matches the patterns. - After each visited entry (found or not), keepGoing(visitCount) is called; if it returns false, the search stops at once and returns what has been found so far. - Then, if the entry is a directory, the search goes into it if recurse is set, it is not a reparse point, and the depth limit allows: the root's entries are at depth 1, and with maxDepth = d , directories at depth d are not entered ( -1 means no limit). - Paths are rootPath + \ + the names on the way down, without doubling a \ that rootPath already ends with.

title: 6.01  Project: A Text Editor
body: Build a complete Notepad-style editor - an edit control or your own text view, files opened and saved in their original encoding and line endings, undo, find and replace, a status bar with line and column, recent files, word wrap and fonts. This lesson is the plan, the key code, and the order to build it in. What you build Xenon Notes - today.md ┌ File Edit Format View Help ─────────────────────────────┐ │ Plans │ │ - finish the editor │ │ - write the finder │ │ │ ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Ln 2, Col 8 100% Windows (CRLF) UTF-8 │ └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ The in the title means unsaved changes. Every piece comes from an earlier lesson: Piece Lessons --- --- Window, menu, accelerators, recent files 1.03, 2.04, project m02 The text view: an EDIT control, or your own with DirectWrite 2.05, 4.03 Open and Save dialogs with file types 3.02 Reading and writing files safely 5.01 Encodings and line endings 1.02, this lesson's practice Status bar 3.05 Find and Replace dialogs (modeless) 3.01 Settings: font, word wrap, window position 5.02 Drag a file onto the window to open it 5.05 High DPI 3.04 The text view: two options Option 1, the EDIT control. A multi-line EDIT ( ES_MULTILINE ES_AUTOVSCROLL WS_VSCROLL , plus ES_AUTOHSCROLL WS_HSCROLL when word wrap is off) gives you editing, selection, the caret, clipboard and a single undo level for free. Raise its text limit ( EM_SETLIMITTEXT ) above the default 30 000 characters. Word wrap is switched by re-creating the control with or without ES_AUTOHSCROLL , moving the text across. Line and column come from EM_LINEFROMCHAR and EM_LINEINDEX . This is how Notepad was built for decades. Option 2, your own view. A Direct2D window with DirectWrite layouts (lesson 4.03) and your own document model : multi-level undo, syntax colouring, very large files. The project at the end of this milestone writes that model: the text, edits, undo and redo with typing grouped into words, line and column, find and replace. Start with option 1; the model can replace it later without changing the rest of the program. Encodings and line endings A text editor must save a file the way it found it . Opening a file: 1. Read the bytes. 2. Detect the encoding: a BOM (byte order mark) EF BB BF means UTF-8, FF FE UTF-16 little-endian, FE FF UTF-16 big-endian. Without a BOM, check whether the bytes are valid UTF-8 (lesson 1.02's decoder without replacements); if not, assume the legacy code page ( CP_ACP ). 3. Convert to the internal form (UTF-16 for the EDIT control, or UTF-8 for your own model). 4. Detect the line endings: CRLF, LF or CR. If a file mixes them, use the most common one. Remember both, show them in the status bar, and use them when saving: a Unix file with LF endings stays LF, and a UTF-8 file without a BOM stays without one. The practice writes this detection and conversion. Dirty state and closing Track whether the document differs from what is on disk (an EN_CHANGE notification sets the flag; saving clears it), and show it in the title. Every path that discards the document goes through one function: cpp-norun bool confirmDiscard() // true if it is OK to continue { if (!m_dirty) return true; const int answer = MessageBoxW(m_hwnd, (L"Save changes to " + displayName() + L"?").c_str(), L"Xenon Notes", MB_YESNOCANCEL MB_ICONWARNING); if (answer == IDCANCEL) return false; if (answer == IDYES) return save(); // false if the save failed or was cancelled return true; } New, Open, opening a recent file, dropping a file, and WM_CLOSE all call it first. Windows also sends WM_QUERYENDSESSION when the user signs out: answer it the same way. Find and Replace Use modeless dialogs (lesson 3.01) so the user can keep editing. Search from the caret, wrapping around at the end, with "Match case"; Replace All should be one undo step. Keep the last search text so F3 (Find Next) works after the dialog is closed. Order to build in 1. Window, menu and an EDIT control that fills the client area, with the message font. 2. Open and Save As with file dialogs; reading and writing UTF-8. 3. Dirty flag, title, confirmDiscard everywhere. 4. Encoding and line-ending detection, kept when saving; status bar. 5. Find, Find Next, Replace, Go To Line. 6. Word wrap, font selection, zoom; settings saved. 7. Recent files, drag and drop, command-line file argument, high DPI. Check yourself quiz ? Why must an editor remember a file's encoding and line endings? - So it can show them in the title bar - Because the EDIT control cannot display text with LF endings + So it saves the file the way it found it instead of silently converting it - Because Windows refuses to save a file in a different encoding A Unix file with LF endings should stay LF, and UTF-8 without a BOM should stay without one. The editor keeps both, shows them in the status bar and uses them when saving. ? How does an editor detect that a file is UTF-16 little-endian? - By checking whether its bytes are valid UTF-8 + By its byte order mark FF FE at the start of the file - By its byte order mark EF BB BF at the start of the file - By the file's .txt extension FF FE marks UTF-16 little-endian and FE FF big-endian; EF BB BF is the UTF-8 BOM. Without a BOM the editor checks for valid UTF-8 and otherwise assumes the legacy code page. ? Why should every "discard the document" path go through one function such as confirmDiscard ? - Because MessageBoxW may only be called from one place in a program - So the program can save automatically without asking - Because WM_CLOSE is the only message that can discard a document + So no way of replacing or closing the document skips the unsaved question New, Open, a recent file, a dropped file, WM_CLOSE and WM_QUERYENDSESSION all replace or close the document. One function means none of them can lose changes without asking.
