title: Common Errors
body: Message or symptom Usual cause Fix Lesson --- --- --- --- Errors about min or max in standard headers windows.h defines min and max macros define NOMINMAX before including it 1.01 Text shows as ? or boxes The A functions with a legacy code page, or UTF-8 passed where UTF-16 is expected Call the W functions; convert at the boundary 1.02 The window cannot be moved, resized or closed Unhandled messages not passed to DefWindowProcW Return DefWindowProcW(...) for everything you do not handle 1.03 The program keeps running after the window closes No PostQuitMessage in WM_DESTROY Call PostQuitMessage(0) 1.03 One CPU core at 100 % WM_PAINT without BeginPaint / EndPaint , so the area never becomes valid Always pair them 1.05 Drawing stops after a while GDI objects leaked (deleted while selected, or never deleted) Select the old object back, then DeleteObject ; watch "GDI objects" in Task Manager 1.05 Mouse positions jump to about 65 000 LOWORD used for coordinates on multi-monitor setups GET_X_LPARAM / GET_Y_LPARAM 1.04 Typed text has the wrong letters on some keyboards Text built from WM_KEYDOWN Use WM_CHAR (and keep TranslateMessage in the loop) 2.01 Alt+F4 stops working WM_SYSKEYDOWN swallowed Pass system keys you do not use to DefWindowProcW 2.01 A drag gets stuck "pressed" Capture lost without a button-up Handle WM_CAPTURECHANGED 2.02 A countdown runs slow Counting WM_TIMER ticks Compute from the real clock 2.03 Ctrl+S does nothing although the menu shows it No accelerator table, or TranslateAcceleratorW missing from the loop Load the table and translate before dispatching 2.04 Controls look like Windows 95 No common controls v6 manifest entry Add the dependency (lesson 3.05) 3.05 Controls use a bold old font Controls not given a font WM_SETFONT with the message font 2.05 Tab does nothing No IsDialogMessageW in the loop Add it, and WS_TABSTOP on controls 2.05 The program is blurry on a laptop Not DPI aware Per-monitor v2 in the manifest; scale sizes 3.04 Everything is tiny at 150 % DPI aware but sizes not scaled MulDiv(value, dpi, 96) everywhere 3.04 Flicker when resizing Background erased before painting Return 1 from WM_ERASEBKGND ; double buffer; WS_CLIPCHILDREN 4.01 The window goes blank after a driver update Direct2D device loss ignored Re-create device resources on D2DERR_RECREATE_TARGET 4.02 Edges of transparent images have dark fringes Straight alpha filtered as premultiplied Convert to 32bppPBGRA 4.04 "The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process" (32) Share mode conflict Use suitable share modes; retry briefly 5.01 A recursive search never ends . , .. or links followed Skip them and reparse points 5.01 A registry string is cut in half Size passed in characters instead of bytes (length + 1) sizeof(wchar_t) 5.02 Access denied writing settings Writing to HKLM or Program Files Use HKCU and AppData 5.02 CreateProcessW crashes A string literal passed as the command line Pass a writable buffer 5.03 Arguments with spaces break Missing or wrong quoting Quote with the backslash rules 5.03 Reading a child's output hangs Our copy of the pipe's write end still open Close it after CreateProcessW 5.03 The window freezes ("Not responding") Long work or waiting on the UI thread Move it to a worker thread 5.04 Random crashes with threads Data shared without a lock, or a worker touching windows Lock shared data; post messages to the UI thread 5.04 A deadlock between two threads SendMessageW to a waiting thread, or locks taken in different orders PostMessageW ; one lock order 5.04 Pasted text has odd line breaks Line endings not normalised Convert \r\n , \r and \n 5.05 SmartScreen warns about the program The .exe is not signed Code-sign with a timestamp 6.02 Access violation in memory allocated with VirtualAlloc The pages were reserved but never committed Commit with MEM_COMMIT before use 7.01 VirtualFree fails with ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER MEM_RELEASE with a size other than 0, or not the reservation base Pass the base address and size 0 7.01 VirtualProtect fails No place for the old protection Pass a valid DWORD for the old value 7.01 Non-English text shows as ? or garbage in the console Bytes written in the wrong code page WriteConsoleW , or SetConsoleOutputCP(CP_UTF8) and UTF-8 7.02 Escape sequences print literally Virtual terminal processing is off SetConsoleMode with ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_PROCESSING 7.02 An overlapped read seems to fail with ERROR_IO_PENDING That code means started, not failed Wait for the completion 7.03 Memory corruption after CancelIoEx The buffer or OVERLAPPED was freed before the cancelled operation completed Free only after its completion arrives 7.03 The SCM says the service did not respond in time A long start without status reports Report SERVICE_START_PENDING with increasing checkpoints and wait hints 7.04 StartServiceCtrlDispatcherW fails with 1063 The program was started from a console, not by the SCM Start it with sc start , or add a console mode for debugging 7.04 AdjustTokenPrivileges succeeds but the privilege is not enabled The token does not have it Check GetLastError() == ERROR_NOT_ALL_ASSIGNED 7.05 CoCreateInstance fails with CO_E_NOTINITIALIZED COM was not initialised on this thread Call CoInitializeEx first 7.06 A COM object leaks or is destroyed too early Unbalanced AddRef and Release Use ComPtr 7.06

title: Glossary
body: Every term from the course, in alphabetical order. The lesson that introduces each one is in brackets. Term Meaning --- --- Accelerator table A table mapping key combinations to command ids, translated in the message loop. (2.04) Access token The description of who a process runs as: user SID, groups, privileges and integrity level. (7.05) Allocation granularity The 64 KB unit at which reservations of address space start. (7.01) Anchor Which edges of its parent a control keeps a fixed distance from when the parent is resized. (3.03) Apartment The COM threading model of a thread: single-threaded (STA) for UI threads or multithreaded (MTA). (7.06) BOM Byte order mark: bytes at the start of a text file that identify its encoding ( EF BB BF , FF FE , FE FF ). (6.01) Capture Directing all mouse messages to one window, even when the mouse is outside it. (2.02) Client area The inside of a window, without the frame, title bar and menu. (1.03) COM Windows' component object model: objects created by class id, used through interfaces, released when done. (3.02) Commit Back reserved pages with memory so they can be used. (7.01) Common controls List view, tree view, status bar and other controls from comctl32, drawn with visual styles in version 6. (3.05) Completion port A queue that receives a packet when each overlapped operation on its handles finishes. (7.03) Control handler The function a service registers to receive stop, pause and other controls. (7.04) Device context (HDC) A drawing surface with its current pen, brush, font and colours. (1.05) Device-dependent resource A Direct2D object on the GPU that must be re-created when the device is lost. (4.02) Dialog unit The layout unit of dialog templates, based on the dialog's font, so dialogs scale with text size. (3.01) DIP Device-independent pixel: 1/96 inch, Direct2D's unit when DPI is set. (4.02) Direct2D The GPU-accelerated 2D drawing API with antialiasing and transforms. (4.02) DirectWrite The text layout and rendering API used with Direct2D. (4.03) Double buffering Drawing a frame off-screen and copying it to the window in one step, to avoid flicker. (4.01) DPI awareness A program's declaration that it scales itself for the monitor's DPI instead of being stretched. (3.04) GDI The original Windows drawing API: device contexts, pens, brushes, fonts, bitmaps. (1.05) GetLastError Returns the thread's last error code, set by most failing API functions. (1.01) Guard page A page whose first access raises a one-time exception. (7.01) Handle An opaque value referring to a system object, closed with its type's own function. (1.01) HRESULT A 32-bit result code used by COM: negative means failure. (1.01) Integrity level The trust level in a token: low, medium, high or system. (7.05) Invalid region The part of a window that needs repainting; WM_PAINT is sent while it is not empty. (1.05) IUnknown The base COM interface: QueryInterface, AddRef and Release. (7.06) Known folder A standard folder such as AppData or Documents, located with SHGetKnownFolderPath. (5.01) Manifest XML embedded in an .exe that sets visual styles, DPI awareness, privileges and more. (6.02) Message A notification (input, painting, timers, commands) delivered to a window procedure. (1.03) Message loop The loop that takes messages from the thread's queue and dispatches them. (1.03) Modal / modeless A dialog that blocks its owner until closed, or one that stays open alongside it. (3.01) Notification A control's message to its parent about an event: WM_COMMAND codes or WM_NOTIFY structures. (2.05, 3.05) Overlapped I/O Reads and writes that start and return at once, and complete later. (7.03) Page The unit of memory protection and commit, 4 KB on x64. (7.01) Posted / sent message A message put in the queue and returned from at once, or delivered directly with the caller waiting. (1.04) Premultiplied alpha Pixels whose colour channels are already multiplied by their alpha. (4.04) Privilege A system-wide right in a token, such as shutting down the computer, enabled when needed. (7.05) Reference count The number of holders of a COM object; the object deletes itself at zero. (7.06) Registry Windows' hierarchical database of keys and typed values. (5.02) Reparse point A junction or symbolic link in the file system, which can point anywhere, including back up the tree. (5.01) Reserve Claim a range of address space without memory behind it. (7.01) Resource Data compiled into the .exe: menus, dialogs, icons, strings, version information. (2.04) Service A background program started and controlled by the service control manager. (7.04) Service control manager The Windows component that starts, stops and tracks services. (7.04) Share mode What other programs may do with a file while you have it open. (5.01) SID A security identifier for a user, group or computer, such as S-1-5-32-544. (7.05) Surrogate pair Two UTF-16 code units encoding one code point above U+FFFF. (1.02) Text layout A DirectWrite object holding one string laid out in a box, for drawing and hit-testing. (4.03) UAC User Account Control: administrators run with a filtered token until they elevate. (7.05) UI thread The thread that owns the windows and runs the message loop; it must never block. (5.04) UTF-16 The encoding Windows uses internally: 16-bit units, with surrogate pairs for rare characters. (1.02) Virtual list view A list view that stores no items and asks for the text of visible rows only. (3.05) Virtual terminal sequence An escape sequence (ESC ...) that sets colour or moves the cursor in a console. (7.02) Virtual-key code The number identifying a physical key in key messages, such as VK_LEFT or 'A'. (2.01) Visual styles The modern look of controls, enabled by the common controls version 6 manifest entry. (3.05) W and A functions The UTF-16 (wide) and legacy code page (ANSI) versions of text functions. (1.02) WIC The Windows Imaging Component, which decodes and encodes image files. (4.04) Window class A registered description of a kind of window, including its window procedure. (1.03) Window procedure The function that handles a window's messages. (1.03) Worker thread A thread that does slow work and posts results to the UI thread. (5.04)
